docs.title: Spanish Texts Statistics (esTS)
docs.text:
¿Cómo esTáS, texto?

esTS computes statistics of Spanish texts: basic statistics, readability, lexical diversity, lexical sophistication, style, phonostatistics, morphology, syntax and cohesion - by published formulas with the coefficients and the scales of their authors, and by the parts of speech, the features and the dependencies of Universal Dependencies.

The library works both with raw strings and with Doc objects of spaCy; most statistics need no trained model (Installation).

Try it without installing in the demo on Hugging Face Spaces: paste a text and get its readability, the metrics, the plots and the highlighting of its fragments.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Extraction

    Tokenizers of sentences, words and character N-grams that know the inverted marks, the dialogue dash and the abbreviations of Spanish

    Extraction

  • Syllables and stress

    Division of a word into syllables and its stress by the orthographic rules, with no dictionary

    Syllables and stress

  • Basic statistics

    Numbers of sentences, words, letters, syllables and punctuation marks by type and their distributions

    Basic statistics

  • Readability

    Fernández Huerta, Szigriszt-Pazos with the INFLESZ scale, Gutiérrez de Polini, Crawford, Legibilidad µ, SOL, LIX and RIX with a consensus grade, the school stages of Spain and reading time

    Readability metrics

  • Lexical diversity

    Type-Token Ratio and its variations, MATTR, MSTTR, Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity, HD-D, the indices of Simpson and Yule, entropy, the laws of Zipf and Heaps, over the whole text or over windows with confidence intervals

    Lexical diversity metrics

  • Morphology

    Parts of speech and fifteen grammatical features of Universal Dependencies with the markers of Spanish: the moods, the non-finite forms, the copulas ser and estar, the adverbs in -mente

    Morphological statistics

  • Syntax

    Statistics of the dependency tree (dependency distances, depth, clauses, coordination) with the constructions of the administrative style: the passive with ser and with se, the participial and the gerund clauses, the chains of de, the split predicates

    Syntactic statistics

  • Cohesion

    Overlap of nouns, arguments and content words between sentences in the manner of Coh-Metrix, givenness, temporal cohesion and the density of 250 Spanish discourse markers by class

    Cohesion statistics

  • Lexical sophistication

    How rare the words of a text are, in the manner of TAALES: frequency, range, dispersion and surprisal by a frequency dictionary of Google Books Ngram, the frequency bands top-1000 to 10000, lexical density

    Lexical sophistication statistics

  • Style

    SEO indicators of Advego and Text.ru (nausea, water content, spam score, naturalness by Zipf's law, keyword density) and the markers of the officialese by the Spanish-language guides to plain language: verbal nouns, compound prepositions, parenthetical expressions and clichés

    Style metrics

  • Phonetics

    Shares of the classes of sounds of a rule-based transcription, consonant clusters, hiatuses, open syllables, hardness and the indices of alliteration and assonance

    Phonostatistics

  • Verse

    Metrical syllables and the meter of a poem, the stress profile and the types of the endecasílabo, the rhyme in full and by assonance with its scheme, the strophes and the form of a poem

    Verse statistics

  • Corpus measures

    Keywords against a reference corpus or the frequency dictionary, collocations, the dispersion of a word over the parts of a text, a KWIC concordance, authorship by stylometry (Burrows's Delta, Zeta, the Mendenhall curve, the function words) and the comparison of corpora over 132 features of a text

    Corpus measures

  • Datasets

    A corpus of Spanish-language literature in the public domain (150 works by 33 authors in four genres), a collection of sonnets of the 15th-20th centuries with the metrical pattern and the rhyme of every line and a frequency dictionary of 83,785 lemmas by Google Books Ngram

    Datasets

  • Visualization

    Zipf's law, literature fingerprinting, word tree, corpus and stylometric plots, vocabulary growth and frequency spectrum, sentence lengths and the highlighting of a text by the fragments the statistics count

    Visualizers

  • Components

    Components of a spaCy pipeline, so that a text is annotated and measured in one pass and the statistics travel with the Doc

    spaCy components

  • Exceptions

    Errors of one hierarchy whose classes are also built-in Python exceptions

    Exceptions and logging

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

pip install pyests

The distribution on PyPI is pyests, the package it installs is ests. The dependencies, the spaCy model and the datasets are on the Installation page.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
CodeResult 
from ests import BasicStats, DiversityStats, ReadabilityStats

text = "Hay tres clases de mentiras: mentiras, malditas mentiras y estadísticas"

BasicStats(text).get_stats()
ReadabilityStats(text).flesch_reading_easy
DiversityStats(text).ttr

A walkthrough of one short story with every tool of the library is in the notebook examples/01_text_walkthrough.ipynb, which opens in Colab; the notebooks on prose authors, sonnets and corpus measures are on the examples page.

Project structure
  • demo - the demo on Hugging Face Spaces (Gradio)
  • docs - project documentation
  • ests:
    • basic_stats.py - basic text statistics
    • cohesion_stats.py - cohesion statistics
    • components.py - spaCy components
    • constants.py - constants of the Spanish language and of the metrics
    • diversity_stats.py - lexical diversity metrics
    • exceptions.py - library exceptions
    • extractors.py - extractors of sentences, words and character N-grams with the Spanish tokenizers
    • lexical_stats.py - lexical sophistication statistics
    • morph_stats.py - morphological statistics
    • phon_stats.py - phonostatistics
    • readability_stats.py - readability metrics
    • style_stats.py - style metrics
    • syllables.py - syllabification and stress
    • syntax_stats.py - syntactic statistics
    • utils.py - helper tools
    • verse_stats.py - verse statistics
    • corpus - corpus measures:
      • collocations.py - collocations and association measures
      • compare.py - comparison of corpora by the features of a text
      • dispersion.py - word dispersion over the parts of a text
      • keyness.py - keywords against a reference corpus or the frequency dictionary
      • kwic.py - KWIC concordance
      • stylometry.py - Burrows's Delta, Zeta, the function words and other stylometry measures
    • datasets - datasets:
      • freq_dict.py - the frequency dictionary by Google Books Ngram
      • spanish_literature.py - the corpus of Spanish-language literature
      • spanish_sonnets.py - the sonnets of the 15th-20th centuries
    • resources - embedded lexical resources (the discourse markers, the 10,000 most frequent lemmas)
    • visualizers - plots:
      • corpus.py - lexical dispersion, keyness chart, collocation network
      • fingerprinting.py - literature fingerprinting
      • highlight.py - text highlighting
      • sentences.py - sentence lengths
      • stylometry.py - dendrogram, principal components, scaling, Mendenhall curves
      • vocabulary.py - vocabulary growth and frequency spectrum
      • word_tree.py - word tree
      • zipf.py - Zipf's law
  • examples - notebooks with examples
  • scripts - scripts that build the archives of the datasets, fetch the anyTS pages of the documentation and check the outputs of the notebooks
  • tests - tests mirroring the package structure

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
StatsComponent(nlp, name)

The base of the components of spaCy that put the statistics of a text into an extension of Doc: a component registers the extension when added to a pipeline and puts the statistics of every document into doc._.<name>. Writing components in general is described in the documentation of spaCy.

The components of esTS are subclasses of the StatsComponent of the anyTS core, one for every class of statistics.

Note

The examples below use the model es_core_news_sm, which is installed apart: python -m spacy download es_core_news_sm (see installation).

CodeResult 
import ests
import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("es_core_news_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("ests_basic", name="basic")
doc = nlp("El gato duerme en la ventana. Los niños juegan en el parque.")
doc._.basic.n_words, doc._.basic.c_letters
nlp("?!")._.basic is None

(12, {2: 5, 3: 1, 4: 1, 5: 1, 6: 3, 7: 1})
True

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description nlp Language - Pipeline the component is added to name str - Name of the component in the pipeline and of the extension

spaCy sets both at nlp.add_pipe(factory, name=...); the other parameters of a component are passed in the config dictionary of the same call.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The factories carry the prefix of the library: ests_basic, ests_readability, ests_diversity, ests_morph, ests_syntax, ests_cohesion, ests_lexical, ests_style, ests_phon, ests_verse, and the component of sentence boundaries ests_blank_lines. They are declared as entry points of spacy_factories, so a pipeline saved with these components (nlp.to_disk(path), spacy package) loads with spacy.load(path) without importing the library.

The name of the pipe is the name of the extension: nlp.add_pipe(factory, name="basic") puts the statistics into doc._.basic. Without name both take the name of the factory. The extension follows the pipe when the pipeline renames it (nlp.rename_pipe). A name taken by an extension of another package raises ParameterError instead of replacing it: at add_pipe, or at the first document after rename_pipe, which renames the pipe before the component learns its name. A component taken from another pipeline (add_pipe(name, source=other)) is the same object in both, so under a new name it writes to that extension in the other pipeline too; a separate component comes from the factory, add_pipe(factory, name=...). The same component can be added twice under different names, with different parameters. A document with no words - an empty string, whitespace, punctuation alone - passes through a component untouched, its extension left at None.

In ests_lexical a document of numbers alone passes untouched as well, and in ests_verse a document without letters.

Serialization

A component keeps an object of statistics in doc._.<name>, and spaCy cannot serialize it: Doc.to_bytes(), DocBin(store_user_data=True) and nlp.pipe(..., n_process>1) fail with these components in the pipeline. To save a document, leave the user data out (doc.to_bytes(exclude=["user_data"])) or keep doc._.<name>.get_stats() separately; for multiprocessing compute the statistics in the main process after nlp.pipe, without the components.

Adding a component extends the tokenizer of its pipeline with the rules for the dashes of a dialogue glued to the words and for the abbreviations in every case (add_dash_rules), as in the string API: sí--dijo is two words and a dash, SR. one word. A tokenizer that is not the Tokenizer of spaCy is left as it is.

docs.title: Components of the classes of statistics
docs.text:
Component Factory Class of statistics Parameters BasicStatsComponent ests_basic BasicStats - ReadabilityStatsComponent ests_readability ReadabilityStats preset, basic DiversityStatsComponent ests_diversity DiversityStats window_len, mtld_threshold, mtld_min_len, hdd_sample_size, log_base MorphStatsComponent ests_morph MorphStats - SyntaxStatsComponent ests_syntax SyntaxStats - CohesionStatsComponent ests_cohesion CohesionStats - LexicalStatsComponent ests_lexical LexicalStats data_dir StyleStatsComponent ests_style StyleStats stopwords, top_n, nausea_stopwords, cliches PhonStatsComponent ests_phon PhonStats window_len VerseStatsComponent ests_verse VerseStats seseo

The basic, readability, diversity, phonetic and verse statistics need no annotation of a model. In the pipeline of es_core_news_sm the parts of speech come from the morphologizer (or a tagger with an attribute_ruler; a tagger alone does not give them), the parse from the parser and the lemmas from the lemmatizer. A component whose annotation is missing, excluded components included, raises SourceError when the document goes through it.

docs.title: Basic statistics
docs.text:
BasicStatsComponent(nlp, name)

BasicStatsComponent puts the basic statistics of a document into its extension.

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text:
ReadabilityStatsComponent(nlp, name, preset=None, basic=None)

ReadabilityStatsComponent puts the readability metrics into the extension, computed from the document or, with basic, from the basic statistics another component put into it. A library sets basic_factory, the factory of its component of the basic statistics, which the error names when that extension holds none.

Parameter Type Default Description preset str None Preset of the coefficients, one of the presets of the class; the default of the class if None basic str None Extension of a component of the basic statistics to reuse instead of computing them again

With preset left at None the config of a saved pipeline holds no preset, and the pipeline takes the default of the class when it is loaded; a library that wants its default written into the config gives it in the signature of its subclass.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a stats_class that is not concrete, a preset that is not a string or not one of the class, an extension not named by a string;
  • SourceTypeError - a class without basic_stats_class and no basic;
  • SourceError - a document whose extension basic holds no basic statistics of the class.

The presets of esTS are general and classic, the preset of the class general. In esTS the class of statistics and its basic_stats_class are set, so the errors of stats_class and SourceTypeError do not occur. The component named by basic comes before this one in the pipeline; the message of SourceError names the component ests_basic (basic_factory) to add there.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_readability", name="readability")
config = {"preset": "classic", "basic": "basic"}
nlp.add_pipe("ests_readability", name="readability_classic", config=config)
doc = nlp("El gato duerme en la ventana. Los niños juegan en el parque.")
round(doc._.readability.flesch_reading_easy, 2)
round(doc._.readability_classic.flesch_reading_easy, 2)

102.19
105.72

docs.title: Lexical diversity metrics
docs.text:
DiversityStatsComponent(nlp, name, window_len=50, mtld_threshold=0.72, mtld_min_len=10, hdd_sample_size=42, log_base=10)

DiversityStatsComponent puts the lexical diversity metrics into the extension, by a class of the library that reads a Doc. Its parameters are those of DiversityStats, with the same defaults.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a wrong parameter (check_params of the diversity).
Parameter Type Default Description window_len int 50 Window size for MATTR and segment size for MSTTR mtld_threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W mtld_min_len int 10 Minimum factor length for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W hdd_sample_size int 42 Sample size for HD-D log_base float 10 Logarithm base for the Summer, Maas and Dugast metrics CodeResult 
config = {"window_len": 100, "log_base": 2.718281828459045}
nlp.add_pipe("ests_diversity", name="diversity", config=config)
doc = nlp("El gato duerme en la ventana. Los niños juegan en el parque.")
round(doc._.diversity.ttr, 3), round(doc._.diversity.sttr, 3)

(0.833, 0.916)

docs.title: Morphological statistics
docs.text:
MorphStatsComponent(nlp, name)

MorphStatsComponent puts the morphological statistics into the extension. The pipeline needs a morphologizer and a lemmatizer before the component.

Raises:

  • SourceError - a document without the parts of speech or the lemmas.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_morph", name="morph")
doc = nlp("El gato duerme en la ventana. Los niños juegan en el parque.")
doc._.morph.pos[:4]

('DET', 'NOUN', 'VERB', 'ADP')

docs.title: Syntactic statistics
docs.text:
SyntaxStatsComponent(nlp, name)

SyntaxStatsComponent puts the syntactic statistics into the extension; they need a parser before it.

In esTS they need a lemmatizer before it as well.

Raises:

  • SourceError - a document without a dependency parse or the lemmas.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_syntax", name="syntax")
doc = nlp("El gato duerme en la ventana. Los niños juegan en el parque.")
doc._.syntax.tree_depth, doc._.syntax.mean_dependency_distance

(2.0, 1.6)

docs.title: Cohesion statistics
docs.text:
CohesionStatsComponent(nlp, name)

CohesionStatsComponent puts the cohesion statistics into the extension; by default they need the parts of speech and the lemmas before it.

In the pipeline of es_core_news_sm they come from the morphologizer and the lemmatizer.

Raises:

  • SourceError - a document without the parts of speech or the lemmas.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_cohesion", name="cohesion")
doc = nlp("El informe fue aprobado. Sin embargo, el informe no resuelve el problema.")
doc._.cohesion.noun_overlap_adjacent, round(doc._.cohesion.connectors, 2)

(1.0, 83.33)

docs.title: Lexical sophistication statistics
docs.text:
LexicalStatsComponent(nlp, name, data_dir=None)

LexicalStatsComponent puts the lexical sophistication statistics into the extension, with the frequency dictionary of its attribute freq_dict: None by default, for the dictionary of the class, and set by a library in the constructor of its component. A document gets the statistics when it has a word of iter_doc_words (with join_hyphens) other than a number of the method is_number, anyts.utils.is_number by default; a library gives the numbers its class leaves out, so a document of numbers alone passes untouched.

In esTS freq_dict is the frequency dictionary FreqDict of the directory data_dir, and is_number takes the numbers of the Spanish NUMBER_PATTERN (2020, 1.500,50, 3.º). The pipeline needs a morphologizer before the component; the lemmas of the model are not used. The frequency bands and the lexical density are computed without the dictionary, the statistics by the dictionary need it downloaded.

Parameter Type Default Description data_dir str None Directory of the frequency dictionary; the default one if not given

Raises:

  • SourceError - a document without the parts of speech;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the statistics by the dictionary and get_stats() when the dictionary is not downloaded;
  • ConfigValidationError of spaCy - a data_dir that is not a string, at add_pipe.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_lexical", name="lexical")
doc = nlp("El felinólogo examinaba al minino con parsimonia.")
round(doc._.lexical.coverage, 3), round(doc._.lexical.p_top1000, 3)
nlp("2020 1.500,50 3.º")._.lexical is None

(0.857, 0.429)
True

docs.title: Style metrics
docs.text:
StyleStatsComponent(nlp, name, stopwords=None, top_n=10, nausea_stopwords=None, cliches=None)

StyleStatsComponent puts the style metrics into the extension.

Parameter Type Default Description stopwords list[str] None Stopwords of the water content; those of the class if None top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words of the academic nausea and of the naturalness by Zipf's law (NAUSEA_TOP_N) nausea_stopwords list[str] None Words left out of the most frequent words of the academic nausea; those of the class if None cliches list[str] None Cliches; those of the class (cliches_list) if None

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - stopwords, nausea stopwords or cliches that are not a list of strings;
  • ParameterError - a top_n that is not an integer of at least one.

Without the lists the water content takes the stopwords of STOPWORDS and the one-word parenthetical expressions, the academic nausea leaves out the words of is_stopword, and the clichés come from OFFICIALESE_CLICHES; NAUSEA_TOP_N is a constant of anyts.constants. The verbal nouns need a morphologizer and a lemmatizer before the component, and without them reading verbal_nouns, markers() or get_stats() raises SourceError; the other metrics read the words alone.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_style", name="style")
doc = nlp("Se procedió a la revisión del expediente a la mayor brevedad.")
round(doc._.style.cliches, 2), round(doc._.style.verbal_nouns, 2)
nlp.add_pipe("ests_style", name="style_cliches", config={"cliches": ["se procedió a"]})
doc = nlp("Se procedió a la revisión del expediente a la mayor brevedad.")
round(doc._.style_cliches.cliches, 2)

(18.18, 33.33)
9.09

docs.title: Phonostatistics
docs.text:
PhonStatsComponent(nlp, name, window_len=3)

PhonStatsComponent puts the phonetic statistics into the extension; window_len (PHON_WINDOW_LEN by default) is the window in words of the alliteration and the assonance.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a window_len that is not an integer of at least 2.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_phon", name="phon", config={"window_len": 5})
doc = nlp("Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal")
round(doc._.phon.hardness, 3), round(doc._.phon.alliteration, 3)

(0.458, 0.975)

docs.title: Verse statistics
docs.text:
VerseStatsComponent(nlp, name, seseo=False)

VerseStatsComponent puts the verse statistics into the extension. The statistics read the line breaks and blank lines of the document, so pass the text of a poem to nlp with its lines not joined; the component needs no annotation of a model. A document with no letter passes untouched, and a text with letters but no Spanish syllables gives empty statistics.

Parameter Type Default Description seseo bool False Pronounce c and z before e and i as s in the rhyme

Raises:

  • ConfigValidationError of spaCy - a seseo that is not a boolean, at add_pipe.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ests_verse", name="verse")
doc = nlp(
    "Que por mayo era, por mayo,\ncuando hace la calor,\ncuando los trigos encañan\ny están los campos en flor,"
)
doc._.verse.meter, doc._.verse.c_clausulas

('octosílabo', {'aguda': 2, 'llana': 2})

docs.title: Sentences after blank lines
docs.text:
start_sents_after_blank_lines(doc)

A component that starts a sentence at the first token after a blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - so that a heading, a list item or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, as in the sentence extractor. It goes before the parser, senter or sentencizer, which keeps its starts and places the others. The whitespace before such a start stays with the sentence before it, and the marks that open a paragraph (a dash of a dialogue, ¡, «) stay with its first word. Alone, the component leaves the sentences within a paragraph unsplit and sets partial boundaries (has_sents), so the statistics take the sentences of such a document from its text. A parsed document, such as one passed through the pipeline again, passes untouched, since spaCy keeps its sentences. A language library registers the component under its prefix, Language.component("<prefix>_blank_lines", func=start_sents_after_blank_lines).

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object

In esTS the component is registered as ests_blank_lines. Without it the es_core_news_sm model glues a paragraph without a final mark to the next sentence, and the statistics of a Doc differ from those of the same string. The pipeline of ests.utils.get_nlp, which parses the strings of the morphological, syntactic, cohesion and lexical statistics, has it before the parser.

CodeResult 
nlp = spacy.load("es_core_news_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("ests_blank_lines", before="parser")
doc = nlp("Novedades\n\nImportación rápida. Menos errores")
[sent.text.strip() for sent in doc.sents]

['Novedades', 'Importación rápida.', 'Menos errores']

docs.title: Everything in one pipeline
docs.text:
The ten components can share one pipeline.

CodeResult 
import ests
import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("es_core_news_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("ests_blank_lines", before="parser")
factories = (
    "basic",
    "readability",
    "diversity",
    "morph",
    "syntax",
    "cohesion",
    "lexical",
    "style",
    "phon",
    "verse",
)
for factory in factories:
    nlp.add_pipe(f"ests_{factory}", name=factory)

doc = nlp("El gato duerme en la ventana. Los niños juegan en el parque.")
(
    doc._.basic.n_words,
    round(doc._.readability.flesch_reading_easy, 2),
    round(doc._.diversity.ttr, 3),
    doc._.morph.pos[:2],
    doc._.syntax.tree_depth,
    doc._.cohesion.p_given,
    round(doc._.lexical.p_top1000, 3),
    round(doc._.style.water, 2),
    round(doc._.phon.p_vowels, 3),
    doc._.verse.n_lines,
)

(12, 102.19, 0.833, ('DET', 'NOUN'), 2.0, 0.0, 0.667, 50.0, 0.457, 1)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Jupyter notebooks in the examples/ directory of the repository, with the library at work on its datasets. Each opens in Google Colab with a button and installs the library - esTS 0.7 or newer - and, if it needs it, the spaCy model; the outputs of all cells are stored in the files, so the notebooks can be read without running.

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
uv sync --group examples
uv run jupyter lab examples/

make notebooks runs every notebook again, writes the outputs into the files and strips the metadata of the run; a workflow runs them every week and fails when an output the prose quotes has moved.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All library exceptions inherit the base class EstsError and a built-in Python class, so they can be caught by either, and except ValueError keeps working.

Exception Built-in class When raised EstsError Exception Base class, never raised itself SourceTypeError TypeError The source is not a string or a Doc; the text of an extractor is not a string; a string, a Doc, an iterator or an object that is not iterable is passed where a list of words is expected, or the list holds something other than strings, such as spaCy tokens; the texts of a visualizer are not lists of words; the frequencies of zipf are not a Counter; the measure of fingerprinting or the tokenizer is not callable, or the tokenizer returns a non-iterable or something other than strings; a path is not a string or a Path; the stopwords or the clichés (style metrics, highlighting) are a string, not a list; a word of the syllables, of the transcription or of the stopwords is not a string; the keywords of keyness_plot, the collocations of collocation_network or the concordances of format_kwic are not a list; the features of compare_corpora or corpus_features are not a function SourceError ValueError The source has no words, sentences, texts or collocations, lacks the annotation a statistic needs (parts of speech, lemmas, dependency parse), is a string longer than the max_length of the pipeline (for the verbal nouns, has a sentence longer than it), or nothing is left after culling; Delta or the principal components get fewer than three texts; a matrix of distances is not square or has an infinite distance; the pipeline of function_words_profile does not tag parts of speech; no text of a comparison has a window of enough words; the keyword of wordtree is not found or has no word next to it ParameterError ValueError Not an integer: a length, window, step, number of items or other count, even a whole float. Out of range: a threshold, window, segment size, number of items, logarithm base, confidence level, number of bootstrap samples or bound of a frequency band (1-10,000); a negative limit of records or length bound of an extractor; parts of dispersion that do not add up to the words; an empty keyword of kwic. Unknown: a preset, scale, metric name, measure, variant, keyword field, genre or part of speech. Highlighting: an unknown layer or one the source does not allow (syntactic layers and verbal nouns on a string or on a Doc without the parse or the lemmas), layers that are neither a list nor a string, an alliteration threshold outside (0, 1], a number of words of a long sentence or of syllables of a complex word below 1. Plots: the axes are not a matplotlib Axes. A reading ease that is not a finite number (nan, an infinity) converted into a grade; parts of speech of find_connectors that are not as many as the words UnknownStatError ParameterError, KeyError An unknown statistic is requested by name, as in DiversityStats.windowed DatasetNotFoundError OSError The spaCy model is not installed or a dataset is not downloaded; the message gives the command that fixes it DataFileError ValueError The archive of a dataset is not ZIP or TAR, cannot be extracted, is empty or has paths outside its directory, or its target directory cannot be created; a line of a dataset file cannot be read DownloadError RuntimeError The file could not be downloaded or its directory created, or it failed the checksum twice

The classes are available from ests and from ests.exceptions. They are the classes of the anyTS core under the same names, EstsError being its anyts.exceptions.AnyTSError: aliases, not subclasses, so except EstsError catches the errors raised by the code of the core too, and a traceback shows anyts.exceptions.SourceTypeError.

Note

DatasetNotFoundError is the first error a new user usually meets: MorphStats("El gato duerme") without the model es_core_news_sm raises it with the download command. SpanishLiterature().get_texts() before download() and the statistics of LexicalStats by the frequency dictionary raise it too.

CodeResult 
from ests import EstsError, ParameterError, WordsExtractor

try:
    WordsExtractor(ngram_range=(2, 1))
except ParameterError as e:
    print(e)

try:
    WordsExtractor(tokenizer=42).extract("El gato duerme.")
except EstsError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)

The lower N-gram bound is greater than the upper
SourceTypeError

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
The library prints nothing on its own: the anyTS core sends messages about downloading and extracting datasets (the download() methods) to the anyts logger at the INFO level. The logger has a NullHandler by default, so the messages are silent; to see them, configure logging in your application:

CodeResult 
import logging

from ests.datasets import SpanishSonnets

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(name)s: %(message)s")
SpanishSonnets(data_dir="/tmp/ests_data").download()

anyts.datasets: Downloading the file https://github.com/SergeyShk/esTS/raw/master/ests/datasets/data/spanish_sonnets_v1.tar.xz
anyts.datasets: The file is downloaded: /tmp/ests_data/spanish_sonnets_v1.tar.xz
anyts.datasets: Extracting the archive /tmp/ests_data/spanish_sonnets_v1.tar.xz

The print_stats() methods of the statistics classes, MorphStats.print_markers() and print_kwic() write to standard output by design; logging does not affect them.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• python 3.11 or newer
  • spaCy 3.8.15 or newer
  • anyts 0.3.6 or newer within 0.3, the language-independent core: the extractors, the basic statistics and the common readability formulas, the lexical diversity metrics, the corpus measures, the plots and the machinery of the highlighting come from it with the tokenizer, the lemmatizer, the sentence splitter and the syllables of Spanish
  • numpy, scipy, pandas, simplemma 2
  • matplotlib and graphviz for the visualizers

The dependencies are installed with the package.

Graphviz

The graphviz package among the dependencies is only a wrapper: rendering the word tree and the network of collocations requires the executables of Graphviz, installed separately (brew install graphviz, apt install graphviz, conda install graphviz), otherwise render() and displaying the graph in Jupyter fail with ExecutableNotFound. Nothing else needs them.

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
The distribution on PyPI is pyests, the package it installs is ests:

pip install pyests

docs.title: From the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SergeyShk/esTS.git
cd esTS
uv sync --all-groups

docs.title: The spaCy model
docs.text:
Basic statistics, readability, lexical diversity, the style metrics except the verbal nouns, phonostatistics and verse statistics need no trained model. The morphological, the syntactic (with a parser), the cohesion and the lexical sophistication statistics of a string need one, and so do the verbal nouns of the style metrics, function_words_profile, the features of a text, the comparison of corpora and building a Doc yourself. The test suite needs it too; the test dependency group installs it:

python -m spacy download es_core_news_sm

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
The corpus of literature, the sonnets and the frequency dictionary are downloaded once by their download() method; the statistics of LexicalStats by the dictionary and keyness against it need FreqDict().download(). The archives go to the directory ests_data next to the installed package (ests.constants.DEFAULT_DATA_DIR), dicts for the dictionary and texts for the corpus and the sonnets. Where that directory cannot be written, pass another one in data_dir (FreqDict(data_dir="...")) or set the environment variable ESTS_DATA_DIR before the package is imported:

export ESTS_DATA_DIR=~/ests_data

docs.title: Syllables and stress
docs.text:
The ests.syllables module divides a Spanish word into syllables and finds its stressed syllable from the spelling alone, without a dictionary or a trained model. The basic statistics, the readability formulas, the phonostatistics and the verse statistics are built on these functions.

The rules follow the Ortografía de la lengua española (RAE, 2010): two weak vowels always form a diphthong (huir, je-sui-ta, guion), and tl is split as in Spain (at-las).

docs.title: Syllabification
docs.text:
syllabify(word)

Division of a word into syllables. A syllable is built around a vowel nucleus: a single vowel, a diphthong or a triphthong.

Rule Example a weak vowel (unaccented i, u, ü) next to another vowel forms a diphthong ai-re, puen-te, rui-do, ciu-dad two strong vowels form a hiatus, as do two close vowels of the same letter, with or without a tilde po-e-ta, le-er, a-é-re-o, chi-i-ta, chi-í-es an accented weak vowel is strong dí-a, pa-ís, ba-úl a weak vowel between two others gives a triphthong a-ve-ri-guáis, buey a weak vowel before a strong one goes with that vowel chi-hua-hua, ca-ca-hue-te an h between vowels does not break a diphthong ahu-ma-do, prohi-bir, de-sahu-cio the u of qu, and of gu before e and i, is silent; ü is a vowel que-so, gue-rra, pin-güi-no y is a vowel at the end of a word and a consonant before a vowel rey, U-ru-guay, ma-yo a single consonant or digraph goes to the next syllable ca-sa, mu-cho, pe-rro an obstruent with l or r goes to the next syllable ha-blar, o-tro other consonant pairs are split ac-to, is-la, at-las, rit-mo of three or more consonants the last two go to the next syllable when they form such a cluster, otherwise only the last one does com-pra, cons-truir, ins-ti-tu-to, obs-tá-cu-lo, tungs-te-no

The word is normalized to NFC and lower-cased. It is split into parts at digits, hyphens and other non-letters, each part is syllabified on its own (te-ó-ri-co-prác-ti-co), and a part without vowels (an abbreviation like sh) yields no syllables. Vowels with foreign diacritics count as accented strong vowels (Björk). A diaeresis marks a hiatus: the ü of verse outside gü and qü and the ï (sü-a-ve, glo-rï-o-sa), which leave the stress to the rules of the word, and the ë of French (Ci-tro-ën), which takes it; the Portuguese ão and õe are diphthongs (São, Ca-mões).

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.syllables import syllabify

syllabify("murciélago")
syllabify("averiguáis")

['mur', 'cié', 'la', 'go']
['a', 've', 'ri', 'guáis']

docs.title: Syllable count
docs.text:
count_syllables(word)

The number of syllables of a word by syllabify.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.syllables import count_syllables

count_syllables("Uruguay")

3

docs.title: Word stress
docs.text:
word_stress(word)

The index of the stressed syllable of a word, counted from zero as in syllabify.

Rule Example a written accent marks the stressed syllable ca-mión, ár-bol, mur-cié-la-go a word ending in a vowel, in n or s after a vowel, or in y after a consonant is stressed on the penultimate syllable ca-sa, jo-ven, lu-nes, whis-ky any other word is stressed on the last syllable pa-pel, re-loj, ro-bots, U-ru-guay a monosyllable is stressed on its only syllable rey, y

Forms with enclitic pronouns carry the accent by the same rules (dí-ga-me-lo). For an adverb in -mente and for a hyphenated compound the main stress is the last of word_stresses (fá-cil-men-te - 2).

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Returns None for a word without vowels.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.syllables import word_stress

word_stress("camión"), word_stress("casa"), word_stress("murciélago")

(1, 0, 1)

docs.title: All stresses
docs.text:
word_stresses(word)

All stressed syllables of a word in ascending order. A single index for most words. Two indices for an adverb in -mente, which keeps the stress of its adjective (fá-cil-men-te - 0 and 2, fe-liz-men-te - 1 and 2), and one index per part of a hyphenated compound (te-ó-ri-co-prác-ti-co - 1 and 4).

An adverb is recognized by its shape: a stem of at least one syllable before -mente that ends like an adjective (in a vowel, l, r, z, n or s) or carries an accent, so cruel-men-te counts too. Words of the same shape that are not adverbs are listed in NON_ADVERBS_MENTE of ests.constants: adjectives and nouns (demente, vehemente) and subjunctives of verbs in -mentar (fundamente, complemente); an unlisted subjunctive of that kind gets a second stress.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Returns an empty list for a word without vowels.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.syllables import word_stresses

word_stresses("fácilmente"), word_stresses("teórico-práctico"), word_stresses("demente")

([0, 2], [1, 4], [1])

docs.title: Stress type
docs.text:
stress_type(word)

The class of a word by the position of its main stress, that of word_stress, with the names of the endings of verse lines:

Type Stress Example aguda on the last syllable ca-mión llana on the penultimate syllable ca-sa esdrújula on the antepenultimate syllable mur-cié-la-go sobresdrújula earlier dí-ga-me-lo Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Returns None for a word without vowels.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.syllables import stress_type

tuple(stress_type(word) for word in ("camión", "casa", "murciélago", "dígamelo"))

('aguda', 'llana', 'esdrújula', 'sobresdrújula')

docs.title: Collocations
docs.text:
collocations(words, window=5, measure='logdice', min_freq=2, node=None, top_n=None)

Collocation extraction - pairs of words that occur together more often than independence would give: fixed expressions, terminology, the combinatorics of a word. The measures of association are those of Sketch Engine and of nltk.metrics.association.

Pairs are ordered, as in NLTK: the right word occurs at most window words after the left one, each pair of positions counted once; window=1 gives bigrams. The measures take the pair frequency divided by the window (Church and Hanks 1990, as in NLTK), which keeps the expected frequency independent of the window and Dice and the minimum sensitivity at most one; freq_pair stays undivided. So with window > 1 an always adjacent pair gets a logDice of \(14 - \log_2 window\) (13 at a window of 2), not 14 as in Sketch Engine with its raw co-occurrence; 14 needs a pair at every distance within the window. node keeps the pairs with the given word on either side.

Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor; lemmas suit fixed expressions, word forms suit grammatical constructions.

ests.corpus re-exports the function of the anyTS core. Words are extracted with WordsExtractor; for Spanish fixed expressions such as punto de vista or llevar a cabo take its lemmas (use_lexemes=True).

CodeResult 
from ests import WordsExtractor
from ests.corpus import collocations

words = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True).extract(
    "El gato estaba en la ventana y miraba a los pájaros. Los pájaros se fueron y el gato "
    "se durmió en la ventana. Mañana el gato volverá a estar en la ventana y mirará a los pájaros."
)

collocations(words, window=2, top_n=1)
[
    (c.left, c.right, round(c.score, 2))
    for c in collocations(words, window=1, node="gato", min_freq=1, measure="mi")[:2]
]

[Collocation(left='en', right='ventana', freq_left=3, freq_right=3, freq_pair=3, score=13.0)]
[('gato', 'volver', 3.62), ('gato', 'estar', 2.62)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order window int 5 Greatest distance between the words of a pair measure str 'logdice' Measure of anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES min_freq int 2 Minimum frequency of a pair node str None Word whose combinatorics is needed; None - every pair top_n int None Number of collocations; None - all of them

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. An unknown measure, a window or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, a min_freq that is not an integer and a node that is not a string raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Collocation(left, right, freq_left, freq_right, freq_pair, score)

A list of Collocation named tuples by descending measure and frequency of the pair (ties broken alphabetically); pd.DataFrame(found) gives a table.

Field Type Description left str Left word right str Right word, occurring within the window after the left one freq_left int Frequency of the left word freq_right int Frequency of the right word freq_pair int Frequency of the co-occurrence score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures of measure by key, with their names and descriptions in anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES:

Key Measures Range Higher means mi Frequency of the pair against the expected one, in bits Any number A stronger association mi3 MI with the frequency of the pair cubed Any number A stronger association t_score Difference of the observed and the expected frequency of the pair Any number A surer association dice Share of the pair in the occurrences of the two words 0-1 A stronger association logdice Dice coefficient on a logarithmic scale 14 and below A stronger association log_likelihood Significance of the association 0 and above, nan when a word fills the text or a cell is negative A more significant departure from independence, for attracted and avoided pairs alike npmi MI normalized by the information of the pair −1 to 1 A stronger association min_sensitivity Smaller share of the pair in the occurrences of either word 0-1 A stronger association

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.collocations of the frequencies of the words and of the pair and the number of words:

Parameter Type Default Description freq_a int - Frequency \(f_a\) of the first word freq_b int - Frequency \(f_b\) of the second word freq_ab float - Frequency \(f_{ab}\) of the pair n int - Number of words \(N\) of the text

A pair of zero frequency gives nan for MI, MI³, the t-score, logDice and NPMI.

The module ests.corpus.collocations re-exports the functions of the measures (from ests.corpus.collocations import calc_logdice).

docs.title: Mutual information
docs.text:
mi · Church and Hanks (1990)

calc_mi(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The pointwise mutual information of the two words; it overrates rare pairs.

\[ \log_2 \frac{f_{ab} N}{f_a f_b} \]

docs.title: MI³
docs.text:
mi3 · Oakes (1998)

calc_mi3(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The mutual information with the frequency of the pair cubed, which favours frequent pairs.

\[ \log_2 \frac{f_{ab}^3 N}{f_a f_b} \]

docs.title: t-score
docs.text:
t_score · Church et al. (1991)

calc_t_score(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The difference of the observed and the expected frequency of the pair over the root of the observed one; it favours frequent pairs.

\[ \frac{f_{ab} - f_a f_b / N}{\sqrt{f_{ab}}} \]

docs.title: Dice coefficient
docs.text:
dice

calc_dice(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The share of the pair in the occurrences of the two words; it does not depend on the size of the text.

\[ \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b} \]

docs.title: logDice
docs.text:
logdice · Rychlý (2008)

calc_logdice(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The Dice coefficient on a binary logarithmic scale, the default measure, as in Sketch Engine. It does not depend on the size of the text; below zero the link is weak.

\[ 14 + \log_2 \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b} \]

docs.title: Log-likelihood
docs.text:
log_likelihood · Dunning (1993)

calc_log_likelihood(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

\(G^2\) over the 2×2 contingency table of the two words: the observed frequencies \(O\) - \(f_{ab}\), \(f_a - f_{ab}\), \(f_b - f_{ab}\) and \(N - f_a - f_b + f_{ab}\) - against the expected ones \(E\) under independence. A word that fills the whole text, or a negative cell, as of a word paired with itself in a window above one, gives nan.

\[ G^2 = 2 \sum O \ln \frac{O}{E} \]

docs.title: NPMI
docs.text:
npmi · Bouma (2009)

calc_npmi(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The mutual information normalized by the information of the pair: one means the words occur only together. A pair as frequent as the text is long gives nan.

\[ \frac{MI}{-\log_2 (f_{ab} / N)} \]

docs.title: Minimum sensitivity
docs.text:
min_sensitivity · Pedersen (1998)

calc_min_sensitivity(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The smaller of the shares of the pair in the occurrences of each word.

\[ \min\left(\frac{f_{ab}}{f_a}, \frac{f_{ab}}{f_b}\right) \]

docs.title: Corpus comparison
docs.text:
compare_corpora(a, b, window=1000, features=None, labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0, min_words=None)

Compares two corpora of Spanish texts by every feature of a text at once: which statistics tell the corpora apart, and by how much. For single words keyness does the same, for the distances between texts - delta.

The texts are cut in a row into windows of exactly window words by split_windows, so the windows of all texts have one length; an incomplete remainder at the end of a text and a text shorter than a window are dropped unless min_words allows shorter windows. The features of every window are computed by text_features or a function of one's own, and the tables of the two corpora are compared by compare_features of the anyTS core.

Galdós against Unamuno, three novels each from the corpus of literature: Marianela, Misericordia and Torquemada en la hoguera against Niebla, Abel Sánchez and La tía Tula.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import compare_corpora
from ests.datasets import SpanishLiterature

sl = SpanishLiterature()
sl.download()
galdos = [
    record["text"]
    for record in sl.get_records(author="galdos")
    if record["title"] in ("Marianela", "Misericordia", "Torquemada en la hoguera")
]
unamuno = [
    record["text"]
    for record in sl.get_records(author="unamuno")
    if record["title"] in ("Niebla", "Abel Sánchez", "La tía Tula")
]

result = compare_corpora(galdos, unamuno, window=1000, labels=("Galdós", "Unamuno"))
columns = [
    "median_Galdós",
    "median_Unamuno",
    "ci_low",
    "ci_high",
    "cohen_d",
    "cliff_delta",
    "auc",
    "p_holm",
]
result[columns].head(5).round(3)

features = [
    "basic_letters_per_word",
    "readability_lix",
    "morph_p_gerund",
    "morph_polarity_Neg",
    "sents_mean",
    "punct_dash",
    "punct_exclamation",
    "diversity_yule_k",
]
result.loc[features, columns].round(3)

result.loc["sents_mean", ["n_Galdós", "n_Unamuno", "n_texts_Galdós", "n_texts_Unamuno"]].to_dict()

Galdós has the richer vocabulary: the measures built on the number of distinct words - TTR and its transformations, MATTR, MTLD, the hapaxes - tell the authors apart with a delta near or above 0.9, while Yule's K, which weighs the frequent words, gives a medium effect (0.35), so the difference lies mostly in the rare vocabulary. His words and sentences are longer, with nearly twice as many gerunds among the verb forms. Unamuno writes in dialogue: two and a half times as many dashes and exclamation marks per 1000 words, and more negations.

The p-values take the 272 windows of six novels for independent (see the warning below), and by the same test two novels of Galdós, Marianela and Misericordia, differ in 42 features. The interval of the difference of the medians resamples whole novels and is the safer guide: for the length of a sentence it spans 3.1 to 6.7 words, where the windows alone would give 3.9 to 6.0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description a list[str] - Texts of the first corpus b list[str] - Texts of the second corpus window int 1000 Size of a window in words; None - the whole texts features Callable None Function of the features of a text; None - text_features min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window, at most window; None - a whole window, or one word when window is None

labels, n_bootstrap and seed go on to compare_features. compare_corpora checks them with check_comparison_params first, so a wrong name of a corpus or seed fails before any text is parsed.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - texts that are not a list of strings, features that cannot be called;
  • SourceError - a corpus without a window of min_words words or more, a text with a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • ParameterError - a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above window, labels, a number of samples or a seed that check_comparison_params rejects;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the default features without the model installed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
text_features(text, nlp=None)

Returns 132 features of a text prefixed by their source; an undefined feature is nan.

Prefix Features Source basic_ shares of long, complex, simple, mono- and polysyllabic words, of letters, spaces and punctuation marks; letters and syllables per word BasicStats readability_ every readability formula and the consensus grade ReadabilityStats diversity_ every measure of lexical diversity DiversityStats morph_ shares of the values of every morphological feature (morph_pos_NOUN, morph_mood_Sub, morph_polarity_Neg) and the markers of Spanish (morph_p_gerund, morph_p_mente_adverbs) MorphStats by the spaCy model sents_ mean length of a sentence in words, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, autocorrelation of neighbouring lengths (sentence_rhythm) - the rhythm of the text SentsExtractor punct_ frequencies of the punctuation marks by type per 1000 words and the share of the inverted marks punctuation_profile

Left out are the reading time, which only follows the number of words in a window, and the features that repeat others: the share of unique words of BasicStats, which repeats diversity_ttr, its words per sentence, which repeat sents_mean, and the markers of the moods of get_markers, which repeat morph_mood_*.

The parts of speech and the features of a single value - polarity, polite, poss, reflex - are shares of all the words (morph_polarity_Neg is the share of the negations), the other features shares of the words that carry them (morph_mood_Sub is the subjunctive among the moods). A value that does not occur in a window gives 0, a feature absent from the window altogether (no verbs - no tense) gives nan. A value of several values (PronType=Int,Rel of que) is shared equally among its parts, so the shares of a feature still sum to one.

The morphology is parsed by the model es_core_news_sm without its parser, so the marker morph_p_ser, which reads the copulas from the dependencies, is left out; a pipeline passed in nlp runs whole but for the entity recognizer, so functools.partial(text_features, nlp=get_nlp()) brings the parser and morph_p_ser back, and another model goes into the comparison the same way. A novel is compared by windows and not whole, as the pipeline takes at most max_length characters.

The shares of spaces, letters and punctuation marks (basic_p_spaces, basic_p_letters, basic_p_punctuations) count the characters as they are: indents, double and non-breaking spaces of the files reflect the typesetting of an edition and not the text. In a corpus from different sources collapse them beforehand, for instance with re.sub(r"[^\S\n]+", " ", text).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string nlp Language None Pipeline for the morphology; None - the default model without its parser

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a text that is not a string, a pipeline that is not a spaCy Language;
  • SourceError - a text without words, with a character without a UTF-8 form or longer than the max_length of the pipeline;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the default model is not installed.
corpus_features(texts, window=1000, features=text_features, min_words=None)

Returns the matrix of the features of the windows indexed by (number of the text, number of the window), for classifiers of one's own as well; the level text of the index is what the bootstrap of compare_features resamples. Texts without words and windows shorter than min_words are skipped. compare_corpora is corpus_features for each corpus followed by compare_features, and the split lets the features of several corpora be computed once and compared in pairs.

Parameter Type Default Description texts list[str] - Texts of the corpus window int 1000 Size of a window in words; None - the whole texts features Callable text_features Function of the features of a text min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window, at most window; None - a whole window, or one word when window is None

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - texts that are not a list of strings, features that cannot be called;
  • SourceError - a corpus without a window of min_words words or more, a text with a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • ParameterError - a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above window;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the default features without the model installed.

Features of one's own, for instance the syntactic ones, are passed as a function:

CodeResult 
from ests import SyntaxStats
from ests.corpus import compare_corpora, text_features
from ests.utils import get_nlp

nlp = get_nlp()


def features(text):
    stats = SyntaxStats(nlp(text)).get_stats()
    return {**text_features(text), **{f"syntax_{key}": value for key, value in stats.items()}}


result = compare_corpora(
    galdos, unamuno, window=1000, features=features, labels=("Galdós", "Unamuno")
)
result.filter(like="syntax_", axis=0)[columns].head(5).round(3)

docs.title: Comparison of feature tables
docs.text:
compare_features(table_a, table_b, labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0)

Compares two corpora feature by feature. Each corpus is a table of the features of its windows, parts of the texts of about equal size, so the features do not depend on text length. The result has one row per column, by descending absolute Cliff's delta, the features without statistics last. The bootstrap resamples whole texts by the index level text; without it every row is a text of its own. A column missing from one table gives nan.

Parameter Type Default Description table_a DataFrame - Features of the windows of the first corpus, one row per window table_b DataFrame - Features of the windows of the second corpus labels tuple[str, str] ('A', 'B') Names of the corpora for the columns, two strings that give distinct columns n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples seed int / Generator 0 Seed of the random number generator, a non-negative integer, or a numpy Generator; None - a random one

A table that is not a DataFrame, repeats the name of a column or has a column that is not numeric raises SourceTypeError; the other parameters are checked by check_comparison_params.

check_comparison_params(labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0)

Checks the parameters of compare_features before the texts are processed: it raises ParameterError unless the labels are two strings that give distinct columns (("diff", "B") would repeat median_diff), the number of bootstrap samples is an integer of at least one and the seed is None, a non-negative integer or a numpy Generator.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
For a feature with the values \(x_1 \dots x_{n_A}\) in corpus A and \(y_1 \dots y_{n_B}\) in corpus B (undefined and infinite values dropped; with fewer than two values on a side - nan):

Column Description mean_A, mean_B, median_A, median_B means and medians median_diff, ci_low, ci_high the difference of the medians and its 95% percentile bootstrap interval: both sets are resampled n_bootstrap times (bootstrap_median_diff) cohen_d \(d = (\bar{x} - \bar{y}) / s\), \(s\) - the pooled standard deviation; 0.2 - a small effect, 0.5 - medium, 0.8 - large (calc_cohen_d) cliff_delta \(\delta = P(x > y) - P(x < y)\) from −1 to 1; \(\lvert\delta\rvert\) < 0.147 - a negligible effect, < 0.33 - small, < 0.474 - medium, large otherwise (Romano et al. 2006; calc_cliff_delta) auc the feature as a classifier: the share of the pairs of windows with the value in A greater than in B, ties counted as half; \(\delta = 2 \cdot AUC - 1\), 0.5 - the feature does not tell the corpora apart u, p_value the Mann-Whitney U statistic and the two-sided p-value (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu) p_holm the p-value with Holm's correction for the number of features (holm_correction) n_A, n_B number of windows with a defined value n_texts_A, n_texts_B number of texts behind those windows

The columns are anyts.corpus.COMPARISON_COLUMNS with the suffixes a and b replaced by the labels of the corpora. Cliff's delta and the AUC come from the same U statistic and agree; Cohen's d is sensitive to outliers and non-normality, so it is best read next to the delta.

Windows of one text are not independent

The test and the effect sizes take the windows for independent observations, which the windows of one text are not: with few texts the p-values are too small and reflect the chosen texts as much as the corpora. The bootstrap resamples whole texts (a cluster bootstrap), so its interval covers the spread between texts; it needs at least two texts on each side and is rough with few.

docs.title: Functions of the statistics
docs.text:
The statistics of a row are available one by one from ests.corpus:

calc_cohen_d(values_a, values_b)

Cohen's d with the pooled sample variances (ddof=1); nan with fewer than two values on a side or without spread.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus

A value that is not a number or a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

calc_cliff_delta(values_a, values_b)

Cliff's delta, the share of the pairs where the first value is greater minus the share where it is smaller; nan for an empty set or an undefined value. Computed by sorting, in \(O((n_A + n_B) \log n_B)\) time and linear memory.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus

A value that is not a number or a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

bootstrap_median_diff(values_a, values_b, n_bootstrap=1000, rng=None, confidence=0.95, texts_a=None, texts_b=None)

The percentile bootstrap interval of the difference of the medians. With texts_a and texts_b whole texts are resampled, the median of a draw taken over the values of its texts; with fewer than two texts on a side the interval is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples rng Generator None Random number generator of numpy; None - a new one without a seed confidence float 0.95 Confidence level texts_a list None Texts of the values in the first corpus; None - every value is resampled on its own texts_b list None Texts of the values in the second corpus

A value that is not a number or a missing one, values that are not a flat list and texts that are not labels of one type raise SourceTypeError; an n_bootstrap that is not an integer of at least one, a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1), texts not as many as the values and an rng that is not a numpy Generator raise ParameterError.

holm_correction(p_values)

Holm's correction for multiple comparisons: the p-values are sorted in ascending order, the i-th is multiplied by (m − i + 1), where m is the number of defined values, then the running maximum is taken and capped at one; nan stays nan.

Parameter Type Default Description p_values list[float] - p-values

A p-value that is not a number or a missing one and p-values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError, and a p-value outside [0, 1] ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import calc_cliff_delta, calc_cohen_d, holm_correction

round(calc_cohen_d([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7]), 3)
calc_cliff_delta([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7])
holm_correction([0.01, 0.04, 0.03]).round(3).tolist()

0.387
0.25
[0.03, 0.06, 0.06]

docs.title: Windows of a text
docs.text:
split_windows(text, window=1000, min_words=None)

Cuts a text into consecutive windows of exactly window words, so the features that depend on length are comparable between texts. The rest is a window only with at least min_words words (by default a whole window, so it is dropped). A boundary goes before the first word of a window and its opening marks; a straight quote or a dash glued to the last word of the previous window or after a closing mark stays with it ("cuatro", —dijo Juan—, "adiós."). Windows are stripped of whitespace; window=None gives the whole text. It is the split_windows of the core with the words of WordsExtractor and the marks of ests.constants: quotes, brackets, dashes, ¿ and ¡ open a phrase (OPENING_MARKS), the straight quote and the dashes are symmetric (SYMMETRIC_MARKS); the marks that close a phrase are those of the core.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string window int 1000 Size of a window in words; None - the whole text min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window; None - a whole window, or one word when window is None

A text without words or shorter than min_words gives an empty list.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a text that is not a string;
  • SourceError - a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • ParameterError - a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above the window.
CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import split_windows

split_windows("Uno dos tres cuatro cinco", 2, min_words=1)
split_windows("El gato duerme mucho. ¿Dónde está el perro?", 4)
split_windows('Dijo "adiós" y se fue ya', 2)

['Uno dos', 'tres cuatro', 'cinco']
['El gato duerme mucho.', '¿Dónde está el perro?']
['Dijo "adiós"', 'y se', 'fue ya']

docs.title: Rhythm of the sentences
docs.text:
sentence_rhythm(lengths, *, messages=MESSAGES)

Gives the rhythm of the sentences from their lengths in words: the mean sents_mean, the standard deviation sents_std, the coefficient of variation sents_cv and the lag-1 autocorrelation of neighbouring lengths sents_autocorr (Yule, 1939). The deviation needs two sentences, the autocorrelation three of unequal lengths, the coefficient of variation a mean above zero; otherwise, and without sentences, a feature is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description lengths list[int] - Lengths of the sentences in words messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

Lengths that are not a list of integers raise SourceTypeError, a negative length ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import sentence_rhythm

{key: round(value, 3) for key, value in sentence_rhythm([4, 8, 2, 7]).items()}

{'sents_mean': 5.25, 'sents_std': 2.754, 'sents_cv': 0.525, 'sents_autocorr': -0.794}

docs.title: Word dispersion
docs.text:
dispersion(words, parts=10, word=None, min_freq=1)

The dispersion of a word is how evenly it is spread over the parts of a text or of a corpus. Frequency does not tell a word occurring once in every chapter from one gathered in a single chapter; the measures of dispersion (Gries 2008, 2020) complement it.

parts is the number of parts of about equal size or the sizes of the parts in order (sentences, paragraphs, chapters, documents of a corpus), adding up to the number of words. Six measures are computed from the frequencies of every word by part; Gries recommends DP as the main one.

Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the word extractor.

ests.corpus re-exports the function of the anyTS core. Words are extracted with WordsExtractor.

CodeResult 
from ests import SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor
from ests.corpus import dispersion

text = (
    "El gato estaba en la ventana y miraba a los pájaros. Los pájaros se fueron y el gato "
    "se durmió en la ventana. Mañana el gato volverá a estar en la ventana y mirará a los pájaros."
)
we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True)
words = we.extract(text)
sizes = [len(we.extract(sent)) for sent in SentsExtractor().extract(text)]
sizes
dispersion(words, parts=sizes, word="gato")

# Three equal parts: a and pájaro are gathered at the edges of the text
[(d.word, round(d.dp, 2)) for d in dispersion(words, parts=3, min_freq=3)]

[11, 12, 14]
[Dispersion(word='gato', freq=3, dp=0.04504504504504503, dp_norm=0.06410256410256408, juilland_d=0.9307654905484509, carroll_d2=0.9955884389001025, rosengren_s=0.9974825285744621, kl_divergence=0.007241184435774255)]
[('el', 0.1), ('gato', 0.02), ('en', 0.02), ('ventana', 0.02), ('y', 0.02), ('a', 0.34), ('pájaro', 0.32)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order parts int / list[int] 10 Number of parts (from 2 to the number of words) or sizes of the parts word str None Word whose dispersion is needed; None - every word min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a word

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. A parts that is neither an integer from 2 to the number of words nor two or more positive integers adding up to it, a word that is not a string and a min_freq that is not an integer raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Dispersion(word, freq, dp, dp_norm, juilland_d, carroll_d2, rosengren_s, kl_divergence)

A list of Dispersion named tuples by descending frequency: the word, its frequency and the measures; pd.DataFrame(result) gives a table.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures, the fields of Dispersion, with their names in anyts.constants.DISPERSION_STATS_DESC:

Field Measures Range Higher means dp Deviation of the shares of the occurrences from the shares of the parts 0 to \(1 - \min s_i\) More uneven dp_norm DP over its greatest possible value 0-1 More uneven juilland_d Variation of the relative frequencies by part 0-1 More even carroll_d2 Entropy of the relative frequencies by part 0-1 More even rosengren_s Spread of the occurrences against the sizes of the parts \(\min s_i\) to 1 More even kl_divergence Divergence of the shares of the occurrences from the shares of the parts, in bits 0 to \(-\log_2 \min s_i\) More uneven

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.dispersion of the frequencies of the word by part and the sizes of the parts. For \(n\) parts of sizes \(n_i\) and shares \(s_i\) of the text, frequencies of the word by part \(v_i\) and a total frequency \(f = \sum v_i\), \(p_i = v_i / n_i\) is the relative frequency in a part:

Parameter Type Default Description frequencies list[int] - Frequencies of the word by part sizes list[int] - Sizes of the parts

For a word of zero frequency every measure is nan.

The module ests.corpus.dispersion re-exports the functions of the measures (from ests.corpus.dispersion import calc_dp).

docs.title: Deviation of proportions DP
docs.text:
dp · Gries (2008)

calc_dp(frequencies, sizes)

How far the shares of the occurrences of the word by part are from the shares of the parts: 0 means the word is spread in proportion to the sizes of the parts, \(1 - s_i\) that it is all in part \(i\).

\[ DP = \frac{1}{2} \sum \left\lvert \frac{v_i}{f} - s_i \right\rvert \]

docs.title: Normalized DP
docs.text:
dp_norm · Lijffijt and Gries (2012)

calc_dp_norm(frequencies, sizes)

DP divided by its greatest possible value, so the maximum is one whatever the split.

\[ \frac{DP}{1 - \min s_i} \]

docs.title: Juilland's D
docs.text:
juilland_d · Juilland and Chang-Rodríguez (1964)

calc_juilland_d(frequencies, sizes)

One less the coefficient of variation \(V\) of the relative frequencies \(p_i\) over its greatest value \(\sqrt{n - 1}\): 1 means even, 0 all in one part. The standard deviation \(\sigma\) is that of the population, as in Gries (2020); Gries (2008) takes the sample one.

\[ 1 - \frac{V}{\sqrt{n - 1}}, \quad V = \frac{\sigma(p)}{\mu(p)} \]

docs.title: Carroll's D2
docs.text:
carroll_d2 · Carroll (1970)

calc_carroll_d2(frequencies, sizes)

The entropy of the distribution of the relative frequencies \(p_i\) over the parts, divided by its greatest value: 1 means even, 0 all in one part.

\[ \frac{H(p)}{\log_2 n} \]

docs.title: Rosengren's S
docs.text:
rosengren_s · Rosengren (1971)

calc_rosengren_s(frequencies, sizes)

1 means the word is spread in proportion to the sizes of the parts; all in part \(i\), it gives \(s_i\), so \(1/n\) in one of \(n\) equal parts.

\[ \frac{(\sum \sqrt{s_i v_i})^2}{f} \]

docs.title: Kullback-Leibler divergence
docs.text:
kl_divergence · Gries (2020)

calc_kl_divergence(frequencies, sizes)

The divergence of the shares of the occurrences of the word by part from the shares of the parts: 0 means in proportion; it grows when the word is gathered in small parts.

\[ \sum \frac{v_i}{f} \log_2 \frac{v_i / f}{s_i} \]

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text:
keyness(target, reference, measure='log_likelihood', min_freq=1, positive=True, top_n=None)

Keyword extraction (keyness) for a target corpus against a reference one: the words that occur significantly more often in the target corpus than in the reference.

Every word gets two values that Gabrielatos and Marchi and Hardie recommend reading together: the log-likelihood \(G^2\) with its p-value (whether there is a difference) and Log Ratio (how large it is), plus the chosen measure score, which sorts the list. The measures of significance (\(G^2\), chi-square, BIC) and ELL, the effect size of \(G^2\), are negative when the word is more frequent in the reference; %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio are directional by construction.

The reference may be a list of words, a mapping of frequencies (its size is the sum of the counts) or a FrequencyReference. Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor, and both corpora have to be extracted the same way.

The function wraps keyness of the anyTS core and also takes the frequency dictionary FreqDict as the reference; FrequencyReference is in ests.corpus next to it. Words are extracted with WordsExtractor.

CodeResult 
from ests import WordsExtractor
from ests.corpus import keyness

we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True)
target = we.extract(
    "El gato estaba en la ventana y miraba a los pájaros. Los pájaros se fueron y el gato "
    "se durmió en la ventana. Mañana el gato volverá a estar en la ventana y mirará a los pájaros."
)
reference = we.extract(
    "El perro estaba en el suelo y dormía. Después el perro comió y volvió a dormir. "
    "Mañana el perro saldrá a pasear."
)

keyness(target, reference, top_n=1)
[(k.word, round(k.g2, 2)) for k in keyness(target, reference, positive=False, top_n=2)]

[Keyword(word='gato', freq_target=3, freq_reference=0.0, ipm_target=81081.08108108108, ipm_reference=0.0, g2=2.79971718756897, p_value=0.09428093556593176, log_ratio=1.8349407537295037, score=2.79971718756897)]
[('perro', -5.92), ('comer', -1.97)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description target list[str] / dict[str, int] - Words of the target corpus or their frequencies reference list[str] / dict[str, float] / FrequencyReference - Words of the reference corpus, their frequencies or a reference by frequencies measure str 'log_likelihood' Measure of anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES for score and the sorting min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a keyword in its own corpus positive bool True Positive keywords (more frequent in the target corpus) or negative ones (more frequent in the reference) top_n int None Number of keywords; None - all of them

The parameters and the target corpus are checked by check_keyness_params. A reference that is not a list of strings, a counter or a FrequencyReference raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency of a counter and an empty corpus raise SourceError.

reference may also be FreqDict, against which target is word forms. A frequency dictionary that is not downloaded raises DatasetNotFoundError. keyness checks its parameters and the target with check_keyness_params before it reads FreqDict, so a wrong argument fails before the dictionary is loaded.

check_keyness_params(measure='log_likelihood', min_freq=1, top_n=None, target=None)

Checks the parameters of keyness before a frequency dictionary is read: it raises ParameterError unless the measure is one of KEYNESS_MEASURES, the minimum frequency is an integer and the number of keywords is None or an integer of at least one. With target it also raises SourceTypeError unless the target corpus is a list of strings or a mapping of strings to whole frequencies, and SourceError for a negative, nan or infinite frequency.

docs.title: Reference by frequencies
docs.text:
FrequencyReference(counts, size, missing=0.0, key=None, keep=None)

A reference corpus described by its frequencies alone, such as a frequency dictionary built from a corpus too large to pass as words:

Field Type Default Description counts dict[str, float] - Frequencies of the keys in the reference corpus size float - Size of the reference corpus in words missing float 0.0 Frequency of a key missing from counts key Callable None Key of a word of the target corpus in counts, such as its lemma; None - the word itself keep Callable None Whether a word of the target corpus is counted; None - every word

Only the words of the target that keep passes are counted, under their key, in the frequencies and in the size alike. A key missing from counts has the frequency missing, such as the least frequency of a dictionary: an upper bound, so its word may be a positive keyword but never a negative one. Negative keywords come only from the keys of counts that keep passes. A frequency is checked as it is read, so a large dictionary is not gone through for positive keywords: one that is not a number raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite one SourceError. A size or a missing that is not a finite number or is negative raises ParameterError, and a key or a keep that cannot be called SourceTypeError.

The frequency dictionary FreqDict of Google Books Ngram passed as reference is turned into such a reference:

Field FreqDict counts the ipm of FreqDict.word_ipm, the proper nouns included, converted to occurrences in the corpus of the dictionary size CORPUS_SIZE, 63 billion words of the books of 1980-2019 missing the least frequency of the dictionary FreqDict.min_ipm, 0.1 ipm (about 6300 occurrences) key lemma_key: a keyword may carry the label of another lemma, Roma is counted under romo keep the forms made of the letters of WORD_PATTERN; numbers and words with a hyphen or a dot are left out

The target has to be counted the way the dictionary was: word forms with the stop words kept, not lemmas - lemma_key is not idempotent (estado - estar), so WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True) does not fit. The dictionary describes the register of the books, so the negative keywords of a text are the words of scholarly prose (de, social, país).

Against the dictionary the words of a play of Lope de Vega from the corpus of literature give its characters:

CodeResult 
from ests import WordsExtractor
from ests.corpus import keyness
from ests.datasets import FreqDict, SpanishLiterature

text = next(SpanishLiterature().get_texts(author="lope", genre="drama"))
words = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text)
for k in keyness(words, FreqDict(), top_n=5):
    print(k.word, k.freq_target, round(k.ipm_reference, 2), round(k.g2, 1), round(k.log_ratio, 2))
