docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Keyword(word, freq_target, freq_reference, ipm_target, ipm_reference, g2, p_value, log_ratio, score)

A list of Keyword named tuples by descending keyness (ties broken by descending frequency and alphabetically, words of an undefined measure last); pd.DataFrame(keywords) gives a table.

Field Type Description word str Word freq_target int Frequency in the target corpus freq_reference float Frequency in the reference corpus ipm_target float Frequency in the target corpus per million words ipm_reference float Frequency in the reference corpus per million words g2 float Signed \(G^2\) p_value float p-value of \(G^2\) log_ratio float Log Ratio score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures of measure by key, with their names and descriptions in anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES:

Key Measures Range Higher means log_likelihood Significance of the difference of the frequencies Any number A more significant excess in the target corpus chi2 Significance of the difference, with Yates's correction Any number A more significant excess in the target corpus diff Difference of the frequencies per million, in percent of the reference Above −100 A larger excess in the target corpus log_ratio Binary logarithm of the ratio of the frequencies per million Any number A larger excess in the target corpus bic Evidence of the difference: \(G^2\) penalized by the size of the corpora Any number Stronger evidence of an excess in the target corpus, for a word more frequent there ell Effect size of \(G^2\) −1 to 1 as a rule, nan for small expected frequencies A larger excess in the target corpus odds_ratio Ratio of the odds of the word in the corpora 0 to inf, nan if the word fills both corpora Higher odds in the target corpus

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.keyness of the frequencies of a word and the sizes of the corpora, \(N = c + d\):

Parameter Type Default Description a float - Frequency of the word in the target corpus b float - Frequency of the word in the reference corpus c float - Size of the target corpus d float - Size of the reference corpus

A zero frequency in one of the corpora is replaced with 0.5 for %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio (Hardie 2014).

The module ests.corpus.keyness re-exports the functions of the measures (from ests.corpus.keyness import calc_log_likelihood).

docs.title: Log-likelihood
docs.text:
log_likelihood · g2 · p_value · Rayson and Garside (2000)

calc_log_likelihood(a, b, c, d)

The log-likelihood of the frequencies of the word against the expected ones \(E_1\) and \(E_2\); a term of zero frequency is zero. The critical values are anyts.constants.G2_CRITICAL_VALUES: 3.84 for p < 0.05, 6.63 for p < 0.01, 10.83 for p < 0.001, 15.13 for p < 0.0001. The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ G^2 = 2 \left(a \ln \frac{a}{E_1} + b \ln \frac{b}{E_2}\right), \quad E_1 = \frac{c\,(a+b)}{N}, \quad E_2 = \frac{d\,(a+b)}{N} \] 
calc_p_value(g2)

The p-value of a \(G^2\) or a chi-square, whatever its sign, by the chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom; an array of values gives an array.

docs.title: Chi-square
docs.text:
chi2

calc_chi2(a, b, c, d)

The chi-square with Yates's correction over the 2×2 contingency table of the word and the other words of each corpus. When the correction exceeds the difference, the statistic is zero. The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ \chi^2 = \frac{N\,\max(\lvert a(d-b) - b(c-a) \rvert - N/2,\ 0)^2}{(a+b)(N-a-b)\,c\,d} \]

docs.title: %DIFF
docs.text:
diff · Gabrielatos and Marchi (2011)

calc_diff(a, b, c, d)

The difference of the frequencies \(NF\) per million words, in percent of the frequency in the reference.

\[ \frac{NF_a - NF_b}{NF_b} \cdot 100 \]

docs.title: Log Ratio
docs.text:
log_ratio · Hardie (2014)

calc_log_ratio(a, b, c, d)

The binary logarithm of the ratio of the frequencies \(NF\) per million words: one means the word is twice as frequent in the target corpus.

\[ \log_2 \frac{NF_a}{NF_b} \]

docs.title: BIC
docs.text:
bic · Wilson (2013)

calc_bic(a, b, c, d)

The Bayesian information criterion of \(G^2\). In absolute value above 2 it is positive evidence of a difference, above 6 strong, above 10 very strong; a value of the sign opposite to \(G^2\), when \(\lvert G^2 \rvert < \ln N\), means no evidence, not the opposite direction.

\[ \operatorname{sign}(G^2) \cdot (\lvert G^2 \rvert - \ln N) \]

docs.title: ELL
docs.text:
ell · Johnston, Berry and Mielke (2006)

calc_ell(a, b, c, d)

The effect size of \(G^2\): the share of the greatest possible departure from the expected frequencies \(E_1\) and \(E_2\). It grows without bound as the least expected frequency nears one and is nan when that frequency is at most one (a logarithm of zero or below). The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ \frac{G^2}{N \ln \min(E_1, E_2)} \]

docs.title: Odds ratio
docs.text:
odds_ratio

calc_odds_ratio(a, b, c, d)

The ratio of the odds of the word in the two corpora: one means equal odds. A word that fills the whole target corpus gives inf, the whole reference 0, both nan.

\[ \frac{a / (c - a)}{b / (d - b)} \]

docs.title: KWIC concordance
docs.text:
kwic(source, keyword, window=5, by_lemma=False, ignore_case=True)

A KWIC concordance (keyword in context) - every occurrence of a word or a phrase with its context on both sides. Occurrences are found among the words of the text by the word form, ignoring case or respecting it (ignore_case=False), or by the lemma (by_lemma=True); the keyword is lemmatized as a string, so with a lemmatizer a phrase may be written in any form and without one it is given by lemmas. The words of a string and of the keyword come from the tokenizer, those of a Doc from its tokens: a tokenizer that splits a string as the pipeline does finds the same in both. Punctuation and symbols are not words; forms are compared in the composed form of Unicode (NFC), without soft hyphens.

A phrase does not cross the end of a paragraph or a sentence unless the keyword has a final mark or a sentence start in the same place (U.S. Army). A sentence ends at a boundary of a Doc anywhere between the words, an opening mark included, or, without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents), at a sentence start of the sentence splitter, by default a final mark before whitespace. The context is window words on each side as written, punctuation included; whitespace collapses into one space, and occurrences do not overlap.

The function calls the kwic of the anyTS core with the hooks of Spanish. The text and the keyword are split into words the same way, by the tokenizer of the blank Spanish pipeline, so EE. UU. is one word in both; the abbreviations the tokenizer keeps whole (Sr., pág., etc., EE. UU.) are one word in lower case, capitalized and in upper case alike, so sr. pérez finds Sr. Pérez and SR. PÉREZ, and punctuation and symbols are words of neither: ¿Dónde finds Dónde, 20 € finds 20. The word forms and the lemmas are lower-cased; accents are part of the word form: solo and sólo are two forms. The sentences of a string, of the keyword and of the text of a Doc without boundaries are those of SentsExtractor: an ellipsis or an exclamation followed by a lower-case word does not end a sentence, so honrado piensa finds honrado... piensa.

By lemma, the keyword is lemmatized by simplemma, so a phrase is given by lemmas - mirar a el pájaro - or as it is written, and a word of the text is found by its lemma of simplemma and, in a Doc that carries lemmas, by the lemma of the model as well: gatos is found by gato. In Mi amigo vino con una botella de vino the model gives venir to the verb, so venir finds the verb, where simplemma, which sees no context, would find nothing; vino finds both, since simplemma reads the verb as vino.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import kwic, print_kwic

text = (
    "El gato estaba en la ventana y miraba a los pájaros. Los pájaros se fueron y el gato "
    "se durmió en la ventana. Mañana el gato volverá a estar en la ventana y mirará a los pájaros."
)
lines = kwic(text, "ventana", by_lemma=True, window=3)
lines[0]
print_kwic(lines, width=20)

[line.keyword for line in kwic(text, "mirar a los pájaros", by_lemma=True)]

Concordance(start=21, end=28, left='estaba en la', keyword='ventana', right='y miraba a')
        estaba en la  ventana  y miraba a
        durmió en la  ventana  . Mañana el gato
         estar en la  ventana  y mirará a
['miraba a los pájaros', 'mirará a los pájaros']

docs.title: Stylometry
docs.text:
Measures of stylometry and authorship attribution: distances between texts by the frequencies of the most frequent words (Burrows's Delta and its variants, as in stylo), markers of preferred and avoided words (Zeta), Kilgarriff's chi-square distance between corpora and the Mendenhall curve. The functions work on lists of units of a text: lower-case word forms (the usual choice for Delta), lemmas or character N-grams - case and lemmatization belong to the extractors.

The functions are those of the anyTS core, with the profile of the function words of Spanish added as a feature of an author. The units of a text come from WordsExtractor - word forms and lemmas - and CharNgramsExtractor.

docs.title: Burrows's Delta
docs.text:
frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=100, culling=0.0)

Builds the table of relative frequencies of a corpus, a dictionary "name of a text → units": rows are the texts, columns the n_mfw most frequent units by descending mean relative frequency (alphabetically when equal); culling keeps the units that occur in at least the given share of the texts, as in stylo.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError; an empty corpus, a text without units and no unit left after culling raise SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one and a culling that is not a number within [0, 1] ParameterError.

z_scores(table)

Standardizes the columns of a table of frequencies with the sample standard deviation, like scale() of R; a column with the same frequency in every text gives zeros.

Parameter Type Default Description table DataFrame - Table of relative frequencies 
delta(corpus, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0)

Computes a symmetric matrix of distances from the z-scores (a DataFrame with the names of the texts); at least three texts are needed - with two, the z-scores degenerate to ±1/√2 and the distances do not depend on the frequencies.

The variants (anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS), with the formulas of the sources of stylo; \(n\) is the number of units, \(z_A\) and \(z_B\) the vectors of z-scores of the texts:

Variant Key Formula Source Burrows's Delta burrows \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_i \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\) Burrows (2002), dist.delta Quadratic Delta quadratic \(\frac{1}{n} \sqrt{\sum_i (z_{A,i} - z_{B,i})^2}\) Argamon (2008), dist.argamon Eder's Delta eder \(\sum_i \frac{n - i + 2}{n} \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\), \(i\) - rank of the unit by frequency Eder, dist.eder Cosine Delta cosine \(1 - \frac{z_A \cdot z_B}{\lVert z_A \rVert \lVert z_B \rVert}\) Smith and Aldridge (2011), Evert et al. (2015), dist.wurzburg

Cosine Delta clusters the texts by author best in the experiments of Evert et al. The usual number of units is 100 to 500 most frequent words, 100-200 for character N-grams.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

delta_profiles(reference, samples, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0, statistics=None)

Distances by Delta for authorship attribution. The most frequent units, the culling and the statistics of the z-scores come from the reference texts (the profiles of the authors) or from a separate set statistics, such as training windows when the profiles are too few to estimate the spread of the frequencies; the texts under test samples get the same units and scaling. The result is the distances from the samples (rows) to the references (columns); the nearest reference is the presumed author. Unlike in delta, a sample affects neither the units nor the scaling, so its result does not depend on the other samples.

Parameter Type Default Description reference dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the reference texts by the names of the texts samples dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts under test by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in statistics dict[str, list[str]] None Texts of the units and of the statistics of the scaling; None - the reference texts

The corpora, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts for the statistics raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ests import WordsExtractor
from ests.corpus import delta, delta_profiles, frequency_table

texts = {
    "A": (
        "El gato estaba en la ventana y miraba los pájaros. "
        "Los pájaros se fueron y el gato durmió en la ventana."
    ),
    "B": "El perro estaba en el suelo y dormía. Después el perro comió y otra vez dormía en el suelo.",
    "C": "Mañana el gato volverá a la ventana y mirará los pájaros, pero el perro dormirá.",
}
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
corpus = {name: we.extract(text) for name, text in texts.items()}

frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
delta(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
delta(corpus, n_mfw=5, variant="cosine").round(3)

sample = {"?": we.extract("El gato despertó en la ventana y otra vez miraba los pájaros.")}
delta_profiles(corpus, sample, n_mfw=5).round(3)

docs.title: Zeta
docs.text:
zeta(target, comparison, segment_size=2000, top_n=None)

Markers of preferred and avoided words after Burrows (2007) and Craig and Kinney (2009). Every text of both corpora is split into segments of about segment_size words (the length over the size rounded half up, at least one segment); \(DP\) is the share of the segments of a corpus with the word. Zeta is \(DP_{target} - DP_{comparison}\), from −1 to 1 (zeta.craig in stylo; the classic Zeta of Craig, \(DP_{target} + (1 - DP_{comparison})\), is greater by one); the logarithmic Zeta is \(\log_2 \frac{DP_{target}}{DP_{comparison}}\) (Schöch et al. 2018), a zero share replaced by half a segment. The list goes from the words the target corpus prefers to those it avoids.

Parameter Type Default Description target list[str] / list[list[str]] - Words of the target corpus - one text or a list of texts comparison list[str] / list[list[str]] - Words of the comparison corpus segment_size int 2000 Size of a segment in words top_n int None Number of words from the start of the list; None - all of them

The result is a list of ZetaScore(word, dp_target, dp_comparison, zeta, log_zeta) named tuples by descending Zeta, by descending logarithmic Zeta and alphabetically when equal. A corpus that is neither a list of strings nor a list of such lists raises SourceTypeError, and a corpus without words SourceError; a segment_size or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import zeta

zeta(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], segment_size=5, top_n=2)
zeta(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], segment_size=5)[-1]

[ZetaScore(word='gato', dp_target=0.5, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.5, log_zeta=2.0), ZetaScore(word='la', dp_target=0.5, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.5, log_zeta=2.0)]
ZetaScore(word='suelo', dp_target=0.0, dp_comparison=0.5, zeta=-0.5, log_zeta=-2.0)

docs.title: Kilgarriff's chi-square
docs.text:
kilgarriff_chi2(words_a, words_b, n_mfw=500)

The distance between two corpora after Kilgarriff (2001): for the n_mfw most frequent words of the joint corpus the expected frequencies in the corpora are proportional to their sizes, \(\chi^2 = \sum (O - E)^2 / E\) over the words and both corpora. The greater the value, the more the corpora differ; it grows with the size of the corpora, so only pairs of equal sizes are comparable.

Parameter Type Default Description words_a list[str] - Words of the first corpus words_b list[str] - Words of the second corpus n_mfw int 500 Number of the most frequent words of the joint corpus

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a corpus without words SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import kilgarriff_chi2

round(kilgarriff_chi2(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], n_mfw=5), 3)

3.119

docs.title: Mendenhall curve
docs.text:
mendenhall_curve(words)

The shares of the words of every length in characters by ascending length (Mendenhall 1887), a profile of the author comparable between texts whatever their size.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError.

mendenhall_distance(words_a, words_b)

The Jensen-Shannon distance with base 2 between the Mendenhall curves of two texts, from 0 (the distributions coincide) to 1.

Parameter Type Default Description words_a list[str] - Words of the first text words_b list[str] - Words of the second text

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a text without words SourceError.

CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import mendenhall_curve, mendenhall_distance

{length: round(share, 3) for length, share in mendenhall_curve(corpus["A"]).items()}
round(mendenhall_distance(corpus["A"], corpus["B"]), 3)

docs.title: Function word profile
docs.text:
function_words_profile(source, nlp=None)

The shares of the adpositions, the coordinating and subordinating conjunctions, the particles, the pronouns, the determiners and the interjections (ests.constants.FUNCTION_UD_POS: ADP, CCONJ, SCONJ, PART, PRON, DET, INTJ) among the words of the text. Function words do not depend on the topic, so their profile is a classic feature of authorship since Mosteller and Wallace (1964).

The parts of speech are those of the annotation of a Doc that carries them. The words of a list or of a Doc without parts of speech are tagged by the model in their context, so they are to be passed in the order of the text; the punctuation of the list helps the tagging and is not counted. The pipeline is the model es_core_news_sm or the one passed in nlp, without the parser, the lemmatizer and the entity recognizer. In Spanish Universal Dependencies the negation no is an adverb and not a particle, so PART is rare.

Parameter Type Default Description source list[str] / Doc - Words of the text or Doc object nlp Language None Pipeline for a list of words; None - the default model

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings, a pipeline that is not a spaCy Language;
  • SourceError - a source without words, a pipeline that does not tag the parts of speech (spacy.blank("es")), a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the default model is not installed.
CodeResult 
from ests.corpus import function_words_profile

{pos: round(share, 3) for pos, share in function_words_profile(corpus["A"]).items()}

{'ADP': 0.095, 'CCONJ': 0.095, 'SCONJ': 0.0, 'PART': 0.0, 'PRON': 0.048, 'DET': 0.286, 'INTJ': 0.0}

docs.title: Frequency dictionary
docs.text:
FreqDict(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

A frequency dictionary of Spanish lemmas built from the Spanish books of Google Books Ngram (version 20200217): 83,785 lemmas (109,178 rows of a lemma and a part of speech) of the books of 1980-2019, 63 billion words. Every row has the frequency per million words (ipm), the range (the number of years out of 40 in which the lemma occurs), Juilland's D over the years (0-100) and the number of books with the most widespread form of the lemma. The parts of speech are those of Google, with the names of Universal Dependencies: NOUN, PROPN, VERB, ADJ, ADV, PRON, DET, ADP, CONJ (coordinating and subordinating together).

The dictionary is built by scripts/build_freq_dict.py from the 1-grams: only the forms tagged with a part of speech and made of letters are counted (numbers, punctuation and the tag X are dropped), and every form goes to its key by lemma_key. Google has no tag for proper nouns, so a noun form capitalized in at least 90% of its occurrences is PROPN and keeps its form. The decision is taken for the whole form: dios, capitalized in 92% of its occurrences, is PROPN in lower case too, while its NOUN row comes mostly from the plural dioses. The rows below 0.1 ipm or found in fewer than 5 years are left out. The dispersion is computed on the relative frequency of every year; the number of books is a lower bound, as a book with several forms of the lemma is counted once.

For a lookup the parts of speech of a lemma are merged: the frequencies are summed, the range, the dispersion and the number of books are the greatest ones. The dictionary is read once per process, so a FreqDict() for every text is cheap. It is the source of the frequencies of LexicalStats, and its 10,000 most frequent lemmas are the embedded list of the frequency bands. The dictionary size is CORPUS_SIZE, 63,090,618,290 words.

The archive (0.9 MB) is kept in the repository of the library and downloaded once into the data directory.

Licence and attribution

The dictionary is derived from Google Books Ngram, which is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported License, and is distributed under the same licence; the archive carries a README.txt with the source and the changes. Cite the source as: Michel J.-B. et al. Quantitative analysis of culture using millions of digitized books. Science 331 (6014), 2011.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a data_dir that is neither a string nor a Path.
CodeResult 
from ests.datasets import FreqDict

fd = FreqDict()
fd.download()
fd.info["license"]

'CC BY 3.0'

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description data_dir str / Path DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR Path to the dictionary directory; dicts in DEFAULT_DATA_DIR by default, the data directory is described in Installation

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description name str Name of the dataset, freq_dict meta dict[str, str] Reference information: the source, the description, the author, the licence and the citation info dict[str, str] The name and the reference information in one dictionary data_dir Path Absolute path to the dictionary directory filepath str Path to the file of the dictionary, None before the download entries dict[str, Entry] Entries by lemma, the parts of speech merged min_ipm float Minimum frequency in the dictionary (0.1) word_ipm dict[str, float] Frequencies by the key a word form reaches without a part of speech: the rows of the proper nouns go to lemma_key of their forms (roma to romo); the reference of keyness 
Entry(lemma, pos, ipm, range, dispersion, docs)

An entry of the dictionary: a named tuple.

Field Type Description lemma str Lemma in lower case pos tuple[str, ...] Parts of speech of the lemma ipm float Frequency per million words, summed over the parts of speech range int Number of years out of 40 (1980-2019) in which the lemma occurs dispersion int Juilland's D over the years, from 0 to 100 docs int Number of books with the most widespread form of the lemma

The dictionary iterates over its records as get_records() without filters: for record in fd goes over the 109,178 rows of a lemma and a part of speech, while len(fd) counts the 83,785 lemmas with their parts of speech merged, as lookup and in see them.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
download(force=False) downloads the archive, verifies its SHA-256 checksum and extracts the file. A corrupted archive is downloaded again, a missing file is extracted again; after the call the dictionary is read anew.

Parameter Type Default Description force bool False Download the dictionary even if it is already downloaded

An archive that cannot be downloaded or fails the checksum twice raises DownloadError, an archive that cannot be extracted DataFileError.

check_data() checks that the file of the dictionary is in place and returns True; a dictionary that is not downloaded raises DatasetNotFoundError with the commands to download it. The other methods and the attributes of the entries and frequencies check it themselves.

lookup(lemma) returns the entry of a lemma in any case, None for a lemma out of the dictionary; ipm(lemma) returns the frequency of a lemma per million words, 0 for a lemma out of the dictionary. The argument is a key of the dictionary, not a word form: a word form is looked up by its key, computadoras by lemma_key("computadoras") (computador), not by computadora; the lemma of usted in simplemma is tú, so fd.lookup("usted") is None. The same holds for in; LexicalStats and keyness go to the keys themselves.

Parameter Type Default Description lemma str - Lemma

A lemma that is not a string raises SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
from ests.datasets.freq_dict import lemma_key

fd.lookup("Gato")
fd.lookup("dios")

The register of the books

The dictionary describes the written language of books, a good part of them scholarly, and keeps what the books have: the abbreviations of the references are frequent words (pp, cit, vol), and so are the English words of the bibliographies (the, of) and the old spellings of the reprints (fué). The texts are recognized from scans and tagged automatically, so misreadings and tagging errors remain, mostly among the rare lemmas; the lemmatizer knows no context, so a form shared by two lemmas goes to one of them (como is only como, never comer), and a form it does not know stays as it is (darle, verlo).

docs.title: Key of a word
docs.text:
lemma_key(word, proper=False)

The key by which a word is looked up in the dictionary, and by which the dictionary is built (ests.datasets.freq_dict.lemma_key): the word goes to lower case, so that a word at the start of a sentence finds its lemma (Miró - mirar), and then to its lemma by lemmatize. A proper noun keeps its form in lower case (proper=True): París is parís, not the verb parir.

The lemmas depend on the version of simplemma: the dictionary is built with 2.0.0 (the constant SIMPLEMMA_VERSION), and a FreqDict warns once per process when another version is installed, as some words may then miss the dictionary.

Record fields: genre - genre, author - author, title - title, year_from and year_to - the years of the first publication, country - the country of the author in Spanish, text - text, file - path to the file. The records go by genre in the order of genres, within a genre by the folder of the author and by year.

CodeResult

    print(record["title"], record["year_from"], record["author"])

Los caciques 1920 Carlos Arniches
Es mi hombre 1921 Carlos Arniches
El marqués de Bradomín 1907 Ramón del Valle-Inclán
Romance de lobos 1908 Ramón del Valle-Inclán

The spelling follows the edition

The texts keep the spelling of the transcribed editions: 62 of them have the accents of their time (á as a preposition, fué, dió), 87 the modern ones (among them a dozen texts that the transcribers of Project Gutenberg modernized) and one, La vuelta de Martín Fierro, a mixture; Galdós has texts of both kinds. Since á and a are different words for a frequency list, stylometry over the most frequent words can separate the texts by their edition rather than by their author: remove the accent of the monosyllables (á, é, ó, ú, fué, dió, vió) before such a comparison. Abel Sánchez lacks most of the opening ¿ and ¡, as its edition does.

Editions and contents

Several works follow later editions revised by their authors (the Opera Omnia of Valle-Inclán, the complete works of Pereda, Palacio Valdés and Blasco Ibáñez, the much expanded sixth edition of Reglas y consejos sobre investigación científica), under the year of the first publication. Some records are selections or single volumes: Tradiciones peruanas (27 tradiciones), Recuerdos del tiempo viejo I (the first of three volumes), El payador (the only published volume); the Entremeses are the eight of 1615, without the three of doubtful attribution, and Novelas ejemplares go without La tía fingida. Two records hold two works each, as their titles say: Insolación y Morriña and Sonata de otoño. Sonata de invierno. In some plays of the Golden Age the square brackets of the editors remain around the stage directions and the names they added.

docs.title: Spanish sonnets
docs.text:
SpanishSonnets(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

A collection of Spanish sonnets from the Diachronic Spanish Sonnet Corpus (DISCO 5.0): 4,259 sonnets by 1,167 authors from Spain, Latin America and the Philippines, from the 15th century to the early 20th, 60,209 lines. Every line has its metrical pattern and the label of its rhyme, so the collection suits the study of meter and rhyme and the checking of a scansion against the annotation of the corpus.

The sonnets fall into four periods: 15th-17th (1,088 sonnets), 18th (321), 19th (2,845, an anthology of Spain and Latin America) and 20th (5, by the Filipino poet Cecilio Apóstol); 295 sonnets are by women, and the authors were born in 22 countries, most of them in Spain (2,388 sonnets) and Cuba (719).

Only the sonnets in the public domain are kept, 4,259 of 4,523: those by the authors who died before 1946, by the authors of the 15th-18th centuries whose death is unknown and by the authors of the 19th-century anthology born before 1866 or with no dates; most of the Filipino poets are left out. An author of the anthology with no dates is left out too when the dates of VIAF that DISCO matched with high confidence give a death in 1946 or later or a birth in 1866 or later with no death; VIAF only drops an author and never replaces the dates of the source. The metadata of DISCO is corrected by the biographical line of the source: the years of life where DISCO took a later year of it for the death or missed a birth or a death given alone (Echegaray died in 1916, not in 1904), the country of birth where the line names one (Gertrudis Gómez de Avellaneda was born in Cuba, not in Haiti). The Filipino poets have the name before the surname, as the rest; the speakers of the dialogues ([Car], [POETA]) and the calls of the footnotes are removed from the lines, as they are absent from their metrical patterns.

The archive (1 MB, a JSON Lines file) is kept in the repository of the library and downloaded once into the data directory; it is built by scripts/build_spanish_sonnets.py from DISCO at a fixed commit.

Licence and attribution

DISCO is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, and so is this dataset; the archive carries a README.txt with the source and the changes. Cite the source as: Ruiz Fabo P., Bermúdez Sabel H., Martínez Cantón C., Calvo Tello J. Diachronic Spanish Sonnet Corpus (DISCO), version 5.0. Madrid: UNED, 2017-2023; and the article: Ruiz Fabo P., Bermúdez Sabel H., Martínez Cantón C., González-Blanco E. The Diachronic Spanish Sonnet Corpus: TEI and linked open data encoding, data distribution, and metrical findings. Digital Scholarship in the Humanities 36 (Supplement 1), 2021, i68-i80, doi:10.1093/llc/fqaa035.

Parameter Type Default Description period str None Period: 15th-17th, 18th, 19th or 20th author str None Author: a substring of the name, regardless of case and accents country str None Country of birth: a substring of the name in Spanish, regardless of case and accents gender str None Gender of the author: F or M min_len int None Minimum text length (in characters) max_len int None Maximum text length (in characters) limit int None Number of texts

CodeResult

No encuentro paz, ni me permiten guerra;
de fuego devorado, sufro el frío;
abrazo un mundo, y quédome vacío;
me lanzo al cielo, y préndeme la tierra.

get_records with the same parameters extracts the records (with headers) from the dataset. Record fields: id - the identifier of the sonnet in DISCO, period - period, author - author, title - title, country - the country of birth of the author in Spanish (empty when unknown), gender - F or M, birth and death - the years of life (None when unknown), text - text, meter - the metrical pattern of every line, rhyme - the label of the rhyme of every line. In a metrical pattern + is a stressed syllable and - an unstressed one, so its length is the number of metrical syllables: 11 for an endecasílabo, 14 for an alejandrino. Equal labels of the rhyme mark the lines that rhyme together, - a line that rhymes with no other. The records go by period in the order of periods, within a period by the identifier of DISCO sorted numerically (1035e_269 before 1035e_1360), which keeps the sonnets of an author together in the order of their source.

CodeResult 
from collections import Counter

# The first lines of a sonnet with their rhyme and meter
record = next(ss.get_records(author="rubén darío"))
lines = record["text"].replace("\n\n", "\n").split("\n")
for line, pattern, label in list(zip(lines, record["meter"], record["rhyme"]))[:4]:
    print(f"{label} {pattern:<14} {line}")

# The share of endecasílabos and alejandrinos by period
for period in ss.periods:
    lengths = Counter(
        len(pattern) for record in ss.get_records(period=period) for pattern in record["meter"]
    )
    total = sum(lengths.values())
    print(period, f"{lengths[11] / total:.2f}", f"{lengths[14] / total:.2f}")

A -+---+---+-    En medio del abismo de la duda
B +----+-+-+-    lleno de oscuridad, de sombra vana
B +--+---+-+-    hay una estrella que reflejos mana
A -+-+---+-+-    sublime, sí, mas silenciosa, muda.
15th-17th 0.98 0.00
18th 0.99 0.00
19th 0.86 0.09
20th 0.60 0.40

The annotation is automatic

The metrical patterns and the labels of the rhyme are the automatic annotation of DISCO (the scansion by ADSO, by Jumper for the modernist and the Filipino sonnets, the rhyme by RhymeTagger): a reference to compare a scansion with, not a gold standard, as a pattern may miss a synalepha or a stress that a reader would make. Some sonnets have no labels of the rhyme, and the long sequences have none after the letter N: such a label is an empty string.

Sonnets, sequences and titles

4,211 records are sonnets of 14 lines; the rest are sonnets with an estrambote, a few incomplete or irregular ones (Darío's "El soneto de trece versos") and sequences of sonnets that DISCO keeps in one file, up to 98 lines. The sonnets of a sequence kept in separate files have the title Part of: and the title of the sequence. The titles and the spelling are those of the sources of DISCO, some titles in capitals.

docs.title: Character N-gram extraction
docs.text:
CharNgramsExtractor(n=2, lowercase=False, within_words=False, tokenizer=None)

A class for extracting character N-grams from a text - sequences of N characters taken with a sliding window over the string. Character N-grams are a standard feature of stylometry and authorship attribution (Stamatatos 2009) and can replace words in measures such as Burrows's Delta.

Whitespace runs are collapsed into a single space, punctuation marks are kept. With within_words=True N-grams do not cross word boundaries: the text is split into words by the tokenizer, punctuation is dropped, and words shorter than N yield no N-grams.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an n that is not an integer of at least one.

The class extends the CharNgramsExtractor of the anyTS core with the hook of Spanish: its default word tokenizer for within_words, the method tokenize(text), is the default tokenizer of WordsExtractor, the rule-based tokenizer of the spaCy Spanish language class ests.utils.tokenize. The list of N-grams is passed to delta as text units instead of words.

CodeResult 
from ests import CharNgramsExtractor

text = "El gato dormía  en la ventana, y el perro - en el suelo."

ce = CharNgramsExtractor(n=3, lowercase=True)
ce.extract(text)[:6]
CharNgramsExtractor().extract(text)[:8]
CharNgramsExtractor(n=4, lowercase=True, within_words=True).extract(text)

('el ', 'l g', ' ga', 'gat', 'ato', 'to ')
('El', 'l ', ' g', 'ga', 'at', 'to', 'o ', ' d')
('gato', 'dorm', 'ormí', 'rmía', 'vent', 'enta', 'ntan', 'tana', 'perr', 'erro', 'suel', 'uelo')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description n int 2 N-gram length in characters lowercase bool False Convert the text to lower case within_words bool False Take N-grams only inside words tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Word tokenizer for within_words or a regular expression; by default the tokenize method

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
extract(text) extracts N-grams from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string raises SourceTypeError, and so does, with within_words, a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings.

get_most_common(n=10) returns the top N-grams of the text as a list of (N-gram, frequency) pairs, the most frequent first.

Parameter Type Default Description n int 10 Number of top N-grams

A number that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Warning

The method must be called after N-grams have been extracted with extract.

CodeResult 
ce.get_most_common(2)

[('el ', 3), (' en', 2)]

docs.title: Sentence extraction
docs.text:
SentsExtractor(tokenizer=None, min_len=0, max_len=0)

A class for extracting sentences from a text.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound, a minimum above the maximum.

The class extends the SentsExtractor of the anyTS core with the hook of Spanish: its default tokenizer, the method sentenize(text), is the rule-based splitter ests.utils.sentenize.

Note

A sentence ends with a period, an exclamation or question mark or an ellipsis, optionally followed by closing quotes or brackets, when the next word starts with an upper-case letter, a digit, an inverted mark ¿ ¡, an opening quote or bracket or a dash, a dash glued to the mark included when a letter or an opening mark follows it on the same line (baja.--Tiene, as in the editions of Project Gutenberg), while a dash glued to the mark before whitespace closes its line of dialogue and stays with it (¡Traidores!--, viuda.-- El niño); a blank line ends a sentence too. A dash before a lower-case word opens a remark of the narrator and keeps the sentence going: ¿Vienes? —preguntó él. is one sentence, ¿Vienes? —Sí. two. Abbreviations (Sr., Dra., p. ej., EE. UU., a. m.), capital initials (J. L. Borges) and list markers at the start of a sentence or a line (1., 2.1., IV.) do not end a sentence, even before an upper-case word: Llegó a las 5 p. m. Luego se fue. stays one sentence. A lower-case word after an ellipsis or an exclamation mark continues the sentence, and a single line break does not split it, so hard-wrapped texts are handled.

CodeResult 
from ests import SentsExtractor

text = "¿No tienes cien euros? ¡Ten cien amigos! El Sr. García lo dijo... Y se fue."
SentsExtractor().extract(text)

('¿No tienes cien euros?', '¡Ten cien amigos!', 'El Sr. García lo dijo...', 'Y se fue.')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the sentenize method min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. A blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - ends a sentence of any tokenizer: the text is split at blank lines first and every part goes to the tokenizer, so a heading or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, and so is a part without words, such as a line of asterisks, which the statistics leave out. The sentences are stripped of whitespace at the edges before the length bounds, and empty ones are dropped.

Note

A spaCy pipeline can be passed as the tokenizer: tokenizer=lambda text: (sent.text for sent in nlp(text).sents).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
extract(text) extracts sentences from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string and a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings raise SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
import re

SentsExtractor().extract("Novedades\n\nImportación más rápida\nMenos errores\n\n¡Gracias!")
SentsExtractor(tokenizer=re.compile(r", ")).extract("No tengas 100 euros, ten 100 amigos")

('Novedades', 'Importación más rápida\nMenos errores', '¡Gracias!')
('No tengas 100 euros', 'ten 100 amigos')

docs.title: Word extraction
docs.text:
WordsExtractor(tokenizer=None, filter_punct=True, filter_nums=False, use_lexemes=False, stopwords=None, lowercase=False, ngram_range=(1, 1), min_len=0, max_len=0)

A class for extracting words from a text.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an ngram_range that is not a pair of integers or whose lower bound is below one or above the upper one, a length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound, a minimum above the maximum;
  • SourceTypeError - stop words that are not a collection of strings.

The class extends the WordsExtractor of the anyTS core with the hooks of Spanish:

Hook Spanish tokenize(text) the rule-based tokenizer of the spaCy Spanish language class, ests.utils.tokenize lemmatize(word) the lemmas of simplemma, ests.utils.lemmatize number_pattern signed numbers, ranges, fractions, dates, times, percentages and ordinals: -5, +7, 1990-1995, 1.500,50, 12/03/2020, 3:30, 10%, 3.º, 1.ª, 2do

Note

The tokenizer needs no trained model. Punctuation marks, including ¿ and ¡, numbers like 1.500,50, 3.º, 1990-1995 and abbreviations like Sr., EE. UU. are single tokens, and the abbreviations of ests.constants.TOKENIZER_ABBREVIATIONS in every case (sr., SR., ee. uu., Pág., a.m.); words with enclitic pronouns (dámelo) are not split. The dashes of a dialogue glued to the words are split off: --No, sí--dijo, ―dijo él―. give the words No, sí, dijo, él, also next to the underscores of italics (--_Siguro_), while a hyphen between letters (franco-alemán) or before a digit (-5) stays in its token; a suffix quoted with its hyphen (-mente) loses it as well, and so does the number of an item of a list (Artículo 1.- El objeto gives the number 1). A byte order mark at the start of a text, as in a file read with utf-8 instead of utf-8-sig, is split off and dropped. ests.utils.add_dash_rules(nlp) adds the same rules to the ones a spaCy pipeline of one's own has; the model of get_nlp has them already, and the components of the library add them to their pipeline.

Note

simplemma works from a dictionary without a trained model: a known form is mapped to its lower-case lemma (Tienes - tener, NIÑOS - niño), an unknown form is returned unchanged (Madrid, dámelo).

CodeResult 
from ests import WordsExtractor

text = "No tengas 100 euros, ten 100 amigos"

we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, stopwords=["no"], filter_nums=True, ngram_range=(1, 2))
we.extract(text)

('tener', 'euro', 'tener', 'amigo', 'tener_euro', 'euro_tener', 'tener_amigo')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the tokenize method filter_punct bool True Filter punctuation marks filter_nums bool False Filter numbers matched by number_pattern use_lexemes bool False Use word lemmas of the lemmatize method stopwords Collection[str] None Stop words, compared case-insensitively lowercase bool False Convert words to lower case ngram_range tuple[int, int] (1, 1) Lower and upper bound of the N-gram size min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. The filters are applied in order: punctuation, numbers, lemmatization, lower case, stop words, word length. A punctuation mark is a token of marks and symbols only, multi-character ones included: ?!, --, …, € (anyts.utils.is_punctuation). Empty and whitespace tokens are dropped before the filters. N-grams join the words with _.

Note

A ready stop word list is spacy.lang.es.stop_words.STOP_WORDS; note that it also holds frequent verbs like tener.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
extract(text) extracts words from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string and a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings raise SourceTypeError.

With the default tokenizer, a text with a character without a UTF-8 form, as a file read with the wrong encoding gives, raises SourceError, and so do the classes and functions that extract the words of a string with it.

get_most_common(n=10) returns the top words of the text as a list of (word, frequency) pairs, the most frequent first.

Parameter Type Default Description n int 10 Number of top words

A number that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Warning

The method must be called after words have been extracted with extract.

CodeResult 
we.get_most_common(3)

[('tener', 2), ('euro', 1), ('amigo', 1)]

docs.title: Basic statistics
docs.text:
BasicStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, normalize=False, complex_syl_factor=3, long_word_letter_factor=7)

The basic statistics of a text: the counts of its sentences, words, characters, syllables and punctuation marks and the distributions of its words. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. Letters are counted by str.isalpha, so digits, hyphens and marks inside a word are not letters.

The words and the sentences of a string come from the extractors. A Doc gives its tokens as words, without punctuation marks and symbols such as € or %, and its boundaries as sentences, or those of the sentence extractor when it has none or only partial ones (has_sents); an extractor given is used on its text instead. A blank line ends a sentence of a string and of a Doc without boundaries; a Doc with boundaries does so when its pipeline has start_sents_after_blank_lines (registered by a language library under its own name) before the parser, senter or sentencizer. A sentence without words, such as punctuation alone, is not counted.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a threshold that is not an integer of at least one.

The class extends the BasicStats of the anyTS core with the hooks of Spanish: the syllables of a word are counted by count_syllables, and the default extractors are the Spanish SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor. The ordinal indicators º and ª are letters (3.º is a one-letter word). The blank line component of esTS is called ests_blank_lines: nlp.add_pipe("ests_blank_lines", before="parser"). The statistics are computed when the object is created. A string with a character without a UTF-8 form, as a file read with the wrong encoding gives, raises SourceError from the Spanish tokenizer.

CodeResult 
from ests import BasicStats

text = "Hay tres clases de mentiras: mentiras, malditas mentiras y estadísticas"
bs = BasicStats(text, normalize=True)
bs.print_stats()

------------------------------
Sentences          |    1
Words              |    10
Unique words       |    8
Long words         |    5
Complex words      |    5
Simple words       |    5
Monosyllabic words |    4
Polysyllabic words |    6
Characters         |    71
Letters            |    60
Spaces             |    9
Syllables          |    23
Punctuation marks  |    2

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source (a string or a Doc object) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Sentence extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text normalize bool False Compute normalized statistics complex_syl_factor int COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR Minimum number of syllables in a complex word long_word_letter_factor int LONG_WORD_LETTER_FACTOR Minimum number of letters in a long word

The object keeps normalize, complex_syl_factor and long_word_letter_factor under their names.

In esTS the thresholds are those of the core and of the readability formulas: a complex word has three or more syllables, as in SMOG, and a long word seven or more letters, as in LIX and RIX (COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR = 3 and LONG_WORD_LETTER_FACTOR = 7 of anyts.constants).

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
Statistic Type Description Normalized c_letters dict[int, int] Distribution of words by number of letters - c_syllables dict[int, int] Distribution of words by number of syllables - n_sents int Number of sentences containing words - n_words int Number of words - n_unique_words int Number of unique words, case ignored p_unique_words n_long_words int Number of long words, of at least long_word_letter_factor letters p_long_words n_complex_words int Number of complex words, of at least complex_syl_factor syllables p_complex_words n_simple_words int Number of simple words: with a syllable, below the complex ones p_simple_words n_monosyllable_words int Number of monosyllabic words p_monosyllable_words n_polysyllable_words int Number of polysyllabic words, of two syllables or more p_polysyllable_words n_chars int Number of characters without the line breaks - n_letters int Number of letters p_letters n_spaces int Number of spaces of Unicode (category Zs), such as the no-break space, and tabs p_spaces n_syllables int Number of syllables - n_punctuations int Number of punctuation marks p_punctuations c_punctuations dict[str, int] Distribution of punctuation marks by type (count_punctuations) -

With normalize=True the object has the normalized statistics too, of the type float: the counts of the words divided by the number of words, those of the characters by the number of characters.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
count_words_by_syllables(min_syllables) and count_words_by_letters(min_letters) return the number of words with at least the given number of syllables or letters; a minimum that is not an integer raises ParameterError.

The methods recount complex and long words with a threshold other than the one set when the object was created; ReadabilityStats counts the polysyllabic words of SOL and the long words of LIX and RIX by them, so these do not depend on the thresholds of the object.

get_stats(flat) returns a dictionary with the distributions c_letters and c_syllables, the counts of stats_desc, the distribution c_punctuations and, with normalize=True, the normalized counts, as a copy: editing it does not change the object. With flat=True the distributions give a key for every value the text has, such as c_letters_3 and c_punctuations_comma.

print_stats() prints a table with the counts of stats_desc, their descriptions and the headers from stats_headers.

The normalized statistics p_* are not in the table.

to_dataframe() returns the flat statistics, get_stats(flat=True), as a one-row DataFrame of pandas with a column for every key. A dictionary statistic gives columns only for the keys the text has, so in frames of several texts joined with pandas.concat a count a text lacks is NaN. Only these columns may be filled with 0: elsewhere NaN is an undefined value.

docs.title: Punctuation marks
docs.text:
count_punctuations(text, marks=PUNCTUATION_MARKS, dash_pattern=DASH_PATTERN)

Counts punctuation marks by type, the distribution of c_punctuations: commas, periods, question and exclamation marks, ellipses, colons, semicolons, dashes, hyphens, guillemets, quotation marks, parentheses and other marks. Dashes typed with hyphens (dash_pattern) are counted first, then ellipses - …, three or more periods, or two after ? and !, one mark whose periods are not counted as periods (Who?.. is a question and an ellipsis) - then each mark by its type in marks; any other character of the Unicode categories P and S is another mark (§, €, °).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string marks dict[str, str] PUNCTUATION_MARKS Type of every mark, among PUNCTUATION_TYPES dash_pattern Pattern DASH_PATTERN Dashes typed with hyphens

A mark of marks that is not a single character or has an unknown type raises ParameterError; a text that is not a string, marks that are not a mapping and a dash_pattern that is not a compiled regular expression raise SourceTypeError.

esTS counts with the marks and the dash pattern of the core, PUNCTUATION_MARKS and DASH_PATTERN of anyts.basic_stats, which follow Spanish orthography: the inverted ¿ and ¡ are question and exclamation marks (¿Qué? carries two question marks), —, – and the horizontal bar ― are dashes, and so is the raya typed with hyphens - a run of two or more hyphens, a hyphen after whitespace, at the start of a line or after a closing mark, before a space or between a letter and an opening or a closing mark (--Hola --dijo Juan, - Se fueron - dijo, cuatro.-¿Cinco?); a hyphen inside a word, before a digit or at the end of a line inside a word is a hyphen (teórico-práctico, -5), «» are guillemets and "“”‘’ the quotation marks of the three levels of the orthography. The combining marks and the invisible format characters (Unicode M and Cf) are removed from the words but are not counted as marks.

CodeResult 
from ests.basic_stats import count_punctuations

text = "El gato — «fiera»... El perro, claro, - amigo; y alguien (el que vive) — ¡no!"
{kind: count for kind, count in count_punctuations(text).items() if count}

{'comma': 2,
 'exclamation': 2,
 'ellipsis': 1,
 'semicolon': 1,
 'dash': 3,
 'angle_quotes': 2,
 'parentheses': 2}

docs.title: Punctuation profile
docs.text:
punctuation_profile(text, n_words=None)

The frequencies of the punctuation marks by type (count_punctuations) per 1000 words and inverted_share - the share of the inverted marks among all question and exclamation marks: 0.5 when every question and exclamation opens with ¿ or ¡ as the orthography requires, lower when the writer drops them. Without words the frequencies are nan, and so is inverted_share without question and exclamation marks.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string n_words int None Number of words; without it the words are extracted by WordsExtractor

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a text that is not a string;
  • SourceError - without n_words, a text with a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • ParameterError - a number of words that is not a non-negative integer.

The profile depends on text formatting (typographic quotation marks and dashes, the inverted marks), so it is best read separately from linguistic features.

CodeResult 
from ests.basic_stats import punctuation_profile

profile = punctuation_profile(text)
round(profile["dash"], 1), profile["inverted_share"]

(230.8, 0.5)

docs.title: Cohesion statistics
docs.text:
CohesionStats(source, sents_extractor=None, connectors=None, nlp=None)

The cohesion statistics of a text in the manner of Coh-Metrix and of its Spanish adaptation Coh-Metrix-Esp: the overlap of the sentences, the givenness, the temporal cohesion and the connectors of a dictionary. The sentences are compared by lemmas. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy, and it has to be annotated: a string is parsed with es_core_news_sm or with the pipeline passed in nlp, without the named entities, and a Doc must carry the parts of speech, which come from a morphologizer (or a tagger with an attribute_ruler), and the lemmas, which come from a lemmatizer.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type, a pipeline in nlp that is not a spaCy Language, connectors that are not a dictionary of phrases and pairs of strings;
  • SourceError - a source without words; a Doc without the parts of speech or the lemmas (a Doc of spacy.blank("es")); a string longer than the max_length of the pipeline or with a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • ParameterError - an unknown class or kind of a connector;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - a string without nlp when the model is not installed.

The class extends the CohesionStats of the anyTS core with the Spanish layer. A Doc without sentence boundaries - from a pipeline without a parser - is split into sentences by the Spanish SentsExtractor. The features of the words come from the Universal Dependencies annotation, the temporal cohesion compares the tense and the mood of the verbs, and the connectors are found by SpanishConnectorMatcher over the dictionary of load_connectors. The print_stats table takes the descriptions of COHESION_STATS_DESC of ests.constants.

The max_length of the pipeline is a million characters by default: split a longer text into parts, or raise max_length on a pipeline of your own and pass it in nlp.

The words are classified by the Universal Dependencies annotation:

Notion Universal Dependencies Nouns NOUN, PROPN Pronouns PRON and the determiners that point at something: possessive (Poss=Yes), demonstrative or personal (PronType=Dem, Prs) - mi libro and este libro hold a pronoun, el libro and cada libro do not, and neither do the quantifiers and the indefinites (cada, todos, ningún, otro, cualquier) Arguments NOUN, PROPN, PRON, without the determiners that count as pronouns Content words CONTENT_UD_POS of anyts.constants (NOUN, PROPN, ADJ, VERB, ADV) without the demonstratives Demonstratives PronType=Dem Tense and mood features Tense and Mood CodeResult 
from ests import CohesionStats

text = (
    "El informe fue aprobado por la comisión. Sin embargo, el informe no resuelve "
    "el problema. Es decir, la comisión aplazó la decisión. Por lo tanto, el "
    "problema sigue abierto."
)
cs = CohesionStats(text)
cs.print_stats()

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute of the object, computed when it is created, and get_stats gives the metrics of the table; aspect_repetition, connectors_inter and connectors_intra are attributes outside it.

docs.title: Binary overlap
docs.text:
noun_overlap_adjacent · noun_overlap_all · argument_overlap_adjacent · argument_overlap_all · content_overlap_adjacent · content_overlap_all · Coh-Metrix

The binary overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFNO1, CRFAO1, CRFSO1 over the adjacent pairs, CRFNOa, CRFAOa, CRFSOa over all of them): the share of the pairs of sentences that share the lemma of at least one noun, argument or content word; nan for a text shorter than two sentences.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pairs sharing a lemma}}{\textrm{Number of pairs}} \]

docs.title: Proportional overlap
docs.text:
content_overlap_prop_adjacent · content_overlap_prop_all · Coh-Metrix

The proportional overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFCWO1, CRFCWOa): the Dice coefficient of the sets of the lemmas of the content words \(A\) and \(B\) of two sentences, averaged over the adjacent pairs or over all of them, 0 for two sentences without content words; nan for a text shorter than two sentences.

\[ \frac{1}{\textrm{Number of pairs}} \sum_{(A, B)} \frac{2 \times |A \cap B|}{|A| + |B|} \]

docs.title: Pronouns and demonstratives
docs.text:
p_pronouns · pronoun_noun_ratio · p_demonstratives

The pronouns, the nouns and the demonstratives are the words analyze marks so, with the features of word_info by default.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pronouns}}{\textrm{Number of words}}, \quad \frac{\textrm{Number of pronouns}}{\textrm{Number of nouns}}, \quad \frac{\textrm{Number of demonstratives}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

In esTS they are those of the table of the classes of words above, the features of token_info.

docs.title: Givenness
docs.text:
p_given

The share of the content words whose lemma was used before in the text, the current sentence included; the first occurrence of a lemma is new.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of given content words}}{\textrm{Number of content words}} \]

docs.title: Temporal cohesion
docs.text:
tense_repetition · mood_repetition · temporal_cohesion · Coh-Metrix

The repetition of the tense of Coh-Metrix (SMTEMP): every sentence gets the dominant value of the feature of its verbs - the most frequent one, the first of the equally frequent - and the metric is the share of the adjacent pairs of sentences with the same value; a pair where one of the sentences has no verb with the feature is skipped, and without a single such pair the value is nan.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pairs with the same dominant value}}{\textrm{Number of pairs with the feature}} \]

Spanish has no aspect in the Universal Dependencies annotation of the models, so esTS compares the mood next to the tense (temporal_features is ("tense", "mood")): temporal_cohesion is the mean of tense_repetition and mood_repetition. The attribute aspect_repetition of the core is nan without the feature Aspect.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
connectors · connectors_<class> · connectors_primary · connectors_secondary

The occurrences of the connectors found in every sentence by the matcher of connector_matcher_class, per 1000 words. An inter-sentential connector links a sentence to the ones before: it opens a sentence, unless the matcher takes it for a subordinator (is_subordinator), whose clause or phrase belongs to the same sentence; the others are intra-sentential. Every class and kind of the matcher gives a density: connectors_causal, connectors_adversative, connectors_concessive, connectors_temporal, connectors_additive, connectors_conditional, connectors_reformulative, connectors_primary and connectors_secondary by default.

\[ 1000 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of connectors}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

connectors_inter and connectors_intra are attributes outside get_stats.

load_connectors()

The connector dictionary of esTS: the file ests/resources/connectors.tsv, 250 discourse markers (marcadores del discurso) of Martín Zorraquino and Portolés (1999) and conjunctions of the NGLE, each with its class of CONNECTOR_CLASSES and its kind of CONNECTOR_KINDS of anyts.constants. The classes are the causal, adversative, temporal and additive connectives of Coh-Metrix with the concessive, conditional and reformulative ones added. The dictionary is read-only and shared by every caller, so a dictionary of your own goes through the connectors parameter.

Class Key Examples Causal causal porque, por lo tanto, así que Adversative adversative pero, sin embargo, en cambio Concessive concessive aunque, a pesar de, de todos modos Temporal temporal cuando, a continuación, por último Additive (ordinals included) additive y, además, por otra parte, en primer lugar Conditional conditional si, a menos que, de lo contrario Reformulative (operators of concretion included) reformulative es decir, en resumen, por ejemplo, en particular, sobre todo

The primary connectors (primary) are conjunctions, conjunctive locutions and adverbs (porque, aunque, además), the secondary ones (secondary) lexicalized phrases (sin embargo, por lo tanto, es decir). si also opens indirect questions and exclamations (no sé si vendrá, ¡pero si es él!) - about a quarter of its occurrences in the corpus of literature - and siempre que is temporal with the indicative and conditional with the subjunctive; both are counted in their class of the dictionary. The rules by which a word of the dictionary counts as a connector are those of the matcher.

CodeResult 
from ests.cohesion_stats import load_connectors

connectors = load_connectors()
len(connectors), connectors["por lo tanto"]

(250, ('causal', 'secondary'))

Warning

The words of a marker are counted as words like any other: the noun embargo of sin embargo is a noun and a content word of its sentence, so a text that repeats a marker gains a little overlap from it.

docs.title: Connector matcher
docs.text:
SpanishConnectorMatcher(connectors)

The search of the connectors (discourse markers: because, however, on the other hand) of a dictionary in the sentences of a text. The dictionary gives the class of every connector - causal, adversative, concessive, temporal, additive, conditional or reformulative (CONNECTOR_CLASSES) - and its kind, primary or secondary (CONNECTOR_KINDS). A connector is matched by the normalized forms of its words, the longest one at every position, without overlaps; a period or a hyphen inside a connector may be split off by the tokenizer (e.g. as e, g). An occurrence is a Connector: the number of the sentence sent, the positions start and end of its words, the connector text as the dictionary writes it, its class cls and kind kind.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a dictionary that is not a mapping of a phrase to a pair of strings;
  • ParameterError - an unknown class or kind.

SpanishConnectorMatcher is a subclass of the core ConnectorMatcher with the rules of Spanish; words and connectors are compared in lower case. A one-word connector takes a part of speech of CONNECTOR_POS - a conjunction, a particle, an adverb, an adposition, an interjection, a proper noun or X - or of CONNECTOR_POS_EXTRA for its form (pues and verbigracia as NOUN, resumiendo, recapitulando and concluyendo as VERB). It is no connector right after a determiner, so el antes y el después holds one connector, y, and not three; and as a proper noun it counts only at the start of a sentence, where the models read a marker so (Primeramente), so the surname in Habló con Juan Luego ayer is no connector. A marker that is part of another phrase is dropped: the words after it of CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_AFTER (antes de la reunión, en cuanto a), the words before it of CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_BEFORE (algo así como) and the parts of speech of the word after it of CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_AFTER_POS (sobre todo el texto) make it none, while antes, firmó el acta and sobre todo cuando llueve count their marker. A few markers depend on their place: pues opening a sentence opens a reply (Pues bien) and is no connector (CONNECTOR_NOT_AT_START), and encima counts inside a sentence only after y, e, ni or pero (y encima llueve, CONNECTOR_ONLY_AFTER). These lists are attributes of the matcher: CONNECTOR_POS is pos_tags, the others are named without CONNECTOR_ in lower case (CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_AFTER is blocked_after); not_after_pos is the determiner DET, start_only_pos the proper noun PROPN, and read_through_marks, split_by_marks and subordinators are empty in esTS.

find(words, sent_index, pos, breaks) returns the occurrences of the connectors in a sentence in the order of its words. The words are those of one sentence without punctuation, the first one its start. With the parts of speech, a one-word connector counts only with one of pos_tags or of pos_extra for its form, never after one of not_after_pos, and with one of start_only_pos only at the start of the sentence; a word without a part of speech (None) passes. Without the parts of speech the rules that read them are skipped. The positions of the punctuation marks breaks cut a connector off its neighbours: a rule does not read a word across a mark, so in so, the end the word after the comma neither blocks nor lets the connector count, unless the connector is one of read_through_marks, and a mark between the words of a connector of split_by_marks makes it none; without them the words are read as adjacent.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the sentence sent_index int 0 Number of the sentence, written into the occurrences pos list[str] None Parts of speech of the words breaks set[int] None Positions of the words a punctuation mark stands before

Words that are not a list of strings and parts of speech that are not a list of strings and None (the tags token.pos_ of spaCy, not the numbers token.pos) and positions of the marks that are not a collection raise SourceTypeError, a number of the sentence or a position of a mark that is not an integer and parts of speech not as many as the words ParameterError.

CohesionStats passes the positions of the punctuation marks of every sentence, so in sin gracia alguna, y el amor the comma cuts y off the determiner alguna and it counts, and encima after a comma counts too.

CodeResult 
from ests.cohesion_stats import SpanishConnectorMatcher, load_connectors

matcher = SpanishConnectorMatcher(load_connectors())
words = ["Vivía", "sin", "gracia", "alguna", "y", "el", "amor", "llegó"]
pos = ["VERB", "ADP", "NOUN", "DET", "CCONJ", "DET", "NOUN", "VERB"]
matcher.find(words, pos=pos)
matcher.find(words, pos=pos, breaks={4})

[]
[Connector(sent=0, start=4, end=5, text='y', cls='additive', kind='primary')]

is_subordinator(connector, pos=None) checks whether an occurrence of a connector ties its clause or phrase to its own sentence: a connector of subordinators, or a one-word connector whose part of speech pos is SCONJ or ADP. The clause of a subordinating conjunction and the phrase of a preposition belong to the sentence of the connector wherever it stands, so a subordinator opening a sentence (when he came, ..., despite the rain, ...) does not link it to the ones before.

With subordinators empty, a subordinator of esTS is a one-word connector tagged SCONJ or ADP (cuando, aunque), so ya que and a pesar de opening a sentence count as inter-sentential.

docs.text:
find_connectors(words, connectors=None, sent_index=0, pos=None)

Searches a sentence for connectors with the find method of SpanishConnectorMatcher over the dictionary connectors, that of load_connectors by default; the other parameters and the errors are those of the matcher and of find. It takes no positions of the punctuation marks, so the words are read as adjacent; a search that keeps the marks goes through find with breaks.

Parameter Type Default Description connectors dict[str, tuple[str, str]] None Class and kind by connector CodeResult 
from ests.cohesion_stats import find_connectors

find_connectors(["Sin", "embargo", "no", "vino"])
find_connectors(["El", "antes", "y", "el", "después"], pos=["DET", "NOUN", "CCONJ", "DET", "NOUN"])

docs.title: Lexical diversity metrics
docs.text:
DiversityStats(source, words_extractor=None, window_len=50, mtld_threshold=0.72, mtld_min_len=10, hdd_sample_size=42, log_base=10)

The main lexical diversity metrics of a text, computed from its words.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words, a string with a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • ParameterError - a parameter that check_params rejects.

The class extends the DiversityStats of the anyTS core: instead of a list of words it takes a text or a Doc object of the spaCy library. The words of a text are extracted by the Spanish WordsExtractor or by a given one, which for a Doc is applied to its text; without an extractor the words of a Doc come from its tokens. The words are always lower-cased, since every metric counts lexemes. The print_stats table has the English descriptions of the metrics of the core, anyts.constants.DIVERSITY_STATS_DESC.

from ests import DiversityStats

text = "Pies no tengo, ando; boca no tengo, hablo: cuándo dormir, cuándo levantarse, cuándo empezar labores"

Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; for a Doc it is applied to its text window_len int 50 Window size for MATTR and segment size for MSTTR (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN) mtld_threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD) mtld_min_len int 10 Minimum factor length for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_MIN_LEN) hdd_sample_size int 42 Sample size for HD-D (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE) log_base float 10 Logarithm base for the Summer, Maas and Dugast metrics (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

The object keeps the words in words, a tuple, and the five parameters under their names, changeable on the object. frequency_spectrum is the frequency spectrum of the words (calc_frequency_spectrum), and honore_r an alias of hapax_index.

check_params(window_len=50, mtld_threshold=0.72, mtld_min_len=10, hdd_sample_size=42, log_base=10, *, messages=MESSAGES)

Checks the parameters of the metrics: a window_len or an hdd_sample_size that is not an integer of at least one, an mtld_min_len that is not a non-negative integer, an mtld_threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) and a log_base that is not a finite number above 1 raise ParameterError. Called before the words are extracted, it reports a wrong parameter before an empty text.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Some metrics depend on conventions that differ between libraries. All of them except the comparison with the MTLD threshold are class parameters:

Parameter Default Other libraries Logarithm base for Summer, Maas, Dugast's U and Dugast's k 10 LexicalRichness, textcomplexity and zipfR - natural MATTR window and MSTTR segment 50 quanteda and koRpus - 100 TTR threshold for MTLD 0.72 0.66-0.75 in the literature Comparison with the MTLD threshold a factor closes at TTR ≤ 0.72 (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010) lexical-diversity and TAALED - strict <; the values differ when TTR hits the threshold exactly Minimum MTLD factor length 10 koRpus - only in MTLD-MA, dropping shorter factors instead of extending them; LexicalRichness and textcomplexity - not applied HD-D sample size 42 35-50 in the literature

According to Zenker and Kyle (2021), MATTR, MTLD and HD-D are stable on texts of 50-200 words and longer, MTLD-W, MA-MTLD and Maas are unstable on short texts, and the TTR family never stabilizes. Texts of different lengths are compared by the windowed computation with confidence intervals.

ttr

sttr

calc_sttr(text, base=10)

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Summer, 1966). The value depends on the logarithm base (see the conventions). It is nan for a text of one lexeme, where the numerator is undefined, and for a text no longer than the base (\(\log \log N \le 0\)), including such windows of calc_windowed.
