mattr

calc_mattr(text, window_len=50)

A moving-average modification of TTR (Covington & McFall, 2010), independent of text length: a window of fixed size slides over the text, and the TTR of every window is averaged. For texts shorter than the window the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words window_len int 50 Window size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A window_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio (MSTTR)
docs.text:
msttr

calc_msttr(text, segment_len=50)

A segmentation-based modification of TTR (Johnson, 1944), independent of text length: the text is split into segments of fixed size, and the TTR of every segment is averaged; an incomplete last segment is dropped. For texts shorter than the segment the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words segment_len int 50 Segment size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A segment_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD)
docs.text:
mtld

calc_mtld(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A modification of MSTTR (McCarthy, 2005), independent of text length: the number of words divided by the number of factors, the stretches on which TTR drops to the threshold (TTR <= threshold, see the conventions). An incomplete last factor counts in proportion to how close its TTR came to the threshold. The value is the mean of a forward and a backward pass (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010). The minimum factor length is non-standard (Kyle's lexical-diversity), and a min_len of 0 disables it. If no factor completes and TTR never drops below 1, the value is infinity.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MA-MTLD)
docs.text:
mamtld

calc_mamtld(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A moving-window modification of MTLD after MTLD-MA of koRpus: a factor starts at every position of the text, and the value is the mean length of the completed factors over a forward and a backward pass. koRpus makes the forward pass only, closes a factor at TTR strictly below the threshold and drops factors shorter than the minimum length instead of extending them. If no factor completes, the value is nan. The metric is unstable on short texts.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: MTLD with a moving window and text wrap (MTLD-W)
docs.text:
mtldw

calc_mtldw(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A modification of MA-MTLD after mtld_ma_wrap of lexical-diversity and TAALED: factors not completed by the end of the text continue from its beginning, so all positions get equal weight. A factor cannot be longer than the text. If no factor completes, because the text is shorter than min_len or TTR drops to the threshold from no start, the value is nan. The metric is unstable on texts shorter than 100 words.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D)
docs.text:
hdd

calc_hdd(text, sample_size=42)

An alternative to vocd-D (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010): the exact expected TTR of a random sample of sample_size words, without drawing samples. The hypergeometric distribution gives the probability that the sample holds each lexeme at least once; HD-D is the sum of these probabilities divided by the sample size. For texts shorter than 50 words or than the sample size the metric is undefined, and the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words sample_size int 42 Sample size in words (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE)

A sample_size that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Simpson's index (D)
docs.text:
simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_simpson_index(text)

The probability that two words drawn from the text at random without replacement are the same lexeme; \(n\) is the number of occurrences of a lexeme in the text. For texts shorter than two words the index is undefined, and the value is nan; the same holds for the inverse Simpson's index and the Gini-Simpson index.

\[ \frac{\sum n\times(n-1)}{\textrm{(Number of words)}\times(\textrm{Number of words}-1)} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Simpson's index (1/D)
docs.text:
inverse_simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_inverse_simpson_index(text)

An estimate of the Hill number of order two (\(1/\sum_k p_k^2\)) from pairs drawn without replacement. If all words of the text are unique, Simpson's index is 0 and the inverse index is infinity.

\[ \frac{1}{D} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Gini-Simpson index (1-D)
docs.text:
gini_simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_gini_simpson_index(text)

The probability that two randomly chosen words of the text are different.

\[ 1-D \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hapax index (Honoré's R)
docs.text:
hapax_index · honore_r · Wikipedia

calc_hapax_index(text)

A hapax (Greek ἅπαξ λεγόμενον - "said only once") is a word that occurs only once in a corpus: baciyelmo, Sancho Panza's word for the barber's basin that Don Quixote takes for a helmet, is a hapax of Cervantes (chapter 44 of the first part of Don Quixote). The index coincides with Honoré's measure (1979), with the natural logarithm. If all words of the text are hapaxes, the index is infinity; for texts shorter than two words it is undefined, and the value is nan. calc_honore_r is the same function.

\[ 100\times\frac{\ln {\textrm{(Number of words)}}}{1-\frac{\textrm{Number of hapaxes}}{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
frequency_spectrum

calc_frequency_spectrum(text)

The number of lexemes \(V_i\) occurring exactly \(i\) times in the text, as a dictionary by the frequency \(i\) in ascending order. The hapax index, Yule's K and I, Herdan's Vm, Sichel's S, Michéa's M, Baayen's P, the hapax ratio and the α₂ exponent are computed from it, with the formulas of Tweedie and Baayen (1998).

Notation: \(N\) - number of words, \(V\) - number of lexemes, \(V_i\) - number of lexemes with frequency \(i\), \(V_1\) - hapaxes, \(V_2\) - dis legomena, \(p_k\) - relative frequency of a lexeme.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Yule's characteristic (Yule's K)
docs.text:
yule_k

calc_yule_k(text)

Yule's characteristic (Yule, 1944), one of the few measures theoretically independent of text length (Tweedie & Baayen, 1998); in practice it converges as the text grows. It is proportional to Simpson's index: \(K \approx 10^4 \cdot D\). For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

\[ K = 10^4\times\frac{\sum_i i^2 V_i - N}{N^2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Yule's characteristic (Yule's I)
docs.text:
yule_i

calc_yule_i(text)

The inverse Yule's characteristic. If all words of the text are unique, the value is infinity; for texts shorter than two words it is nan.

\[ I = \frac{V^2}{\sum_i i^2 V_i - V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Herdan's Vm
docs.text:
herdan_vm

calc_herdan_vm(text)

Herdan's measure (Herdan, 1955), theoretically independent of text length. For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

\[ V_m = \sqrt{\sum_i V_i \left(\frac{i}{N}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{V}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Sichel's S
docs.text:
sichel_s

calc_sichel_s(text)

Sichel's measure (Sichel, 1975) - the share of dis legomena, lexemes with frequency 2, among all lexemes. Stable across texts of different lengths.

\[ S = \frac{V_2}{V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Michéa's M
docs.text:
michea_m

calc_michea_m(text)

Michéa's measure (Michéa, 1969) - the reciprocal of Sichel's measure. If the text has no dis legomena, the value is infinity.

\[ M = \frac{V}{V_2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Brunet's W
docs.text:
brunet_w

calc_brunet_w(text, a=0.172)

Brunet's measure (Brunet, 1978). Values for texts usually lie within 10-20.

\[ W = N^{V^{-a}}, \quad a = 0.172 \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words a float 0.172 Exponent (BRUNET_W_EXPONENT)

An a that is not a finite number raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dugast's k
docs.text:
dugast_k

calc_dugast_k(text, base=10)

Dugast's measure (Dugast, 1979), not to be confused with Dugast's U - the DTTR metric. The value depends on the logarithm base. For texts no longer than the base (\(\log N \le 1\)) the measure is undefined, and the value is nan.

\[ k = \frac{\log V}{\log \log N} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Baayen's P
docs.text:
baayen_p

calc_baayen_p(text)

Baayen's measure (Baayen, 1991) - the share of hapaxes among all words of the text. It equals the slope of the vocabulary growth curve at the end of the text: the probability that the next word is new (Evert, 2004).

\[ P = \frac{V_1}{N} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hapax ratio
docs.text:
hapax_ratio

calc_hapax_ratio(text)

The share of hapaxes among all lexemes of the text.

\[ \frac{V_1}{V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: The α₂ exponent
docs.text:
alpha2

calc_alpha2(text)

An estimate of the Zipf-Mandelbrot parameter from the lower part of the frequency spectrum (Evert, 2004). If the text has no hapaxes, the value is nan.

\[ \alpha_2 = 1 - \frac{2 V_2}{V_1} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Shannon entropy
docs.text:
entropy · Wikipedia

calc_entropy(text)

The entropy of the lexeme distribution in bits. The Hill number of order one is \(2^H\) (perplexity), of order zero - \(V\); the inverse Simpson's index estimates the one of order two.

\[ H = -\sum_k p_k \log_2 p_k \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Evenness
docs.text:
evenness

calc_evenness(text)

Pielou's evenness - the ratio of the Shannon entropy to its maximum for the given number of lexemes. For texts of a single lexeme it is undefined, and the value is nan.

\[ \frac{H}{\log_2 V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Perplexity
docs.text:
perplexity

calc_perplexity(text)

The Hill number of order one, the effective number of lexemes of the text.

\[ 2^H \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf's law slope
docs.text:
zipf_alpha · Wikipedia

calc_zipf_alpha(text)

The exponent \(\alpha\) of Zipf's law \(f(r) \propto r^{-\alpha}\), where \(r\) is the frequency rank of a lexeme, estimated by linear regression of log frequency on log rank. For natural texts \(\alpha\) is close to 1. The rank-based least squares estimate is biased; maximum likelihood is more accurate. For texts of a single lexeme the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf-Mandelbrot fit
docs.text:
Wikipedia

fit_zipf_mandelbrot(text)

Fits the Zipf-Mandelbrot law \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) to the rank-frequency distribution. With \(q = 0\) it is Zipf's law with exponent \(s\); the shift \(q\) captures the flattening of the curve on the most frequent words. The fit is by least squares in logarithmic coordinates with \(q \ge 0\), \(s \ge 0\); the lexemes of zero frequency in a counter are left out. The result is a ZipfMandelbrot named tuple with the fields c, q, s and r2 - the coefficient of determination of the fit in logarithmic coordinates. All fields are nan for texts of fewer than three lexemes, with identical frequencies of all lexemes or when the fit diverges. The parameters are unstable on short texts: the law describes large corpora.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] / Counter - List of words or a counter of their frequencies

A counter whose words are not strings or whose frequencies are not numbers raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency SourceError (check_counts).

The Zipf's law visualizer draws this fit with show_fit=True.

CodeResult 
from ests.diversity_stats import fit_zipf_mandelbrot

# the frequencies 12, 6, 4, 3 follow the law f = 12 / r exactly
words = ["a"] * 12 + ["b"] * 6 + ["c"] * 4 + ["d"] * 3
fit = fit_zipf_mandelbrot(words)
round(fit.c, 3), round(fit.q, 3), round(fit.s, 3), round(fit.r2, 3)

(12.001, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)

docs.title: Heaps' law exponent
docs.text:
heaps_beta · Wikipedia

calc_heaps_beta(text)

The exponent \(\beta\) of Heaps' law \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of vocabulary growth with text length, estimated by linear regression of log vocabulary size on log text length along the growth curve. On corpora of millions of words \(\beta\) lies within 0.4-0.6, on a single text within 0.6-0.9, so the values are comparable only between texts of similar length. The value depends on word order and needs several hundred words or more. For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words 
vocabulary_growth(text)

The vocabulary growth curve of a list of words: the vocabulary size after every word of the text.

fit_heaps(text)

Fits Heaps' law over the vocabulary growth curve of a list of words, as calc_heaps_beta does, and returns a HeapsFit named tuple with the parameters k, beta and the coefficient of determination r2, all nan for texts shorter than two words; r2 is nan for a text of one lexeme too.

The Heaps' law plot is built from fit_heaps.

docs.title: Windowed computation
docs.text:
windowed(stat)

calc_windowed(text, func, window_len=100, step=None, confidence=0.95, *, messages=MESSAGES)

The values of a metric over consecutive windows of equal length give their mean, their sample standard deviation and the confidence interval of the mean by Student's distribution. The standard way to compare texts of different lengths; Kubát and Milička's standardized TTR (not Summer's STTR) is a windowed TTR with a 1000-word window and a 95% interval. A text shorter than the window is a single window; nan windows are ignored. With fewer than two windows of a defined value the deviation and the interval are nan, and without any the mean too. A metric infinite in any window (e.g. the inverse Simpson's index on a window of unique words) makes the mean infinite and the deviation and the interval nan. The result is a WindowStats named tuple with the fields mean, std, lower, upper and n_windows, the number of the windows of a defined value.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words func Callable - Function computing the metric from a list of words window_len int 100 Window size step int None Window step; the window size by default, so the windows do not overlap confidence float 0.95 Confidence level messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A func that cannot be called raises SourceTypeError; a window_len or a step that is not an integer of at least one and a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
windowed(stat, window_len=100, step=None, confidence=0.95) computes a metric of get_stats by its name over windows: calc_windowed with the function of the metric and the parameters of the object. The other arguments, the result and the errors are those of calc_windowed; an unknown name raises UnknownStatError.

CodeResult 
ds.windowed("ttr", window_len=5)
ds.windowed("ttr", window_len=5, step=2).n_windows

WindowStats(mean=0.9333333333333332, std=0.11547005383792512, lower=0.6464898180167025, upper=1.220176848649964, n_windows=3)
6

docs.title: Lexical sophistication statistics
docs.text:
LexicalStats(source, freq_dict=None, nlp=None)

Lexical sophistication in the manner of TAALES (Kyle, Crossley and Berger, 2018) - how rare the words of a text are: statistics by a frequency dictionary and its unigram model, the shares of the frequency bands of a list of the most frequent lemmas and the lexical density. The statistics by the dictionary are computed when first read, so the bands and the lexical density need no dictionary data.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a dictionary of another class than that of the library or, without freq_dict_class, one without lookup and ipm or none at all; an analyze that does not give LexicalWord objects;
  • SourceError - a source without words.

In esTS a source that is neither a string nor a Doc and a pipeline in nlp that is not a spaCy Language raise SourceTypeError too; a source without the parts of speech, a string longer than the max_length of the pipeline and a string with a character without a UTF-8 form SourceError; and the metrics by the dictionary without the dictionary downloaded DatasetNotFoundError.

Unlike the lexical diversity metrics, which compare the words of a text with each other, here the words are compared with the frequencies of the language (TAALES). The data source is a text or a Doc object of the spaCy library.

The class extends the LexicalStats of the anyTS core with the Spanish layer: the dictionary is the Google Books Ngram FreqDict (freq_dict_class), and the ranks of the lemmas and the size of the list (rank, top_size) come from the embedded list of its 10,000 most frequent lemmas (get_rank). Whether a word is a proper noun, and whether it is a content word, comes from the annotation, so the source has to be annotated: a string is parsed with es_core_news_sm or with the pipeline passed in nlp, without the parser, the lemmatizer and the named entities, and a Doc must carry the parts of speech (a morphologizer, or a tagger with an attribute_ruler). Numbers (2020, 5,5, 3.º) are not words. The lemmas come from lemma_key, the simplemma lemma in lower case, not from the model; a proper noun keeps its lower-case form. A content word is defined as in CohesionStats: one of CONTENT_UD_POS (nouns, proper nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs) and no demonstrative. The print_stats table has the descriptions of LEXICAL_STATS_DESC of ests.constants, with the range in years out of 40.

The max_length of the pipeline is a million characters by default: split a longer text into parts, or raise max_length on a pipeline of your own and pass it in nlp.

CodeResult 
from ests import LexicalStats
from ests.datasets import FreqDict

FreqDict().download()
ls = LexicalStats("El gato estaba en la ventana y miraba a los pájaros")
ls.print_stats()

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source freq_dict FreqDict None Frequency dictionary; FreqDict() from the default directory by default nlp Language None Pipeline of spaCy that parses a string; without it the model es_core_news_sm is loaded

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description freq_dict FrequencyDictionary Frequency dictionary words, lemmas tuple[str] Words and their lemmas; the bands are counted by the lemmas keys tuple[str] Keys of the words in the dictionary entries tuple[FrequencyEntry / None] Entries of the dictionary, None for a word out of it ranks tuple[int / None] Ranks of the lemmas, None out of the list n_words, n_content_words, n_found int Number of words, of content words and of words found in the dictionary

In esTS the dictionary is a FreqDict, and its entries are the named tuples Entry. The keys of the words in the dictionary (keys, dictionary_keys) are their lemmas, and a proper noun is looked up by its form when the dictionary has it (París as parís, not the verb parir) and by its lemma otherwise (Estados of Estados Unidos as estado, a sentence-initial Miró tagged PROPN as mirar). A word is looked up without the period of an abbreviation (Sr. as sr, pág. as página); an initial (D., J.) keeps it and is out of the dictionary.

CodeResult 
ls = LexicalStats("Miró desde París hacia los Estados Unidos")
ls.lemmas
ls.keys

('miró', 'desde', 'parís', 'hacia', 'el', 'estados', 'unidos')
('mirar', 'desde', 'parís', 'hacia', 'el', 'estado', 'unidos')

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute or a property of the object, and get_stats gives them all. A mean is over the words found in the dictionary, and without them it is nan.

Metric Measures Range Higher means coverage Share of the words found in the dictionary 0-1 More words known to the dictionary mean_ipm, mean_ipm_content Mean frequency per million words of the words found, of the content words found Above 0 More frequent words mean_log_ipm, mean_log_ipm_content Mean decimal logarithm of the frequency of the words found, of the content words found Up to 6 More frequent words mean_range Mean range of the words found 0 and above Words used in more parts of the corpus mean_dispersion Mean dispersion of the words found That of the dictionary By the measure of the dictionary surprisal Mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of the dictionary, in bits 0 and above Rarer words perplexity 2 to the power of the surprisal 1 and above Rarer words p_top1000, p_top2000, p_top5000, p_top10000 Share of the words with a lemma in the top 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of the list 0-1, nan for a band beyond top_size More frequent words p_beyond_top10000 Share of the words with a lemma beyond the top 10000 0-1, nan for a list shorter than 10000 Rarer words lexical_density Share of the content words 0-1 More content words

The metrics rely on two resources; always read the means by the dictionary next to coverage.

Resource Metrics Availability FreqDict - 83,785 lemmas of Google Books Ngram (1980-2019) with ipm, range and dispersion coverage, mean_ipm*, mean_log_ipm*, mean_range, mean_dispersion, surprisal, perplexity downloaded once with FreqDict().download() The embedded list of the 10,000 most frequent lemmas of the same dictionary (ests/resources/google_books_top10000.txt, CC BY 3.0) p_top1000, p_top2000, p_top5000, p_top10000, p_beyond_top10000, band_coverage always

docs.title: Dictionary frequency
docs.text:
coverage · mean_ipm · mean_ipm_content · mean_log_ipm · mean_log_ipm_content · mean_range · mean_dispersion · Google Books Ngram

The metrics are computed from the FreqDict entries for the keys of the words (keys, entries): the means are taken over the words found in the dictionary, over all of them or only over the content words. The range is the number of years out of 40 (1980-2019) in which the lemma occurs in the books, and the dispersion is Juilland's D over the years, from 0 to 100. The mean frequency in ipm is sensitive to function words (el - 98,000 ipm, de - 71,000), so for comparing texts the log frequency or the mean over the content words is more convenient.

Rare words lower the coverage and the log frequency and raise the surprisal and the share beyond the top 10000:

CodeResult 
from ests import LexicalStats

ls = LexicalStats("El felinólogo examinaba al minino con parsimonia")
ls.coverage, ls.mean_log_ipm, ls.surprisal, ls.p_beyond_top10000

(0.8571428571428571, 2.3529196195453976, 13.70650419215419, 0.4285714285714286)

docs.title: Surprisal and perplexity
docs.text:
surprisal · perplexity

calc_surprisal(lemmas, freq_dict)

The mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of a frequency dictionary, in bits; a word out of the dictionary gets its lowest frequency min_ipm. The perplexity is 2 to its power.

\[ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{w} -\log_2 \frac{\max(\textrm{ipm}_w, \textrm{min\_ipm})}{10^6} \] Parameter Type Default Description lemmas list[str] - Keys of the words in the dictionary freq_dict FrequencyDictionary - Frequency dictionary

No words give nan; keys that are not a list of strings and a dictionary without ipm and min_ipm raise SourceTypeError, a lowest frequency that is not above zero ParameterError.

In esTS the dictionary is a FreqDict with the lowest frequency of 0.1 ipm: a dictionary of another class raises SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
from ests.datasets import FreqDict
from ests.lexical_stats import calc_surprisal

calc_surprisal(["gato", "estar", "felinólogo"], FreqDict())

15.392368319318606

docs.title: Frequency bands
docs.text:
p_top1000 · p_top2000 · p_top5000 · p_top10000 · p_beyond_top10000 · band_coverage(bands, unique)

The share of the words whose lemma has a rank (rank) within the top \(N\) of the list, for the bounds 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of FREQUENCY_BANDS; the share beyond the top 10000 is the rest, the words out of the list included. A band beyond the size of the list (top_size) is nan, and so is the share beyond the top 10000 for a list shorter than 10000.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words with a rank up to } N}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

This builds a frequency band profile in the manner of the Lexical Frequency Profile. The bands take the lower-case form of a proper noun: a proper noun whose form is a common lemma gets its rank (Gobierno 106), while the names and their inflected parts (Madrid, Estados) fall beyond the top 10000, so a text full of names has a greater share there.

get_rank(lemma)

The rank of a lemma by the embedded list, None for a lemma outside the list; the lemma may be in any case.

Parameter Type Default Description lemma str - Lemma - the key of lemma_key 
load_top_lemmas()

The whole list from the file ests/resources/google_books_top10000.txt, derived from Google Books Ngram under CC BY 3.0: the rank of every lemma, starting from 1. The list holds the 10,000 most frequent lemmas of the frequency dictionary by decreasing frequency, the parts of speech of a lemma summed; it leaves out the proper nouns, the single letters other than the Spanish words a, e, o, u, y, á, é, ó, and the two-letter lemmas and Roman numerals that simplemma does not know (pp, xix), while the abbreviations of the references (cit) and the English words of the bibliographies (the) stay.

CodeResult 
from ests.lexical_stats import get_rank, load_top_lemmas

get_rank("el"), get_rank("gato"), get_rank("felinólogo")
len(load_top_lemmas())

(1, 2851, None)
10000

docs.title: Morphological statistics
docs.text:
MorphStats(source, nlp=None)

The morphological statistics of a text: the part of speech and the grammatical features of every word in Universal Dependencies terms, their distributions and the markers of Spanish computed from them. The data source is a text or a Doc object of the spaCy library; the statistics are computed when the object is created.

A text is parsed with es_core_news_sm or with the pipeline passed in nlp; a Doc must carry the parts of speech, which come from a morphologizer (or a tagger with an attribute_ruler), and the lemmas, which come from a lemmatizer. Words are taken from the tokens, punctuation marks and symbols are dropped. A text longer than the max_length of the pipeline - a million characters by default - has to be split into parts, or max_length raised on a pipeline of your own passed in nlp.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, a pipeline that is not a spaCy Language;
  • SourceError - a source without words, a Doc without the parts of speech or the lemmas (a Doc of spacy.blank("es") or of a pipeline with the lemmatizer excluded), a string longer than the max_length of the pipeline or with a character that has no UTF-8 form;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - a string without nlp when the model es_core_news_sm is not installed.
CodeResult 
from ests import MorphStats

text = "Si tuviera tiempo, leería el libro que me recomendaste ayer"
ms = MorphStats(text)
ms.print_stats("pos", "mood")

Verb                          |    3
Noun                          |    2
Pronoun                       |    2
Subordinating conjunction     |    1
Determiner                    |    1
Adverb                        |    1

------------------Mood------------------
Unknown                       |    7
Subjunctive                   |    1
Conditional                   |    1
Indicative                    |    1

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
Every statistic is an attribute of the object, a tuple of the values of a feature by word (None for a word the model gives no value of the feature), and get_stats gives the distributions of their values. The values are read from token.pos_ and token.morph of the parse, that is, by context. The statistics are the part of speech and the fifteen features of MORPHOLOGY_FEATURES; the value Unknown in the printed tables means that the model gave the word no value of the feature. The other features the models annotate (AdvType, Foreign, NumForm, Number[psor], PrepCase, Typo, PunctSide, PunctType) are not counted but stay in tags.

Statistic Feature Values pos Part of speech NOUN, PROPN, ADJ, ADV, VERB, AUX, PRON, DET, NUM, ADP, CCONJ, SCONJ, PART, INTJ, SYM, X case Case Nom, Acc, Dat, Com definite Definiteness Def, Ind degree Degree Cmp, Sup, Abs gender Gender Masc, Fem mood Mood Ind, Sub, Imp, Cnd num_type Numeral type Card, Ord, Frac number Number Sing, Plur person Person 1, 2, 3 polarity Polarity Neg polite Politeness Form poss Possessive Yes pron_type Pronoun type Art, Prs, Dem, Ind, Int, Rel, Neg, Tot, Exc reflex Reflexive Yes tense Tense Pres, Past, Imp, Fut verb_form Verb form Fin, Inf, Part, Ger

A feature with several values keeps the form of CoNLL-U: qué, quién, cuál have pron_type equal to Int,Rel, and usted has case equal to Acc,Nom. print_stats names the values by MORPHOLOGY_STATS_DESC of ests.constants, and such a value by the names of its parts - "Interrogative or relative", "Accusative or nominative".

Warning

The statistics are as good as the annotation of the model. es_core_news_sm mis-analyses verbs with enclitic pronouns (dámelo, cuéntamelo come out as nouns with invented lemmas) and tags the imperatives of tú as indicative (Abre la ventana gets Mood=Ind), so p_imperative under-reports and p_indicative absorbs the orders: in the dialogue of the corpus of literature it finds about one imperative in ten. es_core_news_lg does little better (15%); the transformer model es_dep_news_trf passed in nlp finds 87% of them, and in drama p_imperative rises from 1.6% to 7.5% - at the cost of about 1 GB with PyTorch and five times the time on a CPU, and it needs the single line breaks of a hard-wrapped text joined first.

docs.title: Markers of Spanish
docs.text:
get_markers() · print_markers()

The shares of the forms that mark the register of a Spanish text, each of its own base (MORPHOLOGY_MARKERS_DESC), so the markers of texts of different lengths can be compared directly; a marker whose base is empty - a text without verbs, without a copula, without adverbs - is nan. The subjunctive marks hypothesis and subordination, estar a state against the property of ser, and the adverbs in -mente a formal, written register.

Marker Share Base p_indicative, p_subjunctive, p_conditional, p_imperative of the indicative, subjunctive, conditional and imperative mood finite forms p_infinitive, p_gerund, p_participle of infinitives, gerunds and participles verb forms p_ser of ser copulas ser and estar p_mente_adverbs of the adverbs in -mente adverbs

The first four markers share the base of the finite forms and sum to one unless the model leaves a finite form without a mood. The next three share the base of all the verb forms of verbs and auxiliaries: a participle that the model annotates as an adjective (la casa pintada) is out of the base, the ones of the compound tenses and the passive (he leído, fue escrito) are in.

The base of p_ser is the copular uses alone, read from the parse: the auxiliaries of the passive and of the progressive (fue escrito, es financiado, está cantando) are left out, while es alta, está cansada and lo importante es que vengas count. For a Doc without a parse the marker is nan.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
get_stats(*args, filter_none=False) returns the distributions of the values of the statistics as a dictionary of counts for each. The statistics are chosen by their names separated by commas, all of them without names, and filter_none=True drops the words without the feature (None). A name that is not a statistic raises UnknownStatError - here and in print_stats and explain_text.

print_stats(*args, filter_none=False) prints the distributions of the chosen statistics as tables, the frequent values first (the example at the top of the page), and explain_text(*args, filter_none=False) returns the words of the text in order with the values of the chosen statistics.

docs.title: Phonostatistics
docs.text:
PhonStats(source, words_extractor=None, window_len=3)

The phonetic statistics of a text: its sounds by class, their clusters, sequences and repetitions, and its syllables. A sound is a letter of a word by default, or a sound of its transcription when a library gives one. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy; the words are taken in lower case, and an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a window that is not an integer of at least 2.

Besides the errors above, a string with a character without a UTF-8 form raises SourceError from the Spanish tokenizer.

The class extends the PhonStats of the anyTS core with the sounds of Spanish. The sounds are those of the transcription of the words (transcribe), not their letters: ch, ll, rr and qu are one sound, h and the u of que and gui none, and x two. The pronunciation is the one of the standard of Spain: yeísmo (ll and y are one sound) and distinción (c before e and i and z are θ, apart from s). The classes of the sounds are the constants of ests.constants in the table below. The syllables are those of syllabify, by the orthographic rules, and a hiatus is two vowels in two neighbouring syllables of a word (po-e-ta, dí-a, bú-ho). The words of a string are extracted by the Spanish WordsExtractor; without an extractor the words of a Doc come from its tokens. No trained model is needed. The print_stats table has the English descriptions of the core, anyts.constants.PHON_STATS_DESC.

Class Sounds Constant Vowels a, e, i, o, u VOWEL_SOUNDS Sonorants m, n, ɲ (ñ), l, r (the tap and the trill are one sound) SONORANT_SOUNDS Voiced obstruents b (b, v), d, g, ʝ (y, ll) VOICED_SOUNDS Voiceless obstruents p, t, k (c, qu, k), f, θ (c, z), s, x (j, g), tʃ (ch) VOICELESS_SOUNDS CodeResult 
from ests import PhonStats

# The first stanza of Sonatina by Rubén Darío (Prosas profanas, 1896)
sonatina = (
    "La princesa está triste... ¿qué tendrá la princesa?\n"
    "Los suspiros se escapan de su boca de fresa,\n"
    "que ha perdido la risa, que ha perdido el color.\n"
    "La princesa está pálida en su silla de oro,\n"
    "está mudo el teclado de su clave sonoro;\n"
    "y en un vaso olvidada se desmaya una flor."
)
ps = PhonStats(sonatina)
ps.print_stats()

docs.title: Transcription
docs.text:
transcribe(word)

Transcribes a word into its sounds, those PhonStats counts. The word is split into syllables (syllabify) and every syllable is read by the rules of the Spanish orthography; the characters that are no Spanish letters (digits, hyphens) are left out.

Spelling Sound Example a, á; e, é; i, í; o, ó; u, ú, ü a, e, i, o, u canción - k a n θ i o n h none; hi before a vowel at the start of a syllable is ʝ ahora - a o r a, hielo - ʝ e l o ch tʃ hechizo - e tʃ i θ o c before e, i; z θ cena - θ e n a c elsewhere, qu before e, i, k k queso - k e s o g before e, i; j x gente - x e n t e g elsewhere, gu before e, i g guerra - g e r a ll; y before a vowel ʝ calle - k a ʝ e y at the end of a syllable i hoy - o i r, rr r perro - p e r o ñ ɲ niño - n i ɲ o v b vaca - b a k a x; x at the start of a word k s; s examen - e k s a m e n, xilófono - s i l o f o n o w u whisky - u i s k i

The pronunciation is the one of the standard of Spain, with yeísmo and distinción. A rule reads the spelling of a word, not its history: the x of México is k s, as in examen.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.

transcribe("hechizo")

Every metric is an attribute of the object, computed when it is created, and get_stats gives them all.

Metric Measures Range Higher means p_vowels Share of the vowels among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds A more vocalic text p_sonorants Share of the sonorants among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds A more sonorous text p_voiced Share of the voiced obstruents among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds More voiced obstruents p_voiceless Share of the voiceless obstruents among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds More voiceless obstruents consonant_vowel_ratio Ratio of the consonants to the vowels 0 and above, nan without vowels Denser consonants p_heavy_clusters Share of the clusters of three consonants or more 0-1, nan without clusters Heavier clusters p_hiatus Hiatuses of word_hiatus per word 0 and above, nan without sounds More vowels in a row cv_entropy Shannon entropy of the CV patterns of the words, in bits 0 and above, nan without sounds More varied shapes of the words hardness Voiceless obstruents to the vowels and the sonorants 0 and above, nan without vowels and sonorants A harder sound alliteration Repetition index of the consonants in windows of window_len words 0 and above, nan for a text shorter than the window or with no consonant shared by two words Consonants repeated closer together assonance Repetition index of the vowels in windows of window_len words 0 and above, nan for a text shorter than the window or with no vowel shared by two words Vowels repeated closer together p_open_syllables Share of the syllables that end in a vowel 0-1, nan without syllables More open syllables mean_syllable_len Mean length of a syllable in sounds 1 and above, nan without syllables Longer syllables

The functions of the cards are imported from ests.phon_stats; they take words as strings and count over the sounds of their transcription.

docs.text:
p_vowels · p_sonorants · p_voiced · p_voiceless

The share of the sounds of every class - the vowels, the sonorants and the voiced and voiceless obstruents - among the sounds of all of them; a sound of skipped or of no class (a digit, a letter of another script) counts in none.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of sounds of the class}}{\textrm{Number of vowels and consonants}} \]

The number of the consonants n_consonants to the number of the vowels n_vowels.

docs.title: Consonant clusters
docs.text:
p_heavy_clusters · c_clusters

calc_consonant_clusters(text)

The distribution of the consonant clusters of the words by length, the attribute c_clusters. A cluster is a run of consonant sounds inside a word, across the syllables, a single consonant between vowels or at the edge of a word included: instrumento has the clusters n s t r (4), m (1) and n t (2). The digraphs are one sound (calle, perro, chico), and x is two (extra - k s t r). p_heavy_clusters is the share of the heavy clusters:

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of clusters of 3 consonants or more}}{\textrm{Number of clusters}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings.

docs.title: Hiatuses
docs.text:
p_hiatus

calc_hiatus(text)

The number of hiatuses: two vowels next to each other in two syllables of a word, as syllabify splits them - po-e-ta, dí-a, le-er, a-é-re-o (two). A silent h between the vowels does not break the hiatus (bú-ho, a-ho-ra), and the vowels of a diphthong are one syllable and no hiatus (cie-lo, ciu-dad). p_hiatus is the number of hiatuses of the text per word.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings.
CodeResult 
from ests.phon_stats import calc_hiatus

calc_hiatus(["poeta", "búho", "cielo", "aéreo"])

4

docs.title: Entropy of the CV patterns
docs.text:
cv_entropy

The Shannon entropy of the CV patterns of the words (cv_pattern), in bits, where \(P(p)\) is the share of the words with the pattern \(p\) among the words that have one.

\[ -\sum_{p} P(p) \log_2 P(p) \] 
calc_cv_entropy(text)

The entropy of the CV patterns of a list of words: the higher it is, the more varied the phonetic shape of the words of the text. Words without sounds (numbers) are left out; nan for a text without other words.

cv_pattern(word)

The CV pattern of a word or a syllable: the vowels are written V and the consonants C, over the sounds of the transcription - queso is CVCV, hora VCV, examen VCCVCVC. A syllable is read as a word of its own, so its initial x is s, as at the start of a word: xi is CV, while the syllable xi of México counts as CCV in PhonStats.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words (calc_cv_entropy) word str - Word or syllable (cv_pattern)

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings (calc_cv_entropy), a word that is not a string (cv_pattern).
CodeResult 
from ests.phon_stats import calc_cv_entropy, cv_pattern

cv_pattern("queso"), cv_pattern("examen")
calc_cv_entropy(["poeta", "búho", "cielo", "aéreo"])

('CVCV', 'VCCVCVC')
1.5

docs.title: Hardness
docs.text:
hardness

The number of the voiceless obstruents to the number of the vowels and the sonorants.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of voiceless obstruents}}{\textrm{Number of vowels} + \textrm{Number of sonorants}} \]

A text of p, t, k, s and θ sounds harder than a text of vowels and m, n, l, r.

docs.title: Alliteration and assonance
docs.text:
alliteration · assonance

calc_alliteration(text, window_len=3)

calc_assonance(text, window_len=3)

The alliteration and assonance indices of a list of words: the repetition index calc_repetition_index of anyts.phon_stats over the consonant and over the vowel sounds of the transcription of the words. The sounds count, not the letters: casa and queso repeat k, cena and casa do not; every vowel counts, stressed or not.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words window_len int 3 Window in words (PHON_WINDOW_LEN)

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings;
  • ParameterError - a window that is not an integer of at least 2.
calc_repetition_index(words, window_len, features=None)

The repetition index: the number of windows of window_len neighbouring words where a feature (a letter or a sound) occurs in two words or more, summed over the features, divided by the number expected if the words stood in random order. A window of shuffled words is a sample without replacement, so for a feature found in \(K\) of the \(N\) words, a window of \(w\) words holds it in two words or more with the hypergeometric probability

\[ P = 1 - \frac{\binom{N-K}{w} + K \binom{N-K}{w-1}}{\binom{N}{w}} \]

and the expected number is the sum of these probabilities over the features times the \(N - w + 1\) windows. Since the expectation comes from the text itself, the index shows whether the repetitions gather in neighbouring words, not how frequent a feature is: it averages to 1 over the orders of the words and is well above 1 when the repetitions come closer than chance. A word counts a feature once; the index is nan for a text shorter than the window or with no feature shared by two words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] / list[list[str]] - Features of every word: a string of its letters or a collection of its sounds window_len int - Window in words, at least 2 features Collection[str] None Features to count, all of them by default

Words that are not a list of strings or of collections of strings and features that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a window_len that is not an integer of at least 2 ParameterError.

For words in random order the indices average to 1: the 150 books of the corpus of literature with their words shuffled give 0.98 to 1.02. On the books as written the index of alliteration is a little below 1 for verse and prose alike, 0.90 to 0.99 with a median of 0.95, and the index of assonance about 1, 0.99 to 1.01: over a whole book neighbouring words share a consonant a little less often than chance. The 4,259 sonnets give medians of 0.92 and 0.98, with a wide spread over such short texts (0.59 to 1.30 for alliteration). The repetitions of a poem are local, and the places where they gather are shown by the layer alliteration of the highlighting.

CodeResult 
from ests.phon_stats import calc_alliteration, calc_assonance

# Garcilaso de la Vega, Égloga III
words = "en el silencio sólo se escuchaba un susurro de abejas que sonaba".split()
calc_alliteration(words), calc_assonance(words)

(1.0232558139534884, 1.115942028985507)

docs.title: Syllables
docs.text:
p_open_syllables · mean_syllable_len

The syllables are the sounds of every syllable of a word by syllable_sounds; a syllable without a sound of the classes (a number) is no syllable, in c_syllable_patterns too. An open syllable ends in a vowel by its CV pattern (cv_pattern), and the length of a syllable is the number of its sounds.

The sounds of a syllable are its transcription, the first syllable of a word read as the start of the word: the xi of xilófono is s i, the xi of México k s i.

is_open_syllable(syllable)

Checks whether a syllable is open: an open syllable ends in a vowel sound - ca, que, hoy (the final y is the vowel i); car and pan are closed. The syllable is read as a word of its own.

Parameter Type Default Description syllable str - Syllable

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a syllable that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.phon_stats import is_open_syllable

is_open_syllable("hoy"), is_open_syllable("car")

(True, False)

docs.text:

from ests import PhonStats

PhonStats("Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal").get_stats()

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text:
ReadabilityStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, preset='general')

The readability metrics of a text from its basic statistics: the mean sentence length in words, the mean word length in syllables or letters, the share of polysyllabic and of long words and the variability of word length. The data source is a text, a Doc object of spaCy or ready basic statistics, which are reused as they are; the extractors are passed on to the basic statistics of a text or a Doc. The formulas count only the letters of the counted words, so a word extractor that drops words does not lengthen the mean word.

The metrics are properties computed on each access, so a change of the coefficients of an object applies at once.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string, a Doc nor basic statistics, basic statistics of a class other than those of the library, an extractor of another type, a string or a Doc to a class without basic_stats_class;
  • SourceError - a source without words or sentences;
  • ParameterError - an unknown preset or one that is not a string.

The metrics assess readability on the side of the language - the complexity of words and syntactic constructions, not the typographic design of the text. They presume that short sentences are easier to read than long ones, long words make reading harder, and low-frequency and unfamiliar words slow a reader down.

The class extends the ReadabilityStats of the anyTS core with the formulas and tables of Spanish, given in the cards of the metrics: the basic statistics of esTS, which take the Spanish SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor by default, the coefficient presets of the Flesch reading ease, the formulas of Gutiérrez de Polini, Crawford and SOL, the consensus grade over Crawford, SOL and the reading ease, the school stages of Spain, the interpretation scales and the reading speeds of Spanish readers. A string with a character without a UTF-8 form, as a file read with the wrong encoding gives, raises SourceError from the Spanish tokenizer.

CodeResult 
from ests import ReadabilityStats

text = "Hay tres clases de mentiras: mentiras, malditas mentiras y estadísticas"
rs = ReadabilityStats(text)
rs.print_stats()

                Metric                |  Value
-------------------------------------------------
Flesch reading ease (Szigriszt-Pazos) |  53.55
Gutiérrez de Polini comprehensibility |  33.50
Crawford grade                        |   5.81
Legibilidad µ                         |  50.94
SOL grade (SMOG for Spanish)          |   9.26
LIX readability index                 |  60.00
RIX readability index                 |   5.00
Consensus grade                       |   9.00
Reading time (min)                    |   0.04

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc / BasicStats - Data source (a string, a Doc object or ready basic statistics) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Sentence extraction tool words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool preset str 'general' Coefficient preset: general or classic

The object keeps the basic statistics of the text in bs, the name of the preset in preset, read-only, and the coefficients of the preset by formula in coefficients, a copy that can be changed for one object. An object of another preset can reuse the basic statistics: ReadabilityStats(rs.bs, preset="classic").

docs.title: Coefficient presets
docs.text:
A preset sets the coefficients a, b, c of the Flesch reading ease c − a·ASL − b·ASW, where ASL is the mean number of words per sentence and ASW the mean number of syllables per word, and the scale by which describe_level, describe and the consensus grade read it. The other formulas do not depend on the preset.

Preset Source Formula Scale general Szigriszt-Pazos (1993), fórmula de perspicuidad 206.835 − 1.0·ASL − 62.3·ASW INFLESZ (Barrio-Cantalejo et al., 2008) classic Fernández Huerta (1959) 206.84 − 1.02·ASL − 60·ASW the seven bands of the author

The formula of Fernández Huerta takes the mean sentence length, with the correction of Law (2011). The table of all coefficients is ests.constants.READABILITY_PRESETS, and the scale of each preset is in PRESET_SCALES.

CodeResult 
classic = ReadabilityStats(rs.bs, preset="classic")
rs.flesch_reading_easy, classic.flesch_reading_easy
rs.describe_level(), classic.describe_level()

(53.545000000000016, 58.640000000000015)
('algo difícil', 'bastante difícil')

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
A formula is computed by the function of its card on the counts of bs. The reading ease takes its coefficients from coefficients, set by the preset; the formulas of Gutiérrez de Polini, Crawford and SOL are computed with the coefficients of their functions, and coefficients does not affect them. A formula of counts gives nan when the number of words or of sentences it divides by is zero.

Metric Measures Range Higher means flesch_reading_easy Ease of reading by the sentence length and the syllables per word Nominally 0-100, above 100 for the simplest texts and below 0 for the hardest An easier text gutierrez_polini_index Comprehensibility by the letters per word and the sentence length Below 95.2, ordinary prose 30-50 An easier text crawford_grade Grade by the sentences and the syllables per 100 words Years of schooling, below 0 for the simplest texts; fitted on grades 1-6 A harder text mu_index Mean word length in letters against its variance Above 0, nan with fewer than two words or without variability An easier text sol_grade Grade by the polysyllabic words per sentence, SMOG converted to Spanish Years of schooling, slightly below 0 for the simplest texts A harder text lix Sentence length and the share of long words 0 and above A harder text rix Long words per sentence 0 and above A harder text consensus_grade Median of the grade formulas and the reading ease as a grade Years of schooling A harder text reading_time Reading time at the reading speed (reading_speed) Minutes, above 0 A longer text smog_index Grade by the polysyllabic words per sentence, English coefficients; outside get_stats Years of schooling A harder text

The other formulas of the core with their English coefficients - flesch_kincaid_grade, coleman_liau_index, automated_readability_index and gunning_fog_index - are properties of the object outside get_stats as well, since they are fitted on English texts; their cards are on the anyTS page.

docs.title: Flesch reading ease
docs.text:
flesch_reading_easy · Szigriszt-Pazos, 1993 · Fernández Huerta, 1959

calc_flesch_reading_easy(n_syllables, n_words, n_sents, a=1.0, b=62.3, c=206.835)

The ease of reading a text by the mean sentence length in words and the mean word length in syllables.

\[ c - a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} - b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

The default coefficients are those of the fórmula de perspicuidad of Szigriszt-Pazos (1993). The coefficients of Fernández Huerta (1959) are given by the classic preset, with the correction of Law (2011): the last term takes the mean sentence length, not the number of sentences per 100 words that Fernández Huerta printed.

Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 1.0 Coefficient a, at the mean sentence length b float 62.3 Coefficient b, at the mean word length in syllables c float 206.835 Coefficient c, the constant

The scale of describe_level and describe follows the preset: the level_scale method of esTS gives the scale of ests.constants.READING_EASE_SCALES named in PRESET_SCALES - the INFLESZ scale of Barrio-Cantalejo et al. (2008) for general and the bands of Fernández Huerta for classic. The INFLESZ scale:

Value Level Text type [80, ∞) muy fácil comics, children's books [65, 80) bastante fácil primary school textbooks [55, 65) normal general press [40, 55) algo difícil secondary school textbooks (−∞, 40) muy difícil scientific and technical texts 
flesch_reading_easy_to_level(flesch_reading_easy, scale='inflesz')

The band of a scale of READING_EASE_SCALES for the reading ease: inflesz (above), szigriszt (Szigriszt-Pazos, 1993, integer bands: muy difícil 0-15, árido 16-35, bastante difícil 36-50, normal 51-65, bastante fácil 66-75, fácil 76-85, muy fácil 86-100) and fernandez_huerta (Fernández Huerta, 1959: muy difícil below 30, difícil 30-50, bastante difícil 50-60, normal 60-70, bastante fácil 70-80, fácil 80-90, muy fácil above 90). The describe_level method reads the reading ease of the object by any of them with its scale parameter.

Parameter Type Default Description flesch_reading_easy float - Value of the reading ease scale str 'inflesz' Name of the scale: inflesz, szigriszt or fernandez_huerta

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an unknown scale or one that is not a string, a value that is not a finite number.
CodeResult 
from ests.readability_stats import flesch_reading_easy_to_level

flesch_reading_easy_to_level(53.5), flesch_reading_easy_to_level(53.5, "szigriszt")

('algo difícil', 'normal')

Sources: Szigriszt Pazos, F. Sistemas predictivos de legibilidad del mensaje escrito: fórmula de perspicuidad. Universidad Complutense de Madrid, 1993. Barrio-Cantalejo, I. M. et al. Validación de la Escala INFLESZ para evaluar la legibilidad de los textos dirigidos a pacientes. Anales del Sistema Sanitario de Navarra, 31(2), 2008. Fernández Huerta, J. Medidas sencillas de lecturabilidad. Consigna, 214, 1959. Law, G. Error in the Fernández Huerta readability formula. LINGUIST List 22.2332, 2011.

docs.title: Gutiérrez de Polini comprehensibility
docs.text:
gutierrez_polini_index · Gutiérrez de Polini, 1972

calc_gutierrez_polini_index(n_letters, n_words, n_sents)

The fórmula de comprensibilidad of Gutiérrez de Polini, by the mean word length in letters and the mean sentence length. The higher the value, the easier the text. It was fitted on sixth-grade school texts and has no scale of its own: ordinary prose lies between 30 and 50, and a text above 70 is read by a young child.

\[ 95.2 - 9.7 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - 0.35 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences CodeResult 
from ests.readability_stats import calc_gutierrez_polini_index

calc_gutierrez_polini_index(n_letters=60, n_words=10, n_sents=1)

33.5

Source: Gutiérrez de Polini, L. E. Investigación sobre lectura en Venezuela. Ministerio de Educación, Caracas, 1972.

docs.title: Crawford grade
docs.text:
crawford_grade · Crawford, 1989

calc_crawford_grade(n_syllables, n_words, n_sents)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the sentences and the syllables per 100 words. The formula was fitted on Spanish primary school readers of grades 1-6, so higher values saturate. The higher the value, the harder the text.

\[ -0.205 \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of sentences}}{\textrm{Number of words}} + 0.049 \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - 3.407 \] Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences CodeResult 
from ests.readability_stats import calc_crawford_grade

calc_crawford_grade(n_syllables=23, n_words=10, n_sents=1)

5.812999999999999

Source: Crawford, A. N. Fórmula y gráfico para determinar la comprensibilidad de textos del nivel primario en castellano. Lectura y Vida, 10(4), 1989.

docs.title: Legibilidad µ
docs.text:
mu_index · Muñoz Baquedano and Muñoz Urra, 2006

calc_mu_index(c_letters)

The mean number of letters per word divided by its sample variance, times 100; there are no coefficients to fit. Words without letters (numbers) are left out; with fewer than two words or without variability the index is undefined (nan).

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\bar{x}}{s^2}, \quad s^2 = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1} \]

where \(x_i\) is the number of letters of a word and \(n\) the number of words.

Parameter Type Default Description c_letters dict[int, int] - Distribution of words by number of letters

A c_letters that is not a mapping raises SourceTypeError.

The variance divided by n − 1 is the cuasivarianza of the authors, which reproduces the worked example of their manual; ReadabilityStats passes BasicStats.c_letters. The bands of the authors, ests.constants.MU_SCALE, are the scale of describe_level and describe:

Value Level [91, ∞) muy fácil [81, 91) fácil [71, 81) un poco fácil [61, 71) adecuado [51, 61) un poco difícil [31, 51) difícil (−∞, 31) muy difícil 
mu_to_level(mu_index)

The band of the scale MU_SCALE for a value of Legibilidad µ.

Parameter Type Default Description mu_index float - Value of Legibilidad µ

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a value that is not a finite number, such as the undefined index (nan).
CodeResult 
from ests import BasicStats
from ests.readability_stats import calc_mu_index, mu_to_level

mu = calc_mu_index(BasicStats(text).c_letters)
mu, mu_to_level(mu)

(50.943396226415096, 'difícil')

Source: Muñoz Baquedano, M. Legibilidad y variabilidad de los textos. Boletín de Investigación Educacional, 21(2), 2006; the program and manual at legibilidadmu.cl.

docs.title: SOL grade
docs.text:
sol_grade · Contreras et al., 1999

calc_sol_grade(n_complex, n_sents, a=0.74, b=-2.51)

The years of schooling needed to read a Spanish text: the conversion of Contreras et al. of its SMOG index S, computed with the original coefficients, into the grade of the English scale. The higher the value, the harder the text. ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of three or more syllables.

\[ b + a \cdot S \] Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of words of three or more syllables n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.74 Coefficient a, at the SMOG index b float -2.51 Coefficient b, the constant

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a number of words or sentences that is not a non-negative integer.
CodeResult 
from ests.readability_stats import calc_smog_index, calc_sol_grade

calc_smog_index(n_complex=5, n_sents=1), calc_sol_grade(n_complex=5, n_sents=1)

(15.903189008614273, 9.258359866374562)

Source: Contreras, A., García-Alonso, R., Echenique, M., Daye-Contreras, F. The SOL formulas for converting SMOG readability scores between health education materials written in Spanish, English, and French. Journal of Health Communication, 4(1), 1999.

docs.title: LIX readability index
docs.text:
lix · Björnsson, 1968

calc_lix(n_long_words, n_words, n_sents)

The mean sentence length plus the percentage of long words, the words of more than six letters; there are no coefficients to fit. The values read as text types:

Value Text 0-30 very easy texts, children's books 30-40 easy texts, fiction, newspaper articles 40-50 texts of medium difficulty, magazine articles 50-60 hard texts, popular science, official texts 60-100 very hard texts, laws and bureaucratic language \[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of long words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_long_words int - Number of long words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences

These bands, anyts.constants.LIX_LEVELS with English labels, are the scale of describe_level and describe; its last band is open above.

docs.title: RIX readability index
docs.text:
rix · Anderson, 1983

calc_rix(n_long_words, n_sents)

The long words, of more than six letters, per sentence; there are no coefficients to fit. The values read as grades:

Value Grade < 0.2 1 0.2-0.5 2 0.5-0.8 3 0.8-1.3 4 1.3-1.8 5 1.8-2.4 6 2.4-3.0 7 3.0-3.7 8 3.7-4.5 9 4.5-5.3 10 5.3-6.2 11 6.2-7.2 12 > 7.2 college \[ \frac{\textrm{Number of long words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_long_words int - Number of long words n_sents int - Number of sentences

In esTS RIX has no scale of bands, so describe_level("rix") raises ParameterError; describe takes the grades of Anderson as years of schooling (anyts.constants.RIX_GRADES, college as 13) and gives the stage of the Spanish school system and the reader age by grade_to_age.

docs.title: Consensus grade
docs.text:
consensus_grade

The consensus_grade attribute is the median of the values of the grade formulas (grade_stats) rounded half up, together with the reading ease in years of schooling (reading_ease_to_grade), not rounded. A library aligns the bounds of reading_ease_grades, and of each scale of preset_reading_ease_grades, with its scale of the reading ease, so that the consensus grade and describe read the value alike.

The grade formulas of esTS (ests.constants.READABILITY_GRADE_STATS) are Crawford and SOL. esTS converts the reading ease by the scale of the preset with its own reading_ease_to_grade(flesch_reading_easy) method, which calls flesch_reading_easy_to_grade with the preset of the object, so the reading_ease_grades of the core are not used.

Warning

Crawford was fitted on primary school readers and saturates for adult texts; SOL was fitted on health education materials. The consensus grade of a technical text mostly reflects the reading ease band.

calc_consensus_grade(grades, flesch_reading_easy=None, preset='general')

The median of the values of the grade formulas rounded half up, together with the reading ease converted into years of schooling by flesch_reading_easy_to_grade with the scale of the preset, not rounded.

\[ \textrm{median}\left(\lfloor g_1 + 0.5 \rfloor, \ldots, \lfloor g_k + 0.5 \rfloor, \textrm{grade}(\textrm{reading ease})\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description grades list[float] - Values of the grade formulas flesch_reading_easy float None Value of the reading ease preset str 'general' Coefficient preset of the reading ease

Raises:

  • ParameterError - no values at all, a grade or a reading ease that is not a finite number, an unknown preset or one that is not a string;
  • SourceTypeError - grades that are not a list.
flesch_reading_easy_to_grade(flesch_reading_easy, preset='general')

Conversion of the Flesch reading ease into years of schooling for the consensus grade by the bands of the scale of the preset, ests.constants.READING_EASE_GRADES: the grade of the first band whose lower bound the value reaches, or 13 below the last bound; values above 100 belong to the first band. With the general preset, through the text types of the INFLESZ bands and the school stages of Spain:

Reading ease Grade Text type [80, ∞) 3 comics and children's books, primary school grades 1-3 [65, 80) 5 primary school textbooks, grades 4-6 [55, 65) 8 general press, ESO [40, 55) 11 secondary school textbooks, bachillerato (−∞, 40) 13 scientific texts, university

With the classic preset, through the interpretation table of Flesch kept by Fernández Huerta: 90-100 - 5, 80-90 - 6, 70-80 - 7, 60-70 - 8.5, 50-60 - 10, 40-50 - 11, 30-40 - 12, below 30 - 13.

Parameter Type Default Description flesch_reading_easy float - Value of the reading ease preset str 'general' Coefficient preset whose scale is read

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a reading ease that is not a finite number (the nan of a text without words or sentences, an infinity), an unknown preset or one that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.readability_stats import calc_consensus_grade, flesch_reading_easy_to_grade

flesch_reading_easy_to_grade(53.545), flesch_reading_easy_to_grade(53.545, "classic")
calc_consensus_grade([5.813, 9.258], 53.545)

(11, 10)
9.0

docs.title: Reading time
docs.text:
reading_time · reading_time_by_speed(wpm) · reading_time_by_norm(norm) · Brysbaert, 2019 · Ripoll, Tapia and Aguado, 2020

calc_reading_time(n_words, wpm=278)

The reading time of a text in minutes: the number of words divided by the reading speed.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{wpm}} \]

A number of words that is not a non-negative integer and a speed that is not a positive number raise ParameterError.

The default speed is the silent reading speed of adults in Spanish, 278 words per minute, from the meta-analysis of Brysbaert (2019). The norms of reading_time_by_norm, ests.constants.READING_SPEED_NORMS, are the mean speeds of Spanish-speaking students by school year from the meta-analysis of Ripoll, Tapia and Aguado (2020) - grade_1 to grade_11, that is primary school 1-6, ESO 7-10 and bachillerato 11 - and of adults from Brysbaert (2019), as pairs (aloud, silent):

Norm Aloud Silent grade_1 49 30 grade_2 73 79 grade_3 85 95 grade_4 104 125 grade_5 114 137 grade_6 124 155 grade_7 134 180 grade_8 136 176 grade_9 143 180 grade_10 164 200 grade_11 161 186 adult 191 278 Parameter Type Default Description n_words int - Number of words wpm float 278 Reading speed, words per minute (READING_SPEED_WPM)

Sources: Brysbaert, M. How many words do we read per minute? A review and meta-analysis of reading rate. Journal of Memory and Language, 109, 2019. Ripoll, J. C., Tapia, M. M., Aguado, G. Velocidad lectora en alumnado hispanohablante: un metaanálisis. Revista de Psicodidáctica, 25(2), 2020.

docs.title: SMOG index
docs.text:
smog_index · McLaughlin, 1969

calc_smog_index(n_complex, n_sents, a=1.043, b=30, c=3.1291)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the polysyllabic words per sentence. In the original formula the polysyllabic words have three or more syllables and b brings their number to a sample of 30 sentences.

\[ a \cdot \sqrt{b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of polysyllabic words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}}} + c \]

A number of words or sentences that is not a non-negative integer raises ParameterError.

The index is fitted on English and stays outside get_stats; for Spanish it is the input of the SOL grade. ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of three or more syllables.

Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of polysyllabic words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 1.043 Coefficient a, at the square root b float 30 Coefficient b, the number of sentences of the sample c float 3.1291 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
describe_grade(stat) returns the school stage and reader age for the consensus grade or the grade formula stat, consensus_grade by default; another metric raises ParameterError.

The grade formulas of esTS are crawford_grade and sol_grade.

describe_level(stat) returns the band of the interpretation scale (level_scale) of the metric stat, flesch_reading_easy by default; a metric without a scale of bands and an undefined value (nan) raise ParameterError.

In esTS the metrics with a scale of bands are flesch_reading_easy, mu_index and lix, and describe_level(stat, scale) also takes a scale of READING_EASE_SCALES for the reading ease - inflesz, szigriszt or fernandez_huerta - in place of the scale of the preset, None by default; a scale given for another metric and an unknown scale raise ParameterError. level_scale(stat) returns the scale of a metric as lower bounds and their bands - for the reading ease the scale of the preset - or None for a metric without a scale of bands, RIX included.

describe(stat) returns the reading of any metric by its scale: for the consensus grade and a grade formula the school stage and reader age (describe_grade), for a metric with a scale of bands (level_scale) its band, for another metric of grade_scales the stage and age of the years of schooling its scale gives, and None for a metric without a scale or with an undefined value (nan). A name that is neither in stats_desc nor a public property of the class raises UnknownStatError.

In esTS the grade formulas are read as stages of the Spanish school system, and so is RIX through the grades of Anderson; the formula of Gutiérrez de Polini, the reading time and the formulas of the core with their English coefficients have no scale.

reading_time_by_speed(wpm) returns the reading time of the text in minutes at the speed wpm, words per minute; a speed that is not a positive number raises ParameterError.

reading_time_by_norm(norm) returns the reading times of the text in minutes at the speeds of the norm norm of reading_speed_norms, in their order; an unknown norm raises ParameterError.

The norms of esTS give the speeds aloud and silently, so the method returns the reading times aloud and silently.

get_stats() returns a dictionary of the readability metrics of stats_desc.

print_stats() prints a table of the readability metrics with their descriptions from stats_desc under the headers of stats_headers.

CodeResult 
rs.describe_grade(), rs.describe_grade("crawford_grade")
rs.describe_level(scale="szigriszt"), rs.describe_level("mu_index")
rs.level_scale("flesch_reading_easy")
rs.reading_time_by_speed(200), rs.reading_time_by_norm("grade_4")
{stat: rs.describe(stat) for stat in rs.get_stats()}
rs.get_stats()
