docs.title: Scales
docs.text: The describe_level method reads the reading ease, Legibilidad µ and LIX by the scales of bands of their cards, and describe reads any metric: these three by the same scales, the grade formulas, the consensus grade and RIX by the school stages of grade_to_age; for a metric without a scale it gives None.

docs.title: School stage and age
docs.text:
grade_to_age(grade)

The stage of the Spanish school system and the reader age by the value of a grade formula, in years of schooling counted from the first year of primary school at the age of six: the value is rounded half up and falls into the first stage whose last year it does not exceed, values below 1 into grades 1-3. The stages are ests.constants.GRADE_AGE_LEVELS and POSTGRADUATE_LEVEL:

Grade Stage Age 1-3 primary school, grades 1-3 6-9 years 4-6 primary school, grades 4-6 9-12 years 7-10 ESO 12-16 years 11-12 bachillerato 16-18 years 13-16 university 18-22 years above 16 postgraduate over 22 years Parameter Type Default Description grade float - Value of a grade formula

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a grade that is not a finite number.
CodeResult 
from ests.readability_stats import grade_to_age

grade_to_age(9.0), grade_to_age(17)

('ESO (12-16 years)', 'postgraduate (over 22 years)')

docs.title: Band of a scale
docs.text:
scale_level(value, scale)

The band of a scale for a value: the scale is given as the lower bounds of its bands in descending order, the value falls into the first band whose bound it reaches, and the lowest band is open below.

Parameter Type Default Description value float - Value of a metric scale list[tuple[float, Any]] - Lower bounds and their bands in descending order

A value that is not a finite number and a scale that is empty, not a list of pairs of a finite lower bound and a band or with bounds that do not descend raise ParameterError.

The scales of esTS are READING_EASE_SCALES and MU_SCALE of ests.constants; LIX is read by the LIX_LEVELS of the core.

CodeResult 
from ests.constants import MU_SCALE, READING_EASE_SCALES
from ests.readability_stats import scale_level

scale_level(50.9, MU_SCALE), scale_level(50.9, READING_EASE_SCALES["fernandez_huerta"])

('difícil', 'bastante difícil')

docs.title: Style metrics
docs.text:
StyleStats(source, words_extractor=None, stopwords=None, top_n=10, cliches=None, nlp=None, nausea_stopwords=None)

The style metrics of a text: the SEO metrics of Advego and Text.ru and the markers of the officialese style. The services publish no formulas, so the common definitions are taken. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy.

The SEO metrics are counted on the words of the word extractor, in lower case by default, or on the tokens of a Doc; an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc. The markers are counted on the word forms in lower case (forms), whatever the extractor.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type, a list that is not a list of strings;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a top_n that is not an integer of at least one.

The class extends the StyleStats of the anyTS core with the hooks of Spanish, given in the cards of the metrics: the stopwords, the compound prepositions, parenthetical expressions and clichés that the Spanish-language guides to plain language warn about, found with their contractions and the forms of their verbs, and the nouns derived from a verb among the nouns of the spaCy model. The words of a string are extracted by the Spanish WordsExtractor and are not lemmatized, so the forms of one word count as different words, as in Advego; to compute by lemmas, pass a WordsExtractor with use_lexemes=True and lowercase=True. The print_stats table takes the descriptions of ests.constants.STYLE_STATS_DESC.

The verbal nouns need the parts of speech and the lemmas: a Doc gives its own annotation, also when an extractor takes its text, and a string is parsed with es_core_news_sm or with the pipeline passed in nlp the first time verbal_nouns or markers() is read - the other metrics of a string need no model. A string longer than the max_length of the pipeline is parsed in parts of whole sentences. Besides the errors above, a pipeline that is not a spaCy Language raises SourceTypeError and a string with a character without a UTF-8 form raises SourceError from the Spanish tokenizer; reading verbal_nouns or markers() raises SourceError for a Doc without the parts of speech or the lemmas and for a string with a sentence longer than the max_length of the pipeline.

The examples of this page take a notice written in the administrative style:

CodeResult 
from ests import StyleStats

official = (
    "En el marco del procedimiento de referencia, y a efectos de dar cumplimiento a lo "
    "dispuesto en la normativa vigente, se procedió a la revisión de la documentación "
    "presentada. No obstante, en virtud de la resolución de la comisión, se llevará a cabo "
    "la notificación de la misma a la mayor brevedad, en tiempo y forma."
)
ss = StyleStats(official)
ss.print_stats()

                  Metric                  |  Value
-----------------------------------------------------
Classic nausea                            |   2.83
Academic nausea (%)                       |  17.86
Water content (%)                         |  57.14
Spam score (%)                            |  37.50
Naturalness by Zipf's law (%)             |  53.57
Verbal nouns (% of nouns)                 |  47.06
Compound prepositions (per 100 words)     |   5.36
Parenthetical expressions (per 100 words) |   1.79
Officialese clichés (per 100 words)       |   8.93

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; for a Doc it is applied to its text stopwords list[str] / set[str] None Words of water; is_stopword if not given top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words of the academic nausea and the naturalness by Zipf's law (NAUSEA_TOP_N) cliches list[str] / set[str] None Clichés; OFFICIALESE_CLICHES if not given nlp Language None spaCy pipeline that parses a string for the verbal nouns; the model es_core_news_sm of ests.utils.get_nlp if not given nausea_stopwords list[str] / set[str] None Stopwords left out of the most frequent words of the academic nausea; is_stopword if not given

A set of words is taken in sorted order. NAUSEA_TOP_N is a constant of anyts.constants.

check_params(top_n, *, messages=MESSAGES)

Checks the number of the most frequent words: one that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words tuple[str] Words of the SEO metrics forms tuple[str] Word forms in lower case, of the markers

The metrics are properties computed on each access.

The pipeline of the parameter nlp is kept in the attribute nlp, None if not given.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
get_stats gives all the metrics. A metric is computed by the function of its card on words or forms with the hooks of the class.

Metric Measures Range Higher means classic_nausea Repetition of the most frequent word 0 and above, grows with the text One word pressed harder academic_nausea Share of the most frequent significant words 0-100 % A narrower vocabulary water Share of the words without content 0-100 % Less content per word spam Share of the repeated words 0-100 % More repetition zipf_naturalness Agreement of the top frequencies with Zipf's law 0-100 %, nan without ranks to compare Closer to a natural text verbal_nouns Share of the verbal nouns among the nouns 0-100 %, nan without nouns A more nominal style compound_prepositions Compound prepositions per 100 words 0-100 More officialese parentheticals Parenthetical expressions per 100 words 0-100 More insertions cliches Cliches per 100 words 0-100 More cliches

The functions of the cards are imported from ests.style_stats. The cards give the norms of Advego, Text.ru, pr-cy and megaindex; the norms of the services are meant for texts of several hundred words, and on short texts nausea and spam are uninformative. esTS gives the metrics no scales, so describe gives None; the markers of the officialese have no norms.

The functions of the core cards check their words too: words and keywords that are not a list of strings, and a normalize that cannot be called, raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Classic nausea
docs.text:
classic_nausea · Advego

calc_classic_nausea(text)

How much one word is pressed: the square root of the occurrences \(f_1\) of the most frequent word. The value is not corrected for the length of the text, so it grows with the text; no words give 0.

\[ \sqrt{f_1} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

The norm of Advego is at most 7, 1-5 in practice.

docs.title: Academic nausea
docs.text:
academic_nausea · nausea_words() · Advego

calc_academic_nausea(text, top_n=10, stopwords=None)

The share of the occurrences of the top_n most frequent significant words among all the words, in percent. The exact formula of Advego is not published. With the stopwords the top ten of almost any text would be de, la, que, el, and its nausea above the norm. The norm of Advego is 5-15%, for texts of several hundred words: in a short text the top ten is a large share of the words whatever the style.

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\sum_{w \in \textrm{top}_n} f_w}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words (NAUSEA_TOP_N) stopwords list[str] / set[str] None Stopwords left out of the most frequent words; is_stopword if not given

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings, stopwords that are not a list or a set of strings;
  • ParameterError - a top_n that is not an integer of at least one.
find_nausea_words(text, top_n=10, stopwords=None)

The top_n most frequent words without the stopwords, those the academic nausea counts, with their occurrences: the most frequent first, words of equal frequency in the order of the text. A stopword is a word of stopwords, in any case, or, without the list, a word of is_stopword. The parameters and the errors are those of calc_academic_nausea.

is_stopword(word)

Whether a word is a stopword, in any case: the 265 forms of ests.constants.STOPWORDS - the closed classes of the grammar: articles and the other determiners (este, cada, mucho), pronouns (él, cuyo, nadie), prepositions, conjunctions and interjections, with the adverbs that point, relate or ask (aquí, así, dónde) and the ones that negate, affirm or focus (no, solo, también) - and the one-word parenthetical expressions of PARENTHETICALS (finalmente, naturalmente). The forms of the old orthography are included (á, ó, tí). StyleStats takes it for the academic nausea without nausea_stopwords and for the water content without stopwords.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.style_stats import find_nausea_words, is_stopword

is_stopword("Aquel"), is_stopword("sin"), is_stopword("trigo")
find_nausea_words(["gato", "y", "gato", "y", "perro"], top_n=1)

(True, True, False)
{'gato': 2}

docs.title: Water content
docs.text:
water · Text.ru

calc_water(text, stopwords=None)

The share of the words without content, in percent: the words of stopwords, in any case, or, without the list, the stopwords of is_stopword. The norms of Text.ru: up to 15% natural, 15-30% excessive, above 30% high.

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of water words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words stopwords list[str] / set[str] None Words of water; is_stopword if not given

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings, stopwords that are not a list or a set of strings.

The water content of Spanish

The norms of Text.ru are set for Russian, which has no articles; a Spanish text has more water by its grammar alone. Compare the water content of texts with each other, not with the norm.

docs.title: Spam score
docs.text:
spam · Text.ru

calc_spam(text)

The share of the repeated words in percent: every occurrence of a word after the first.

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\textrm{Number of words}}\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

To compute it by lemmas, extract the words with lemmatization. The norms of Text.ru: up to 30% natural, 30-60% SEO-optimized, above 60% spammed.

docs.title: Naturalness by Zipf's law
docs.text:
zipf_naturalness · pr-cy, megaindex

calc_zipf_naturalness(text, top_n=10, *, messages=MESSAGES)

The agreement of the frequencies of the most frequent words with the ideal distribution \(f_r = f_1 / r\), where \(r\) is the rank. The first rank is ideal by construction, and above \(f_1\) the ideal frequency falls below one, so the ranks run from 2 to \(R = \min(\textrm{top\_n}, V, f_1)\). Negative values are cut to 0. Without ranks to compare - all the words hapaxes, one lexeme or top_n below 2 - the value is nan.

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{1}{R - 1} \sum_{r=2}^{R} \frac{|r \cdot f_r - f_1|}{f_1}\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words (NAUSEA_TOP_N) messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

The ideal distribution is that of Zipf's law; the norm of pr-cy and megaindex is at least 50%.

docs.title: Verbal nouns
docs.text:
verbal_nouns

calc_verbal_nouns(nouns)

The share of the nouns derived from a verb among the lemmas of the nouns, in percent; nan without nouns. A noun is derived from a verb by its suffix - -ción, -sión, -miento, -anza, -encia, -ancia, -aje, -dura, -azgo (revisión, nombramiento, aprendizaje) - or is one of the nouns whose derivation leaves no suffix behind (uso, pago, envío), as in the split predicates of SyntaxStats. The rule also catches the nouns of other origins with the same endings (ciencia, distancia). The function takes the lemmas of the tokens tagged NOUN, not the words: a noun and a verb form may be spelt alike (uso, viaje).

Parameter Type Default Description nouns list[str] - Lemmas of the nouns

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - nouns that are not a list of strings.
noun_lemmas(doc)

The lemmas of the tokens of a Doc tagged NOUN. StyleStats takes the nouns of a Doc the same way, and those of a string from its parse by the pipeline of nlp or get_nlp, run without the parser and the named entities.

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is not a Doc;
  • SourceError - a Doc without the parts of speech or the lemmas.
CodeResult 
from ests.style_stats import calc_verbal_nouns, noun_lemmas
from ests.utils import get_nlp

calc_verbal_nouns(["revisión", "proyecto", "nombramiento", "casa"])
lemmas = noun_lemmas(get_nlp()("Se procedió a la revisión de los proyectos"))
lemmas, calc_verbal_nouns(lemmas)

50.0
(['revisión', 'proyecto'], 50.0)

docs.title: Compound prepositions and clichés
docs.text:
compound_prepositions · cliches

calc_phrase_density(text, phrases)

The occurrences of the phrases of a list per 100 words, with the contractions and the forms of the verbs of expand_phrases. At every position the longest phrase is taken, and the phrases found do not overlap. StyleStats counts this way, over the word forms (forms), the compound prepositions of COMPOUND_PREPOSITIONS (en el marco de, a efectos de, en virtud de) and the clichés of OFFICIALESE_CLICHES (dar cumplimiento, proceder a, a la mayor brevedad) or of the parameter cliches.

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of phrases found}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words phrases list[str] / set[str] - Phrases, words separated by spaces

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings, phrases that are not a list or a set of strings.
expand_phrases(text, phrases)

The phrases spelled out in the forms of a text, each with the phrase of the list it spells out. A phrase ending in a or de also takes the contraction with the article (a efectos del, conforme al), and a phrase whose first word is an infinitive takes the forms of the text with that lemma (proceder a - procedió a, ser de aplicación - es de aplicación). The lemma is the one of simplemma, and a pronominal lemma counts for its verb (llévese - llevar); the forms simplemma does not lemmatize - some participles (ha dado, ha hecho) and the imperative dese - are given by IRREGULAR_VERB_FORMS. The words after the verb rule out the readings as a noun (el hecho, el puesto). When two phrases spell out the same words, a phrase written so wins over the forms of another (a efectos del stays itself next to a efectos de), and then the first phrase of a list, or of a set in sorted order.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words phrases list[str] / set[str] - Phrases, words separated by spaces

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings, phrases that are not a list or a set of strings.
CodeResult 
from ests.constants import COMPOUND_PREPOSITIONS
from ests.style_stats import calc_phrase_density, expand_phrases

expand_phrases(["se", "procedió", "al", "cierre"], ["proceder a"])
words = "se procedió a la revisión en el marco del proyecto".split()
calc_phrase_density(words, COMPOUND_PREPOSITIONS)

{'proceder a': 'proceder a',
 'proceder al': 'proceder a',
 'procedió a': 'proceder a',
 'procedió al': 'proceder a'}
10.0

The compound prepositions (42) and the clichés (74) are the ones the Spanish-language guides to plain language and style manuals of the administrations flag:

Source Author Year Libro de estilo de la Justicia RAE, CGPJ 2017 Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, 2nd ed. RAE, ASALE online Guía panhispánica de lenguaje claro y accesible RAE, ASALE 2024 Claridad y derecho a comprender Comisión de Modernización del Lenguaje Jurídico 2011 Cómo escribir con claridad European Commission 2015 Manual del Lenguaje Administrativo Ayuntamiento de Madrid about 2008 Comunicación Clara. Guía práctica Ayuntamiento de Madrid 2017 Guía de Comunicación Clara Comunidad de Madrid 2021 Manual de Lenguaje y Estilo Administrativo Región de Murcia 2008 Manual de Lenguaje Claro Secretaría de la Función Pública, Mexico 2007 Guía de lenguaje claro para servidores públicos Departamento Nacional de Planeación, Colombia 2015 Guía de lenguaje claro Colombia Compra Eficiente 2024 Manual de lenguaje claro Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires 2024 Guía para el uso del Lenguaje Claro Legislatura de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires 2024 Manual de Estilo del Lenguaje para uso de la Administración Pública Provincial Provincia de Salta about 2007

Left out are the forms the guides recommend (sobre la base de) or accept (de acuerdo a) and the phrases with frequent neutral uses (en este sentido), but for proceder a and llevar a cabo. A few compound prepositions have neutral uses too (a través de, en caso de, con respecto a), so the density of a neutral text is not zero: compare texts with each other.

docs.title: Parenthetical expressions
docs.text:
parentheticals

calc_parentheticals(text)

The parenthetical expressions of PARENTHETICALS (sin embargo, es decir, por ejemplo, finalmente) per 100 words: the phrases of the list with their contractions (expand_phrases) and, outside them, the one-word expressions of the list. The punctuation is not looked at, so the list holds the expressions set off by commas or standing at the edge of a sentence in most of their occurrences in the corpus of literature, with the series of order (en primer lugar, en segundo lugar). The adverbs of doubt (tal vez, quizá), sobre todo, sin duda and además are not in the list.

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of parenthetical expressions}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - words that are not a list of strings.
find_parentheticals(text)

The bounds of the parenthetical expressions of calc_parentheticals as slices of the list of words, in order. The parameter and the errors are those of calc_parentheticals.

is_parenthetical(word)

Whether a word is one of the one-word expressions of PARENTHETICALS (finalmente, naturalmente, verbigracia), in any case.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ests.style_stats import calc_parentheticals, find_parentheticals, is_parenthetical

words = ["sin", "embargo", "el", "gato", "finalmente", "duerme"]
find_parentheticals(words), calc_parentheticals(words)
is_parenthetical("Finalmente")

([(0, 2), (4, 5)], 33.33333333333333)
True

docs.title: Keyword density
docs.text:
keyword_density(*keywords) · Text.ru

calc_keyword_density(text, keywords, normalize=str.lower)

The occurrences of every keyword per 100 words. A keyword of several words separated by spaces is a sequence of words whose occurrences may overlap. The words and the keywords are compared by their normalized forms, and the keywords of a set come in sorted order.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words keywords list[str] - Keywords or phrases normalize Callable[[str], str] str.lower Normalized form of a word and of a keyword

To compare by lemmas, extract the words with lemmatization and pass lemmas.

CodeResult 
from ests import StyleStats

text = "Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal, en tres tristes trastos"
StyleStats(text).keyword_density("tres tristes", "trigo")

{'tres tristes': 16.666666666666668, 'trigo': 8.333333333333334}

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
keyword_density(*keywords) gives the density of keywords and phrases in percent (calc_keyword_density with normalize of the class), nausea_words() the most frequent significant words of the academic nausea with their occurrences (find_nausea_words).

markers() returns the markers of the officialese found by metric - verbal_nouns, compound_prepositions, parentheticals, cliches - as the forms write them, in the order of the text.

A phrase is found with its contractions and the forms of its verb (expand_phrases). The verbal nouns need the parts of speech and the lemmas, as their metric does, so a string is parsed by the model and a Doc without them raises SourceError.

CodeResult 
ss.markers()

{'verbal_nouns': ('procedimiento',
                  'referencia',
                  'cumplimiento',
                  'revisión',
                  'documentación',
                  'resolución',
                  'comisión',
                  'notificación'),
 'compound_prepositions': ('en el marco del', 'a efectos de', 'en virtud de'),
 'parentheticals': ('no obstante',),
 'cliches': ('dar cumplimiento',
             'procedió a',
             'llevará a cabo',
             'a la mayor brevedad',
             'en tiempo y forma')}

The notice of 56 words has three compound prepositions, five clichés and one parenthetical expression, and almost half of its nouns are derived from a verb. The anaphoric de la misma, which the guides also advise against, is not counted.

The other methods - get_stats, to_dataframe, print_stats and describe - are those of the statistics interface of the anyTS core; the style metrics of esTS have no scales, so describe gives None for the metrics of get_stats. The same notice in plain language:

CodeResult 
plain = (
    "Hemos revisado los documentos que nos envió, como pide la ley. La comisión ha "
    "decidido su caso y le avisaremos lo antes posible."
)
StyleStats(plain).get_stats()
ss.describe("water"), ss.describe("cliches")

{'classic_nausea': 1.4142135623730951,
 'academic_nausea': 43.47826086956522,
 'water': 43.47826086956522,
 'spam': 4.3478260869565215,
 'zipf_naturalness': 100.0,
 'verbal_nouns': 25.0,
 'compound_prepositions': 0.0,

 'cliches': 0.0}
(None, None)

The plain version has no compound prepositions, parenthetical expressions or clichés, and a quarter of its nouns are derived from a verb. The academic nausea says nothing of the style here: neither notice repeats a significant word, so it is ten words over the length of the text, 10/56 and 10/23.

docs.title: Syntactic statistics
docs.text:
SyntaxStats(source, nlp=None)

The syntactic statistics of a text by its dependency tree (Ivanov, Solnyshkina and Solovyev 2018): the measures of the tree and of the syntactic constructions. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy, and it has to be parsed: a string is parsed with es_core_news_sm or with the pipeline passed in nlp, without the named entities, and a Doc must carry the dependencies, which come from a parser, and the lemmas, which come from a lemmatizer. Punctuation marks, symbols (%, €, +) and whitespace are no nodes of the tree, and the distances are counted in positions of words.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, a pipeline in nlp that is not a spaCy Language;
  • SourceError - a source without words; a Doc without the dependencies or the lemmas (a Doc of spacy.blank("es"), of a pipeline without a parser or with the lemmatizer excluded); a string longer than the max_length of the pipeline or with a character without a UTF-8 form;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - a string without nlp when the model is not installed.

The class extends the SyntaxStats of the anyTS core with the Spanish layer. The relations and features are those of the Universal Dependencies annotation of the es_core_news_sm, es_core_news_md and es_core_news_lg models, and the statistics are as good as the parse. The clauses, the passive, the negations and the split predicates follow the rules of Spanish given in the cards of the metrics, and esTS adds its own metrics of the chains of de, the gerund clauses and the sentences with se. The constructions of the administrative style - the passive with ser and with se, the participial and gerund clauses, the chains of de, the split predicates - are the ones the Spanish-language guides to plain language (lenguaje claro) warn about. The print_stats table takes the descriptions of SYNTAX_STATS_DESC of ests.constants.

The max_length of the pipeline is a million characters by default: split a longer text into parts, or raise max_length on a pipeline of your own and pass it in nlp.

CodeResult 
from ests import SyntaxStats

text = (
    "La revisión de las cuentas del organismo fue realizada por el comité. "
    "Se llevó a cabo la reforma, aprobada en 1998, sin que nadie hiciera "
    "mención de los problemas."
)
ss = SyntaxStats(text)
ss.print_stats()

                    Statistic                     |  Value
-------------------------------------------------------------
Mean dependency distance                          |   2.26
Standard deviation of the dependency distance     |   2.15

The functions of the cards are imported from ests.syntax_stats; those of the measures of the tree that esTS does not re-export are on the anyTS page.

docs.title: Dependency distance
docs.text:
mean_dependency_distance · std_dependency_distance · max_dependency_distance · p_adjacent_dependencies

The dependency distance (Liu 2008) is the distance between a word and its head in positions of words, punctuation left out; the head of a sentence has none. mean_dependency_distance and std_dependency_distance are the mean and the standard deviation of the distances of the text, max_dependency_distance the mean of the longest distance of every sentence that has one, and p_adjacent_dependencies the share of the distances of 1. One-word sentences enter none of the metrics. The distances are those of calc_dependency_distances of anyts.syntax_stats.

docs.title: Tree depth
docs.text:
tree_depth

The depth of the dependency tree of a sentence is the longest path from its head to a leaf, in relations between words, 0 for a sentence of one word; the metric is its mean over the sentences. The depth is that of calc_tree_depth of anyts.syntax_stats.

docs.title: Leaves and subtrees
docs.text:
leaves_per_sent · subtrees_per_sent · nodes_per_leaf

A leaf is a word without dependent words (count_children), a subtree a word with them. The nodes per leaf are the words of a sentence over its leaves, averaged over the \(S\) sentences.

\[ \frac{1}{S} \sum_{s=1}^{S} \frac{\textrm{Number of words of } s}{\textrm{Number of leaves of } s} \]

The distribution of the words by number of dependents is the attribute c_children.

docs.title: Valency of the finite verbs
docs.text:
verb_valency

calc_valency(token, join_hyphens=False)

The valency of a token: the number of its dependent words, the relations cc, conj, parataxis and punct left out (anyts.constants.VALENCY_IGNORED_DEPS); with join_hyphens=True a hyphenated dependent counts once, so came in Some-one came has one dependent and not two.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A finite verb is a word tagged VERB with VerbForm=Fin (is_finite_verb of anyts.utils). The Spanish models tag the participle of a compound tense or of the passive with ser (ha llegado, fue construida) as the verb and its auxiliary as AUX, so such predicates are left out.

docs.title: Coordination chains
docs.text:
coordination_chains_per_sent · mean_coordination_chain_len

A coordination chain is a group of words linked by conj: manzanas, peras y ciruelas is one chain of three. A nested coordination and an enumeration split between several heads are one chain too; the length of a chain is the number of its words. The chains are those of calc_coordination_chains of anyts.syntax_stats.

docs.title: Clauses
docs.text:
clauses_per_sent · mean_clause_len

is_clause_head(token)

Checks whether a word heads a clause: the head of the sentence or, by the form of its predicate (predicate_form), a word with ccomp, advcl, acl (a relative clause included), csubj or parataxis (anyts.constants.CLAUSE_DEPS). A finite predicate heads its clause (dijo que había llegado, estaba cantando, los regalos que te van a dar), also under xcomp, which the models give to some finite complements; a predicate in the form of a participle or a gerund heads no clause of that kind - such predicates are counted apart (llegando tarde, habiendo llegado tarde) - and neither does one in the form of an infinitive under acl (el deseo de irse, el miedo de ser robado). Under xcomp an infinitive heads a clause by is_infinitive_clause, and a predicative adjective (parece cansado) heads none. A parenthetical (parataxis) and a coordinated predicate (conj of the head of a clause) count only when they can be a predicate (is_predicate), so that parentheticals such as por ejemplo are no clauses; an infinitive the models attach as conj to the verb of a periphrasis (tiene que salir, va a salir) makes one predicate with it (is_infinitive_periphrasis).

is_infinitive_clause(token)

Checks whether an infinitive under xcomp heads a clause of its own: a predicate in the form of an infinitive that completes its head (quiere salir, le hizo reír, quiere ser médico, quiere ser elegido, cree haber ganado), unless the two make a periphrasis (is_infinitive_periphrasis) or the head is a verb of RAISING_VERBS, parecer (parece dormir).

is_infinitive_periphrasis(token)

Checks whether an infinitive makes a periphrasis with its head: the head is a verb of INFINITIVE_PERIPHRASES (NGLE, ch. 28) and the infinitive is linked to it by one of the words of that verb - a mark, case or cc before the infinitive, or the word right before it, the old spelling á read as a. The verbs are poder, soler and deber with no word (puede salir, suele salir), deber de, tener que, haber que, haber de, ir a, venir a, pasar a, volver a, tornar a, empezar a and por, comenzar a and por, principiar a, poner a, echar a, romper a, llegar a, alcanzar a, acabar de and por, terminar de and por, dejar de, cesar de, parar de, estar para and por. The lemma of the head is that of the model, or of ests.utils.lemmatize when the model gives none of these verbs (it can read a verb opening a sentence as a proper noun: Solía salir).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

The mean length of a clause is the number of the words over the number of the clauses.

docs.title: Subordinate clauses
docs.text:
subordinate_clauses_per_sent · p_complex_sents

is_subordinate_clause_head(token)

Checks whether a word heads a subordinate clause: a clause head (is_clause_head) with ccomp, advcl, acl, csubj (anyts.constants.SUBORDINATE_CLAUSE_DEPS) or xcomp, or a coordinated predicate of a subordinate clause, by the relation of the first word up its chain of conjuncts. An infinitive clause under a verb (quiere salir) is a subordinate clause; the numbers of those alone are the attributes n_infinitive_clauses and infinitive_clauses_per_sent, which get_stats does not give.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

p_complex_sents is the share of the sentences with at least one subordinate clause.

CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import is_clause_head, is_subordinate_clause_head
from ests.utils import get_nlp

doc = get_nlp()("Él quiere salir, pero tiene que quedarse porque parece cansado.")
[token.text for token in doc if is_clause_head(token)]
[token.text for token in doc if is_subordinate_clause_head(token)]

['quiere', 'salir', 'tiene', 'parece']
['salir', 'parece']

docs.title: Modifiers of a noun
docs.text:
modifiers_per_noun

count_noun_modifiers(token, join_hyphens=False)

Counts the modifiers of a noun phrase: the dependents with the relations amod, det, nmod, nummod, acl and their subtypes (anyts.constants.NOUN_MODIFIER_DEPS); conj and appos are no modifiers.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

The nouns are the words tagged NOUN or PROPN: la nueva casa de mi padre gives casa three modifiers, la, nueva and padre.

docs.title: Chains of de
docs.text:
de_chains_per_sent · max_de_chain_len

calc_de_chains(tokens)

The lengths of the chains of de in the order of the words: the chains of calc_modifier_chains whose modifiers are complements with de; el aumento de la eficiencia del uso de los recursos is a chain of length 3, and a single complement (el uso del agua) is no chain.

is_de_modifier(token)

Checks whether a word is a complement introduced by de: a word with the relation nmod whose preposition (case) is de or its contraction del (DE_PREPOSITIONS): el uso del agua, but not la vuelta al campo.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens (calc_de_chains) token Token - Token (is_de_modifier)

max_de_chain_len is the longest chain of the text, 0 without chains.

CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import calc_de_chains
from ests.utils import get_nlp

calc_de_chains(get_nlp()("El aumento de la eficiencia del uso de los recursos fue notable."))

[3]

docs.title: Participial clauses
docs.text:
participle_clauses_per_sent · mean_participle_clause_len

The clauses headed by the words of the hook is_participle_clause; the length of a clause is the number of the words in the subtree of its head (subtree_len).

is_participle_clause(token)

Checks whether a word heads a participial clause: a participle (is_participle) that is not the head of the sentence, carries no auxiliary or copula (has_auxiliary) and has at least one dependent (calc_valency). la casa, construida por los obreros, se vendió has one, while ha pintado and fue construida are predicates. SyntaxStats counts the participial clauses by the same rule.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import is_participle_clause, subtree_len
from ests.utils import get_nlp

doc = get_nlp()("La casa, construida por los obreros en 1900, fue vendida.")
[(token.text, subtree_len(token)) for token in doc if is_participle_clause(token)]

[('construida', 6)]

docs.title: Gerund clauses
docs.text:
gerund_clauses_per_sent · mean_gerund_clause_len

is_gerund_clause(token)

Checks whether a word heads a gerund clause: a predicate in the form of a gerund (predicate_form), simple or compound (llegando tarde, habiendo llegado tarde, siendo elegido presidente), that is not the head of the sentence and has at least one dependent besides its auxiliaries and copulas (calc_valency). The periphrases are left out: one with a finite auxiliary (está cantando) is a finite predicate, and a gerund the models attach as xcomp or advcl to a verb of GERUND_PERIPHRASIS_VERBS - quedar, llevar, seguir, venir, ir, andar, continuar, acabar (sigue trabajando, acabó reconociendo) - heads no clause. The length of a clause is the number of the words in the subtree of the gerund (subtree_len).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import is_gerund_clause
from ests.utils import get_nlp

doc = get_nlp()("Llegando tarde, encontró la puerta cerrada y siguió trabajando.")
[token.text for token in doc if is_gerund_clause(token)]

['Llegando']

docs.title: Passive
docs.text:
p_passive · p_agentless_passive

is_passive(token)

Checks whether a word is a passive verb form: a verb (VERB) that is a participle with the auxiliary ser (PASSIVE_AUX) as aux or cop - la casa fue construida, also when the models read the auxiliary as a copula, el proyecto es financiado - or that carries the se of the passive (expl:pass, SE_PASSIVE_DEP: se construyó la casa). A participle that modifies a noun (la casa construida por los obreros) is a participial clause instead.

is_agentless(token)

Checks whether a passive form has no agent: none of its dependents is one of is_agent - la casa fue construida, but not la casa fue construida por los obreros. A word that is no passive form (is_passive) gives False.

is_agent(token)

Checks whether a word is the agent of a passive: a complement whose preposition (case) is por (AGENT_PREPOSITION), whatever its relation, since the models have no obl:agent.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

The verb forms of p_passive are the words tagged VERB.

CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import is_agentless, is_passive
from ests.utils import get_nlp

doc = get_nlp()(
    "La casa fue construida por los obreros y el proyecto es financiado por el Estado. "
    "Se construyó la casa."
)
[(token.text, is_agentless(token)) for token in doc if is_passive(token)]

[('construida', False), ('financiado', False), ('construyó', True)]

docs.title: Sentences with se
docs.text:
se_passives_per_sent · impersonal_se_per_sent

se_passives_per_sent counts the se of the passive (expl:pass, SE_PASSIVE_DEP: se construyó la casa) per sentence, impersonal_se_per_sent the se of an impersonal sentence (expl:impers, SE_IMPERSONAL_DEP: se vive bien, aquí se trabaja mucho), as the model labels them. A verb with the se of the passive is a passive form of p_passive too.

Warning

es_core_news_sm tells the three se of Spanish apart poorly - it rarely marks an impersonal se and reads se fue dando un portazo as a passive - so read se_passives_per_sent and impersonal_se_per_sent together rather than apart.

CodeResult 
ss = SyntaxStats("Se construyó la casa en un año. Aquí se trabaja mucho.")
ss.se_passives_per_sent, ss.impersonal_se_per_sent

(0.5, 0.5)

docs.title: Infinitives, negations and split predicates
docs.text:
infinitives_per_sent · negations_per_sent · split_predicates_per_sent

The infinitives (is_infinitive of anyts.utils), the words of negation of the hook is_negation and the split predicates of the hook find_split_predicates, per sentence.

is_negation(token)

Checks whether a word is a word of negation: a word with Polarity=Neg, which the models give to no alone, or one of NEGATION_WORDS in any case - no, nunca, jamás, nada, nadie, ninguno with its forms, tampoco; a conjunction (ni of ni... ni) is none. Every such word counts, so the negative concord of Spanish, where one negation is written twice (no vino nadie), gives two. SyntaxStats counts the negations by the same rule.

find_split_predicates(tokens)

is_light_verb(token)

is_split_predicate_noun(token, verb)

The split predicates, pairs of a verb and a noun in the order of the words, replace a verb with a light verb and a noun: hacer una revisión instead of revisar. A light verb (is_light_verb) is a VERB with a lemma of LIGHT_VERBS - hacer, dar, tomar, tener, poner, llevar, prestar, efectuar, realizar, proceder, proporcionar, ejercer. Its nominal part (is_split_predicate_noun) is a NOUN whose lemma is derived from a verb, by the rule of the verbal nouns (revisión, decisión, uso), or one of the nouns of SPLIT_PREDICATE_NOUNS - cabo, cargo, caso, comienzo, cuenta, efecto, fin, gala, hincapié, lugar, manifiesto, marcha, parte - with a verb verb of its fixed expression (llevar a cabo, tomar parte, poner de manifiesto, tener lugar), so poner en primer lugar la seguridad is none. A verb takes one nominal part at most, preferred by relation in the order compound, obj, nsubj (only with the se of the passive: se tomó la decisión), iobj, nmod, obl. A complement with a preposition is the nominal part only in a fixed expression (poner de manifiesto) or with a verb of PREPOSITIONAL_LIGHT_VERBS, proceder (se procedió a la votación); the agent of a passive never is. The pairs found are in the attribute split_predicates.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens (find_split_predicates) verb Token - Verb the noun depends on (is_split_predicate_noun) CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import find_split_predicates, is_negation
from ests.utils import get_nlp

doc = get_nlp()(
    "Se procedió a la votación y el comité tomó parte en la revisión. "
    "No vino nadie, ni Juan ni María."
)
find_split_predicates(doc)
[token.text for token in doc if is_negation(token)]

[(procedió, votación), (tomó, parte)]
['No', 'nadie']

noun_verb_ratio

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of nouns}}{\textrm{Number of verb forms}} \]

The functions work with spaCy tokens: the calc_* and find_* functions take a sequence of tokens (Doc, Span or a list), the is_*, has_* and count_* functions a single token; the words of a sequence are the tokens of is_word of anyts.utils. The functions of the dependency tree come from the core, those of the Spanish constructions are esTS's own.

docs.title: Words of a sequence
docs.text:
get_words(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The words of a sequence of tokens in their order; with join_hyphens=True a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens is one word, given by its part that holds its relation, as with the dependents of get_children (governor in He is vice-governor), or by its first part when a hyphen holds it.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Base relation
docs.text:
base_dep(token)

The relation of a token without its subtype, which Universal Dependencies separates by a colon: nsubj:pass gives nsubj, expl:pass gives expl.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Dependent words
docs.text:
get_children(token, join_hyphens=False)

The dependent words of a token, punctuation and whitespace left out; with join_hyphens=True, the dependents of the whole hyphenated word the token belongs to.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word 
subtree_len(token, join_hyphens=False)

The number of words in the subtree of a token: the token itself and all of its direct and indirect dependents; the arguments are those of get_children.

docs.title: Verb forms
docs.text:
predicate_form(token)

The verb form of a predicate by the forms (VerbForm) of its auxiliaries and copulas (aux, cop): a finite auxiliary makes the predicate finite (había llegado, estaba cantando); otherwise the first auxiliary decides (de haber matado is an infinitive, siendo elegido a gerund), and without auxiliaries the word itself. A participle auxiliary counts as finite: sido and estado follow a form of haber, which the models may attach to another word (hubieras sido albañil). An auxiliary the model leaves without a form is read by its ending when it is a verb of AUXILIARY_VERBS (habéis llegado) - an infinitive in -r and a gerund in -ndo, enclitics after them (ENCLITICS), a finite form otherwise - and skipped when it is not (the old spelling á). It is the predicate_form of the anyTS core with the Spanish reading of an auxiliary without a form. The form is 'Fin', 'Inf', 'Ger' or 'Part', an empty string for a word with no verb form.

is_participle(token)

is_gerund(token)

has_auxiliary(token)

is_participle checks whether a token is a participle (VerbForm=Part) whatever its part of speech, since the models tag a participle that modifies a noun as an adjective (la casa pintada); is_gerund whether it is a gerund (VerbForm=Ger); has_auxiliary whether it carries an auxiliary or a copula (aux, cop).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token CodeResult 
from ests.syntax_stats import is_participle, predicate_form
from ests.utils import get_nlp

doc = get_nlp()(
    "Dijo que había llegado tarde. Lo acusan de haber matado al rey siendo elegido presidente."
)
[(token.text, predicate_form(token)) for token in doc if is_participle(token)]

[('llegado', 'Fin'), ('matado', 'Inf'), ('elegido', 'Ger')]

docs.title: Predicate of a clause
docs.text:
is_predicate(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word can be the predicate of its clause: a verb (VERB, AUX) or a word with a subject of its own (nsubj, csubj and their subtypes, anyts.constants.SUBJECT_DEPS), so the nominal predicate of he is tall passes and a parenthetical word does not.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Chains of modifiers
docs.text:
calc_modifier_chains(tokens, is_modifier, join_hyphens=False)

The lengths of the chains of nested modifiers, in the order of the words. A chain is two or more modifiers each hanging on the previous one, such as the complements of the increase of the efficiency of the use of resources (length 3); the check is_modifier of a language says what a modifier is (a complement with a preposition, a noun in the genitive). A chain starts at a modifier whose head is none, and its length is the number of modifiers in its longest branch. The links are those of get_children: punctuation is no link, and with join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one link.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens is_modifier Callable[[Token], bool] - Whether a word is a modifier of the chain join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A check that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Verse statistics
docs.text:
VerseStats(source, seseo=False)

The verse statistics of a text: the scansion of the lines, the meter and the number of metrical syllables, the rhythmic stresses and the stress profile, the types of the endecasílabo, the endings of the lines, the rhyme, its scheme and the strophes. The data source is a text with its line breaks or a Doc object of the spaCy library; the statistics are computed when the object is created, and no trained model and no dictionary are needed.

The meter of Spanish verse is syllabic: a line is measured by its metrical syllables, and the stresses shape its rhythm. The text is split into lines and stanzas (by blank lines), the words are split into syllables and stressed by syllabify and word_stresses, and the syllables of a line are counted with the synalephas and the law of the final stress; a compound verse, the alejandrino above all, is read as two hemistichs (algorithm). A text with letters but without Spanish syllables (another alphabet) gives empty statistics - n_lines 0, meter None, shares nan.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc;
  • SourceError - a source without letters (empty, digits and punctuation only).
CodeResult 
from ests import VerseStats

# The beginning of the sonnet I by Garcilaso de la Vega
text = """Cuando me paro a contemplar mi estado
y a ver los pasos por do me han traído,
hallo, según por do anduve perdido,
que a mayor mal pudiera haber llegado."""

vs = VerseStats(text)
vs.print_stats()

------------------------------------------------------------
Number of lines                               |      4
Number of stanzas                             |      1
Meter                                         | endecasílabo
Number of metrical syllables                  |      11
Share of lines off the meter                  |     0.00
Share of lines without the rhythmic stresses  |     0.00
Share of rhymed lines                         |     1.00
Share of oxytone endings (aguda)              |     0.00
Share of paroxytone endings (llana)           |     1.00
Share of proparoxytone endings (esdrújula)    |     0.00

docs.title: Meter and metrical syllables
docs.text:
meter · n_feet · c_feet · p_deviations · Quilis, 1984

detect_meter(text)

The meter of a poem by the algorithm: the name of the verse by its metrical syllables - octosílabo, endecasílabo, alejandrino... (VERSE_METERS), and n_feet its number of metrical syllables. c_feet is the distribution of the lines by metrical syllables, and p_deviations the share of the lines off the meter.

The meter is the length of most lines, and it is not determined (None) if more than a tenth of the lines (VERSE_MAX_DEVIATIONS) stay off it after the fitting - a polymetric poem (a silva, a sonnet with an estrambote of heptasílabos), free verse, prose - or if the text has a single line (VERSE_MIN_LINES). The lines of a poem without a meter are fitted to its common lengths - the ones of at least two lines and a tenth of them, as the 7 and the 11 syllables of a lira or a silva - if these take more than half of the lines; otherwise, as in free verse and prose, the lines keep their plain readings.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text of a poem

The errors are those of VerseStats.

from ests.verse_stats import detect_meter

vs.c_feet, vs.p_deviations

docs.title: Rhythmic stresses
docs.text:
p_pyrrhics · stress_profile · c_rhythms · Navarro Tomás, 1972

The rhythmic stresses (VERSE_RHYTHMS) are the ones a meter asks for besides the last stress, which every line has by the law of the final stress: the endecasílabo is stressed on the 6th syllable (a maiore) or on the 4th and the 8th (sáfico) or the 7th (dactílico); a compound verse on the last stress of its first hemistich. p_pyrrhics is the share of the lines of the meter without them, and a meter with the last stress alone, the octosílabo among others, has p_pyrrhics 0.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lines of the meter without its rhythmic stresses}}{\textrm{Number of lines of the meter}} \]

stress_profile is the share of the lines of the meter stressed on each metrical syllable; the syllables are counted from zero, so the 6th syllable is the number 5. Without a meter p_pyrrhics is nan and the profile is empty. c_rhythms is the distribution of the endecasílabos by type:

Type Stresses Name 1-6-10 1st, 6th enfático 2-6-10 2nd, 6th heroico 3-6-10 3rd, 6th melódico 4-6-10, 5-6-10 the first stress on the 4th or the 5th, 6th a maiore 6-10 6th, no stress before it a maiore 4-8-10 4th, 8th, no 6th sáfico 4-7-10 4th, 7th, no 6th nor 8th dactílico, de gaita gallega

A line with the 6th syllable stressed takes its type from its first stress; 4-6-10 counts as sáfico in some treatises. A line with none of the three sets is left out of c_rhythms and counted in p_pyrrhics.

docs.title: Rhyme
docs.text:
p_rhymed · rhyme_schemes · c_rhymes

rhyme_scheme(text, seseo=False)

The rhyme scheme of a poem: the schemes of the stanzas separated by spaces. The object has the schemes by stanza in rhyme_schemes, the share of the rhymed lines in p_rhymed and the distribution of the rhymed lines by the kind of the rhyme, consonante or asonante, in c_rhymes.

A line rhymes by its ending from the last stressed vowel: in full (consonante) if the sounds are the same, by assonance (asonante) if the stressed and the last vowels are. The sounds are the ones of the ear: b and v, c and z (s with seseo), ll and y are one sound, h is silent, the tap r and the trill rr differ. The assonance leaves out the vowels between the stressed and the last one (pálido - a, o), takes the stressed vowel of a diphthong (cielo - e, o; gracia - a, a), reads a final i and u as e and o (fácil - a, e) and gives an aguda its stressed vowel alone. A line rhymes with the lines of the window of RHYME_WINDOW (4) lines before it, across the stanzas, so that the quatrains of a sonnet rhyme ABBA ABBA.

The assonance counts in two cases. A poem whose rhyme is the assonance - at least a third of its lines with no full rhyme, and at least four of them, share one (RHYME_MIN_ASSONANCE, RHYME_MIN_ASSONANT_LINES) - rhymes by the assonances of all its lines, which take in the full rhymes of the same vowels, as an assonant sonnet does. Otherwise the assonance counts on alternate lines with unrhymed lines between them: a run of at least four lines two apart with three in four of the lines between them free of a full rhyme (RHYME_MIN_FREE), or all the even lines of a stanza of an even number of lines, as the second and the fourth line of a copla. So a romance rhymes even when its assonance changes from part to part or its assonant lines also rhyme in full two by two. An assonance of neighbouring lines is no rhyme: in a sonnet of -ado and -ano the two groups stay apart.

The rhyme scheme follows the Spanish usage: the letters go in the order of the rhyme groups of the whole poem, upper-case for the lines of arte mayor (9 syllables and more, VERSE_ARTE_MAYOR) and lower-case for the lines of arte menor, a hyphen for an unrhymed line: a sonnet is ABBA ABBA CDC DCD, a redondilla abba, a lira aBabB, a romance -a-a-a-a. When the 26 letters run out, the letter of a group that no line in the window can join any more is taken again.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text of a poem seseo bool False Pronounce c and z before e and i as s in the rhyme

The errors are those of VerseStats.

docs.title: Strophes and form
docs.text:
strophes · form

A stanza is named by its lines, their lengths, its scheme and its rhyme (VERSE_STROPHES, the first that fits), None if no strophe fits:

Strophe Lines Lengths Schemes Rhyme pareado 2 any aa any terceto 3 arte mayor aba, a-a, abc, aab, abb any tercerilla 3 arte menor aba, a-a any cuaderna vía 4 14 each aaaa consonante cuarteto, serventesio 4 arte mayor abba; abab consonante redondilla, cuarteta 4 arte menor abba; abab consonante seguidilla 4 7-5-7-5 -a-a any copla 4 8 each -a-a asonante lira 5 7-11-7-7-11 ababb consonante quinteto, quintilla 5 arte mayor; arte menor ababa, abaab, abbab, aabab, aabba consonante estrofa manriqueña 6 8-8-4-8-8-4 abcabc consonante sexta rima 6 arte mayor ababcc consonante sexteto 6 arte mayor aabccb, abcabc, abbacc, aabbcc consonante sextilla 6 arte menor aabccb, ababcc, abcabc, aabaab consonante octava real 8 11 each abababcc consonante décima 10 8 each abbaaccddc consonante

A stanza of a poem with no meter is fitted to the syllables of a strophe that asks for them, so that a single lira gets its 7 and 11 syllables. The form of a poem is soneto for 14 lines of a meter of arte mayor in full rhyme with the quatrains ABBA or ABAB and the tercets on rhymes of their own; romance for octosílabos from 8 lines with three in four of the even lines of the stanzas rhymed by assonance, which may change, and three in four of the odd ones unrhymed; the strophe of all the stanzas; silva for heptasílabos and endecasílabos with no meter, longer than a strophe (more than 10 lines) and with no pattern of lengths repeated by all its stanzas; otherwise None.

CodeResult 
# The sonnet I by Garcilaso de la Vega
sonnet = """Cuando me paro a contemplar mi estado
y a ver los pasos por do me han traído,
hallo, según por do anduve perdido,
que a mayor mal pudiera haber llegado;

mas cuando del camino estó olvidado,
a tanto mal no sé por dó he venido;
sé que me acabo, y más he yo sentido
ver acabar comigo mi cuidado.

Yo acabaré, que me entregué sin arte
a quien sabrá perderme y acabarme
si quisiere, y aún sabrá querello;

que pues mi voluntad puede matarme,
la suya, que no es tanto de mi parte,
pudiendo, ¿qué hará sino hacello?"""
vs_sonnet = VerseStats(sonnet)
vs_sonnet.rhyme_schemes, vs_sonnet.strophes, vs_sonnet.form
vs_sonatina.strophes, VerseStats(romance).form

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
accentuate() returns the text with the stresses marked: an acute accent (U+0301) is put after the stressed vowel of every stressed word that has no written accent; the words with a written accent keep it, and the unstressed words of the verse (VERSE_PROCLITICS) stay unmarked, except the last word of a line. The marks are combining characters apart from the written accents, so unicodedata.normalize("NFC", ...) turns them into accented letters. Only the lines with Spanish words are returned (as in lines), the stanzas separated by a blank line. Unlike the accentuate function, the last word of a line is always stressed.

Cuando me páro a contemplár mi estádo
y a vér los pásos por do me hán traído,
hállo, según por do andúve perdído,
que a mayór mál pudiéra habér llegádo.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
A line of Spanish verse is measured by its metrical syllables, which are not the syllables of its words one by one:

  1. Syllables and stresses. Every word is split into syllables by syllabify and stressed by the orthographic rules of word_stresses; an adverb in -mente has two stresses. The unstressed words of the verse (VERSE_PROCLITICS) take no stress: the articles, the prepositions except según, the conjunctions, the relatives (que, cual, donde, como, cuanto), the clitic pronouns (me, te, se, le, nos), the possessives before a noun (mi, tu, su, nuestro, vuestro), the titles before a name (don, fray, san), tan, aun and the interjections oh, ay, ah. The last word of a line is always stressed.
  2. The plain reading. The final vowel of a word and the first one of the next make one syllable - a synalepha (cuan-do‿a-pe-nas, tie-rra‿y‿a-gua). A silent h lets it through (oh‿al-ma), while hi and hu before a vowel (hierba, hueso) and y before a vowel (ya, yo) are consonants and stop it; a consonant at the end of a word stops it too (el | al-ma).
  3. The law of the final stress. A line counts up to its last stressed syllable and one syllable more: a line that ends in an aguda gets a syllable (cuan-do‿ha-ce-la-ca-lor - 6 + 1 = 7), a line that ends in an esdrújula loses one (el pá-ja-ro - 3).
  4. The meter. The meter of a poem is the length of most plain readings; on a tie from three lines up, the tied length with a name that leaves the fewest lines off it wins. Every line is fitted to it with the fewest changes of its plain reading: a longer line joins two vowels of a hiatus in a word - a synaeresis (poe-ta), the ones with an accented i or u (dí-a) last; a shorter line breaks its synalephas from the end of the line - a hiatus, then splits a diphthong of a stressed syllable - a dieresis (su-a-ve, ru-i-do). A written diaeresis marks a hiatus (sü-a-ve) that no synaeresis joins. A line that cannot reach the meter keeps its plain reading and counts as off it. A poem without a meter fits its lines to its common lengths instead, if they take more than half of the lines.
  5. Compound verse. A compound verse of two equal hemistichs (VERSE_HEMISTICHS: 5 + 5, 6 + 6, 7 + 7, 8 + 8, 9 + 9) is tried when more than half of the plain readings split into its hemistichs and its length equals the one of most lines or is one syllable off it; the reading with fewer lines off the meter wins, the compound verse on a tie. The caesura falls after a stressed word and blocks the synalepha, and each hemistich follows the law of the final stress on its own: the alejandrino La princesa está pálida | en su silla de oro is 7 + 7.

On the 60,209 lines of the 4,259 sonnets of SpanishSonnets, the length of a line agrees with the automatic scansion of DISCO in 97.0% of the lines and with rantanplan in 97.7%, and the stress of a metrical syllable of the lines of equal length in 97.4% and 99.6%.

The rhyme is described in its card. Against the automatic rhyme of DISCO (RhymeTagger), 99.1% of the pairs of rhyming lines we find are its pairs, and we find 97.9% of its pairs.

docs.title: Accentuation
docs.text:
accentuate(text)

Marks the stresses of a text by the orthographic rules: an acute accent (U+0301) is put after the stressed vowel of every word without a written accent, both stresses of an adverb in -mente and of a hyphenated compound; the unstressed words of the verse (VERSE_PROCLITICS) stay unmarked. The text is normalized to NFC. For the lines of a poem, where the last word is always stressed, the VerseStats.accentuate method serves.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text CodeResult 
import unicodedata

from ests.verse_stats import accentuate

text = "Yo soy aquel que ayer no más decía el verso azul y la canción profana"
unicodedata.normalize("NFC", accentuate(text))

'Yó sóy aquél que ayér nó más decía el vérso azúl y la canción profána'

docs.text:
split_stanzas(text)

Splits a text into stanzas and lines: the stanzas are separated by blank lines, and the lines without a Spanish syllable (numbers, asterisks, other alphabets) and the roman numerals of the parts of a poem (II, IV.) are left out. The text is normalized to NFC.

    "y a ver los pasos por do me han traído,\n\n* * *\n\n"
    "hallo, según por do anduve perdido,"
